[Todd Spangler](https://variety.com/author/todd-spangler/)

### [Todd Spangler](https://variety.com/author/todd-spangler/)

NY Digital Editor

#### Latest

![Apple CEO Tim Cook John Ternus](https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Apple-Tim-Cook-John-Ternus.jpg?w=1000&h=667&crop=1)

[Tim Cook](https://variety.com/t/tim-cook/) is set to exit as [Apple](https://variety.com/t/apple/)‘s CEO after 15 years. [John Ternus](https://variety.com/t/john-ternus/), senior VP of hardware engineering, will become Apple’s next chief executive officer, the company announced.

Cook will become executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors and Ternus will become its next CEO effective Sept. 1, 2026. The transition, which was approved unanimously by the board of directors, follows “a thoughtful, long-term succession planning process,” the company said.

“It has been the greatest privilege of my life to be the CEO of Apple and to have been trusted to lead such an extraordinary company,” Cook said in a statement. “I love Apple with all of my being, and I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to work with a team of such ingenious, innovative, creative and deeply caring people who have been unwavering in their dedication to enriching the lives of our customers and creating the best products and services in the world.”

### Popular on Variety

### Popular on Variety

Cook, 65, first joined Apple in March 1998 and was named CEO in August 2011, shortly before the death of co-founder and previous CEO Steve Jobs. Prior to that, Cook was the tech giant’s COO and served as head of Apple’s Macintosh division.

Under Cook’s leadership, the company has launched into several new product and service categories, including with entertainment streaming service Apple TV (previously called Apple TV+) and Apple Music. Even with its move into Hollywood and strong growth in digital services, Apple’s selection of Ternus as the next chief exec reflects its belief that physical devices remain the company’s core financial engine.

Ternus, 50, joined the executive team in 2021 as SVP of hardware engineering. Over the course of his 25-year tenure so far at Apple, Ternus has overseen hardware engineering work on a variety of products across every category. The company said he was “instrumental” in the launch of multiple new product lines, including iPad and AirPods, as well as many generations of products across iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch. Ternus joined Apple’s product design team in 2001.

“I am profoundly grateful for this opportunity to carry Apple’s mission forward,” Ternus said in a statement. “Having spent almost my entire career at Apple, I have been lucky to have worked under Steve Jobs and to have had Tim Cook as my mentor. It has been a privilege to help shape the products and experiences that have changed so much of how we interact with the world and with one another.”

Regarding Ternus, Cook said that he “has the mind of an engineer, the soul of an innovator, and the heart to lead with integrity and with honor. He is a visionary whose contributions to Apple over 25 years are already too numerous to count, and he is without question the right person to lead Apple into the future. I could not be more confident in his abilities and his character, and I look forward to working closely with him on this transition and in my new role as executive chairman.”

Arthur Levinson, who has been Apple’s non-executive chairman for the past 15 years, will become its lead independent director on Sept. 1 with the CEO changeover. Ternus will join the Apple board of directors on the same date. Levinson is the founder and CEO of Calico Labs, a Google-backed company focused on researching aging and age-related diseases.

* [AAPL](/quotes/AAPL)

John Ternus, senior vice president of hardware engineering at Apple, during a company event in New York on March 4, 2026.

Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images

[Apple](/quotes/AAPL/) said on Monday that John Ternus is succeeding [Tim Cook](https://www.cnbc.com/tim-cook/) as CEO, with Cook assuming the role of executive chairman on Sept. 1.  
  
Ternus, a senior vice president of hardware engineering, will join Apple's board of directors when he becomes chief. Apple's nonexecutive chairman Arthur Levinson will become the iPhone maker's lead independent director at that time.

"Cook will continue in his role as CEO through the summer as he works closely with Ternus on a smooth transition," Apple said in a [press release](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260420318241/en/). The company said in a filing that the board made the appointment on Friday.

It's the first CEO transition for Apple since Cook, now 65, succeeded Steve Jobs at the helm in 2011, shortly before Jobs' death. Ternus will become Apple's eighth CEO.

"It has been the greatest privilege of my life to be the CEO of Apple and to have been trusted to lead such an extraordinary company," Cook said in a statement. "I love Apple with all of my being, and I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to work with a team of such ingenious, innovative, creative, and deeply caring people who have been unwavering in their dedication to enriching the lives of our customers and creating the best products and services in the world."

![Tim Cook to become Executive Chairman of Apple, John Ternus to take over as CEO](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108294212-17767173571776717355-45397626282-1080pnbcnews.jpg?v=1776717356&w=750&h=422&vtcrop=y)

watch now

VIDEO1:1401:14

Tim Cook to become Executive Chairman of Apple, John Ternus to take over as CEO

[Closing Bell: Overtime](https://www.cnbc.com/closing-bell-overtime/)

Apple also said that Johny Srouji will become chief hardware officer, taking over for Ternus in an expanded role. Srouji, who most recently served as the company's senior vice president of hardware technologies, will also lead hardware engineering.

Apple's market cap increased by more than 20-fold on Cook's watch, closing on Monday at $4 trillion. Cook took home $74.6 million in total compensation last year, including a $3 million base salary and millions more in stock awards, according to [recent regulatory filings](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000320193/d5ac8341-3708-4b1d-89f5-6a0dcec45aa0.pdf). Forbes [estimates](https://www.forbes.com/profile/tim-cook/) his net worth at close to $3 billion.

However, as Cook exits, Apple faces numerous challenges, including an increasingly complex supply chain, geopolitical tensions, the Trump administration's tariffs and a [memory crunch](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/20/memory-crisis-latest-dram-chips-micron-samsung-sk-hynix.html) tied to soaring demand for AI chips.

Ternus, 50, has been Apple's hardware boss and has worked at Apple for about half his life, joining just four years after he graduated from the University of Pennsylvania with a degree in mechanical engineering. He's been widely viewed as next in line, with recent profiles in [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/08/technology/apple-ceo-tim-cook-john-ternus.html) and [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/features/2026-apple-next-ceo/). His portfolio has included oversight of the hardware engineering teams behind the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods and Vision Pro.

Ternus came to Apple in 2001 after a four-year stint as a mechanical engineer at Virtual Research Systems. At Apple, he worked on the product design team, and in 2013 he became a vice president of hardware engineering.

## Revamping the supply chain

During his almost 15-year tenure, Cook oversaw Apple's jump into wearable technology, with the rollout of the Apple Watch, AirPods and the virtual reality headset Vision Pro, which has [struggled](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/02/21/apples-vision-pro-has-a-problem-a-year-into-existence-too-few-apps.html) to find market adoption since its release in 2024.

Revenue almost quadrupled under Cook, climbing to over $400 billion in the latest fiscal year. Cook is best known in Silicon Valley as an operations guru, revamping Apple's supply chain after joining in 1998 as an executive vice president of worldwide sales and operations. When he arrived, Apple was near bankruptcy.

Cook became one of Jobs' loyal lieutenants and was elevated to the role of operations chief in 2005. Before joining Apple, Cook cut his teeth in the tech industry spending 12 years working at [IBM](/quotes/IBM/), helping the company manufacture computers. He also spent time at former PC maker Compaq as a vice president of corporate materials. Cook graduated from Auburn University in 1982 and received an MBA from Duke University in 1988.

Apple CEO Tim Cook and Jalen Brunson, basketball player for the New York Knicks, during the first day of in-store sales of Apple's latest products at Apple's Fifth Avenue store in New York, Sept. 19, 2025.

Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images

For Ternus, perhaps the most critical aspect of his new job will be pushing the company deeper into artificial intelligence, where it's lagged many of its megacap peers.

While the iPhone 17 has done well, Apple has faced criticism from investors and technologists for a perceived lack of cutting-edge AI technology. That criticism grew after Apple last year delayed an upgrade to its Siri voice assistant. In December, Apple revamped its AI leadership, replacing its former chief with a Google veteran.  
  
The company has said it will launch an updated version of Siri this year based on a [Google](/quotes/GOOGL/) Gemini AI model.

Since product designer Jony Ive left Apple in 2019, the company has been operating without one of its cornerstone executives [credited](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/05/21/openai-jony-ive-apple-siri.html) with making its flagship iPhone aesthetically appealing to the masses.  
Ive has since [joined](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/05/21/openai-buys-iphone-designer-jony-ive-device-startup-for-6point4-billion.html) OpenAI, which in May 2025 said it would acquire the design guru's startup in an all-equity deal worth about $6.4 billion.

In recent years, Cook acted as a public statesman to advance Apple's interests, meeting with both foreign and domestic leaders. Initially, he pushed for increased internet privacy protections around the world. In 2016, he notably clashed with the U.S. government over whether Apple would have to help unlock an encrypted iPhone used by a criminal gunman in San Bernardino, California. Cook said to do so would threaten users' privacy, and the FBI eventually found a different way to unlock the device.

Of late, much of Cook's public lobbying has focused on [President Donald Trump](https://www.cnbc.com/donald-trump/), who has threatened and repealed several tariffs on imports from China and other Asian countries where Apple does big business.

In August, Cook visited the White House, appearing with Trump, to tout an announcement that Apple would spend $600 billion in the U.S. over the next five years.

At the August meeting, Trump, who once referred to Cook as "Tim Apple," read a list of the company's commitments next to Cook and said, "I love that you're doing this."

Dan Ives, an analyst at Wedbush Securities, told CNBC's "Fast Money" that the timing of Cook's exit is surprising.  
  
"The view is he was going to stay on maybe for another year," Ives said. "You know, he's even sort of made comments about it in terms of staying."

Cook used a "Good Morning America" appearance last month to [shut down](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/17/apple-ceo-tim-cook-retire-rumors-gma.html) growing speculation about his future at the company, telling viewers that retirement talk is nothing more than a rumor.

Asked about reports that he was preparing to step aside, Cook told ABC, "No, I didn't say that. I haven't said that. I love what I do deeply. Twenty-eight years ago, I walked into Apple, and I've loved every day of it since."

*— CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed to this report.*

Bloomberg Podcasts published a breaking news episode (April 21, 2026) covering Apple's announcement that John Ternus will become the company's next CEO, with Tim Cook transitioning to executive chairman. Ternus, 50, currently senior VP of hardware engineering, will become CEO effective September 1, 2026, and will also join Apple's board of directors. Tim Cook will remain CEO through the summer to oversee a smooth transition, then serve as executive chairman, assisting with global policy maker engagement.

Key details from the announcement and analysis:
- The succession was approved unanimously by Apple's board following a long-term succession planning process.
- Ternus' hardware engineering division will be taken over by longtime deputy Tom Marieb, reporting to newly named Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji, who gains oversight of a combined hardware engineering and hardware technologies group.
- Ternus has spent 25 years at Apple, headed hardware engineering since 2021, and worked on product design for the iPad, Mac development, and computer monitors. He has been taking a more public role recently, including revealing the MacBook Neo at an Apple event in March and appearing on Good Morning America.
- Analysis (from Bloomberg's Tom Giles and Mandeep Singh) noted the announcement was orderly and unsurprising given Ternus was the known heir apparent, though the timing came sooner than expected.
- Apple's stock has been up more than 2,200% since Tim Cook took over in January 2011 (vs. S&P 500 up 465%), with annualized returns of 24.4% vs. 14% for the S&P 500. The stock dipped only about 0.4% in after-hours trading following the announcement.
- Analysts discussed challenges facing Ternus, including Apple's lag in AI/LLM strategy, the need to develop on-device LLM form factors, potential for more aggressive acquisitions (given Apple hasn't invested heavily in its own AI efforts), and supply chain diversification (China, India). Some speculated Ternus may be more acquisitive than Cook was.
- Tim Cook was praised for his capital allocation (Warren Buffett/Berkshire Hathaway became a shareholder) and diplomatic skill navigating relationships with the White House, China, and India.

This is a MacRumors Facebook post dated April 22 (2026) announcing a major overhaul of Apple's executive leadership effective September 1, 2026. Tim Cook will step down as CEO and transition to a new executive chairman role, while John Ternus will become Apple's new CEO. Johny Srouji, who currently leads Apple's chip division, will be promoted to chief hardware officer. The post links to MacRumors' article titled "Apple CEO Tim Cook Stepping Down, John Ternus Taking Over" (macrumors.com/2026/04/20/tim-cook-stepping-down/). The post received 838 reactions, 84 comments, and 53 shares.

The comment section reveals a range of public reactions: some users express optimism about a hardware-focused leader, with one commenter noting Tim Cook's supply chain and marketing background influenced modern product designs, while another hopes John Ternus will be "another Steve." Other commenters express disappointment over perceived lack of innovation under Cook's leadership, with one stating Apple is "3-5 years behind" and another threatening to switch to Android. One user hoped Craig Federighi might have gotten the job due to his "showman flair." Some lighter comments include requests for a macOS-native Health app, a joke about Johny Srouji getting an office with a window, and a suggestion that Tim Cook should do a final September event.

**John Furner** is an American business executive who is the president and [chief executive officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") (CEO) of [Walmart Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walmart "Walmart") He was president and CEO of [Walmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walmart "Walmart") U.S. from 2019 to 2026, and CEO of [Sam's Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam's_Club "Sam's Club") from 2017 to 2019. Furner succeeded [Doug McMillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_McMillon "Doug McMillon"), who retired in January 2026.[[2]](#cite_note-:2-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-:3-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=John_Furner&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Furner was born in 1974 in [Jacksonville, Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville,_Arkansas "Jacksonville, Arkansas").[[5]](#cite_note-Monk18-5) He attended [Sam M. Walton College of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_M._Walton_College_of_Business "Sam M. Walton College of Business")[[6]](#cite_note-Speer18-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) at the [University of Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arkansas "University of Arkansas"), and earned [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") in Business Administration in Marketing Management.[[1]](#cite_note-Furner-1)[[5]](#cite_note-Monk18-5)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=John_Furner&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Furner began his career at Walmart in 1993 as an hourly store associate.[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-:0-9)[[10]](#cite_note-:1-10)[[4]](#cite_note-:3-4) He later became a store manager, district manager, and buyer.[[9]](#cite_note-:0-9)[[11]](#cite_note-11) He became CEO of [Sam's Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam's_Club "Sam's Club")[[10]](#cite_note-:1-10) on February 1, 2017, after working as Sam's Club's chief merchandising officer and, prior that, spending nearly three years in Walmart's international division as EVP of merchandising and marketing for Walmart China.[[12]](#cite_note-Troy18-12)[[13]](#cite_note-Redman19-13)

At Sam's Club, Furner closed 63 stores to better compete with [Costco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costco "Costco"). *The [Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")* reported that sales increased during his time as CEO.[[14]](#cite_note-Nassauer19-14) Based on his experience at Walmart China, Furner focused on increasing the use of technology in Sam's Club warehouses and narrowing its targeted customer.[[12]](#cite_note-Troy18-12)[[15]](#cite_note-Troy17-15) Furner also focused on increasing Sam's Club's private brand business.[[16]](#cite_note-Unglesbee19-16)

Furner became president and CEO of Walmart U.S. in November 2019.[[13]](#cite_note-Redman19-13) He replaced [Doug McMillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_McMillon "Doug McMillon") as CEO of Walmart Inc. in February 2026.[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18)[[2]](#cite_note-:2-2)

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=John_Furner&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Furner is married with four children.[[6]](#cite_note-Speer18-6) He is board chairman of the [National Retail Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Retail_Federation "National Retail Federation") and was a board member of Medal of Honor Foundation in 2020.[[19]](#cite_note-NRF-19)[[20]](#cite_note-MOHF-20)

# John Furner to succeed Doug McMillon as Walmart CEO

![Walmart.](https://www.bakingbusiness.com/ext/resources/2025/11/14/Walmart-Lead.webp?height=667&t=1763139153&width=1080)

*Plans call for John Furner, left, president and CEO of Walmart US, to take over from Doug McMillon, right, as Walmart president and CEO on Feb. 1, 2026.*

 | Source: Walmart

11.14.2025

By [Russell Redman](/authors/284-russell-redman)

[![Google](/images/google_logo.svg)Add as a preferred  
source on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=bakingbusiness.com&location=article_header)

BENTONVILLE, ARK. — When Walmart Inc. wraps up its 2026 fiscal year at the end of January, the world’s largest retailer also will be ushering in a new leader, as John Furner has been named to succeed Doug McMillon as president and chief executive officer.

Plans call for McMillon, 59, to retire on Jan. 31 and for Furner, 51, to take the CEO reins on Feb. 1. In announcing the move on Nov. 14, Walmart said Furner — currently president and CEO of Walmart US, the company’s largest business unit — has joined the board of directors, effective immediately. McMillon is slated to remain on the board until the next annual shareholder meeting in June and stay on as an adviser through fiscal 2027 to aid in the leadership transition.

Walmart said it expects to announce Furner’s successor as Walmart US CEO before the end of the current fiscal year, which ends Jan. 31, 2026.

“John Furner is the right leader to guide Walmart into our next chapter of growth and transformation,” said Greg Penner, chairman of Walmart. “After starting as an hourly associate and being with us for over 30 years in a variety of leadership roles across all three of our operating segments, John understands every dimension of our business, from the sales floor to global strategy. He has proven that he can deliver results while living our values. John’s six-year leadership of our Walmart US business during a time of rapid change, marked by digital acceleration and strong associate engagement, has positioned us for continued success.”

McMillon has been Walmart’s president and CEO since February 2014, after spending five years in the same role at Walmart International. Before that, he was president and CEO of Sam’s Club, Walmart’s warehouse club chain. He has been with Walmart since 1984, when he took a summer job unloading trailers while still in high school.

“Serving as Walmart’s CEO has been a great honor, and I’m thankful to our board and the Walton family for the opportunity,” McMillon said. “I’m incredibly proud of what our associates accomplished and deeply grateful for their commitment to our customers, to each other and to the communities we serve.”

Furner has been president and CEO of Walmart US since November 2019, overseeing more than 4,600 stores and a business with fiscal 2025 net sales of over $462 million. He started his Walmart career as an hourly associate in 1993 and has held leadership roles across merchandising, operations and sourcing. Walmart noted that Furner has lived and worked in multiple countries — including two years as chief merchandising and marketing officer of Walmart China — and was president and CEO of Sam’s Club US for nearly three years.

Citing his collaborative leadership style, Walmart said Furner has fostered associate development, digital innovation and operational excellence during his time at the company.

“I’ve worked with John for more than 20 years,” McMillon said. “His love for our associates and this company runs deep. His curiosity and digital acumen, combined with a deep commitment to our people and culture, will enable him to take us to the next level. He’s uniquely capable of leading the company through this next AI-driven transformation. He’s a merchant, an operator, an innovator and a builder. I know that our future is bright with his leadership.”

McMillon has led Walmart through perhaps its biggest challenge — transitioning a brick-and-mortar retail company into a digitally driven, omnichannel retailer — while also modernizing its huge supply chain by bringing automation to its distribution and fulfillment centers. Also under McMillon’s leadership, Walmart has begun making the companywide adoption of artificial intelligence a cornerstone of its business strategy. Walmart totaled nearly $675 billion in net sales for fiscal 2025, up from $473 billion in fiscal 2014, as McMillon started his tenure as CEO.

“On behalf of the board, I want to thank Doug McMillon for his extraordinary leadership and incredible impact he has had on our company,” Penner said. “Our family and board have stated many times that Doug was uniquely qualified to be CEO at the necessary time for Walmart. Over more than a decade as CEO, Doug led a comprehensive transformation by investing in our associates, advancing our digital and e-commerce capabilities and modernizing our supply chain, resulting in sustained, robust financial performance. He leaves Walmart stronger, more innovative and better aligned with our purpose to help people save money and live better.”

# **Leadership**

![Portrait of John Furner]()

[Download Photo](/content/dam/corporate/images/about/leadership/high-res/John-Furner.jpg)

## **John Furner**

### **President and CEO, Walmart Inc.**

[Print](javascript:window.print();) 

Follow

[![Instagram icon](/content/dam/corporate/site-images/icons/Instagram_glyph_black.png)](https://www.instagram.com/furner/ "Visit John Furner on Instagram")

[![LinkedIn icon](/content/dam/corporate/site-images/icons/LinkedIn-glyph-black.png)](https://www.linkedin.com/in/furner/ "Visit John Furner on LinkedIn")

John Furner is president and chief executive officer of Walmart Inc., leading 2.1 million associates around the world. He is a merchant, an operator and an innovator who is deeply grounded in the company’s purpose and values. Under his leadership, Walmart is building a new era of retail fueled by innovation and artificial intelligence.

Prior to his current role, John served as president and chief executive officer of Walmart U.S., where he led more than 1.5 million associates and was responsible for the strategic direction and performance of Walmart’s omni retail business, including its digital business, 4,600+ physical stores, advertising, health and wellness business and supply chain. As CEO of Walmart U.S., John and the team delivered strong performance — driving growth and innovation, improving associate engagement and integrating technology in ways that improved the experience of shopping with Walmart and being an associate.

Previously, John served as president and chief executive officer of Sam’s Club U.S. Under his leadership, Sam’s Club U.S. had 11 consecutive quarters of positive sales comps and achieved strong membership growth, driven by an enhanced member experience and improved merchandise assortment.

John started with Walmart as an hourly associate in 1993, at Store 100 in Bentonville, Arkansas. Over the past three decades, he has held important roles throughout the company, including assistant store manager, store manager, district manager, buyer, regional general manager, divisional merchandising manager, VP of global sourcing, general merchandise manager, head of marketing and merchandising for Walmart China based in Shenzhen, and chief merchant for Sam’s Club U.S.

In addition to his responsibilities at Walmart, he serves on the board of directors for the National Retail Federation and was chairman from 2022 to 2025.

John holds a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Marketing Management from the University of Arkansas.

# Walmart elects board, welcomes new CEO at annual business meeting

[Business](https://talkbusiness.net/category/business/)[Latest News](https://talkbusiness.net/category/latest-news/)[Northwest Arkansas](https://talkbusiness.net/category/regions/northwest-arkansas-region/)[Retail](https://talkbusiness.net/category/business/retail/)

by [**Kim Souza**](https://talkbusiness.net/author/ksouza42/) ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#f09b839f858a91b084919c9b928583999e958383de9e9584))  June 4, 2026 11:00 am 1,801 views

 ![](https://talkbusiness.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/wmt-shareholders2026-732x385.jpg)  

Walmart Board Chairman Greg Penner called the retailer’s annual business shareholder meeting to order Thursday (June 4) morning, welcoming John Furner as the company’s new CEO and thanking former CEO Doug McMillon for his leadership.

Furner stepped into the top job on Feb. 1. McMillon, 59, will for the next fiscal year work in a consulting role with Furner, who was previously the Walmart U.S. CEO.

“Doug lived with purpose and conviction, and he guided Walmart through periods of significant change, while staying grounded in our values and culture,” Penner said.

Penner, who is married to Carrie, the daughter of Rob Walton and granddaughter of Sam Walton, said he is pleased with the seamless transition of Furner and his management group.

“Their experience, integrity, and long-term orientation to fly us forward, and they are ready to lead in the era of retail that’s defined by AI and innovation,” he said.

Walmart shareholders have plenty to celebrate. Fiscal year 2026 revenue was $713.16 billion, up 4.7% year over year. Consolidated net income grew to $22.27 billion, up from $20.15 billion in fiscal 2025. Operating income totaled $29.82 billion, up from $29.34 million the prior year.

Furner said it’s been exciting to see how Walmart has evolved from a regional retailer to a global omnichannel business that employs 2.1 million workers worldwide.

“Our associates, powered by AI, are delivering faster and more accurately around the world,” he said. “We serve customers and members 280 million times per week at the counter and curbside pickup for delivering to their homes. Walmart is a special company. The business has changed a lot since Sam Walton started his first Walmart, and it’s changed a lot since I started in the garden center, but what hasn’t changed is our people who make the difference.”

**BOARD ELECTION**  
 Shareholders also elected its slate of directors, who have a median age of 58, and 8 years of board tenure. Also, 8 of the 11 directors are deemed independent with no family connection to the Waltons, and 10 of the 11 are non-management. The following directors will serve a one-year term.

Cesar Conde, 52, chairman of NBCUniversal News Group  
 Sarah Friar. 53, chief financial officer at OpenAI  
 John Furner, 51, CEO of Walmart  
 Carla Harris, 63, senior client manager at Morgan Stanley  
 Tom Horton, 64, former CEO of American Airlines  
 Marissa Mayer, 50, founder of Dazzle AI  
 Shishir Mehrotra, 47, CEO of Superhuman Labs  
 Bob Moritz, 62, retired global chairman of PwC  
 Randall Stephenson, 66, retired CEO of AT&T  
 Steuart Walton, 44, chairman and cofounder of Game Aerospace

**OUTSIDE PROPOSALS REJECTED**  
 There were four proposals brought by shareholders, all of which were opposed by the company, and none of which garnered enough votes to pass. In proposal No. 5, shareholders asked the company to adopt cumulative voting in the elections of directors. That would mean that in any election of directors, each shareholder would be entitled to the votes equal to the number of shares owned multiplied by the number of directors to be elected, and that shareholders may allocate such votes among one or more nominees at their discretion, as permitted by applicable law.

In proposal No. 6, shareholders asked for a report on workplace health and safety governance. Proposal No. 7 asked the company to report on its immigration policy and enforcement. Proposition No. 8 requested a report of how the workplace is being impacted by AI and automation.

## Who is the CEO of Microsoft?

As an Indian-American business executive, Satya Narayana Nadella has made significant strides in the tech industry. Born in Hyderabad, India, he pursued a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the Manipal Institute of Technology before moving to the United States.

Over the years, he has held various leadership roles within Microsoft, including executive vice president of the cloud and enterprise group. As CEO, Nadella has been instrumental in steering the company towards cloud computing and overseeing major acquisitions such as LinkedIn.

His leadership has had a positive impact on Microsoft's growth and market share, solidifying his reputation as an innovative and influential leader in the tech world.

### Work History

* **Microsoft**: Chairman and CEO (February 2014 - present)
* **University of Chicago:** Member Board of Trustees (January 2018 - present)
* **Starbucks:** Board Member (January 2017 - present)
* **The Business Council U.S.**: Chairman (January 2021 - January 2023)
* **Fred Hutch:** Board Member (January 2016 - January 2022)

### Education History

Satya Nadella's educational background is a testament to his dedication to technology and business. He began his academic journey at the Manipal Institute of Technology in India, where he earned a Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering. Nadella then moved to the United States to further his education, obtaining a Master's Degree in Computer Science from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee.

Recognizing the importance of business acumen in the tech industry, he also pursued an MBA from the prestigious University of Chicago Booth School of Business, completing the program between 1994 and 1996. This combination of technical expertise and business education has undoubtedly contributed to Nadella's successful career and leadership at Microsoft.

## When did Satya Nadella join Microsoft?

Joining Microsoft in 1992, Satya Nadella has held various leadership roles within the company before becoming the CEO in February 2014. With nearly three decades of experience at Microsoft, Nadella has played a crucial role in the company's transformation, particularly in the areas of cloud computing and enterprise services.

# Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella named chairman of the board

![thumbnail](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/105119178-Jordan_Novet_IMG_4402a.jpg?v=1523299470&w=60&h=60&ffmt=webp)

[Jordan Novet](https://www.cnbc.com/jordan-novet/)[@in/jordannovet/](https://linkedin.com/in/jordannovet/)

[WATCH LIVE](/live-tv/)

Key Points

* Satya Nadella, Microsoft's CEO, is becoming the software company's chair, after running the company for seven years, when he replaced Steve Ballmer.
* Nadella is taking over the chairperson seat from former Symantec CEO John Thompson.

In this article

* [MSFT](/quotes/MSFT)

Satya Nadella speaking at the 2016 World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.

David A. Grogan | CNBC

[Microsoft](/quotes/MSFT/) said Wednesday that CEO Satya Nadella is becoming the chair of the company's board, replacing independent director John Thompson, following a unanimous vote of the software company's board.

The change reflects the success Nadella has had in the past seven years making Microsoft more prominent in technology and business altogether.

"In this role, Nadella will lead the work to set the agenda for the board, leveraging his deep understanding of the business to elevate the right strategic opportunities and identify key risks and mitigation approaches for the board's review," Microsoft said in a [statement](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/microsoft-board-of-directors-announces-role-changes-and-quarterly-dividend-301314220.html).

Under Nadella's watch Microsoft regained the title of world's most valuable public company. Today it stands as the second most valuable, only behind [Apple](/quotes/AAPL/), with Microsoft stock having risen more than 600%.

Nadella's Microsoft has become more focused on cloud computing services to power other company's applications, and the company has expanded through acquisitions of business social network LinkedIn, source code-sharing site GitHub and video-game developer Zenimax.

Microsoft's board members gave plaudits to Nadella for his leadership during the coronavirus pandemic in [the proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312520272025/d31295ddef14a.htm) the company filed in December, with the company delivering 14% revenue growth in the 2020 fiscal year, even as the company faced challenges in advertising and other markets. "The board credits Mr. Nadella for his tremendous progress driving cultural change across the organization, especially given the unprecedented impact of Covid-19 on our business and our people," Microsoft said.

Nadella is one of Microsoft's top individual shareholders, with more than 1.6 million shares of the company's stock.

The move came a year after Bill Gates, a co-founder of Microsoft and its first CEO, left the company's board. Gates stepped down after the board investigated a report that Gates had tried to start an intimate relationship with an employee in 2000, [a company spokesperson said](https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/21/microsoft-ceo-nadella-says-power-in-the-workplace-is-not-to-be-abused.html).

Thompson, formerly CEO of Symantec, joined Microsoft's board in 2012 and replaced Gates as Microsoft's chair in 2014, on the same day Nadella replaced Steve Ballmer as the Microsoft CEO.

June 16 (Reuters) - Microsoft Corp [(MSFT.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/companies/MSFT.O/) on Wednesday named Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella as its new chairman, in place of John Thompson.

Nadella, who took over as CEO in 2014 from Steve Ballmer, has been instrumental in scaling up its business including billion-dollar acquisitions like LinkedIn, Nuance Communications and ZeniMax.

The company said Thompson, who took over as chairman from the software giant's co-founder Bill Gates in 2014, will serve as lead independent director.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

The top-level executive change comes just over a year after Gates stepped down from the board, saying he would focus on philanthropic works of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, one of the world's biggest charities.

The company had last month said it conducted a probe into Gates' involvement with an employee almost 20 years ago after it was told in 2019 that he had tried to start a romantic relationship with the person.

Microsoft had declined to comment on whether its board had decided Gates should go.

The company also declared a quarterly dividend of 56 cents per share payable Sept. 9.

# Microsoft names CEO Satya Nadella chairman of the board

**by [Kurt Schlosser](https://www.geekwire.com/author/kurt/ "Posts by Kurt Schlosser")** on Jun 16, 2021 at 4:10 pmJune 17, 2021 at 7:46 am

![](https://cdn.geekwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/20190506_Microsoft_Build_55-630x420.jpg)

Microsoft announced Wednesday that CEO Satya Nadella will take on the dual role of chairman of the company’s board, replacing independent director John Thompson.

“In this role, Nadella will lead the work to set the agenda for the board, leveraging his deep understanding of the business to elevate the right strategic opportunities and identify key risks and mitigation approaches for the board’s review,” Microsoft said in a [news release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/microsoft-board-of-directors-announces-role-changes-and-quarterly-dividend-301314220.html).

The elevation was a unanimous election by the board’s independent directors. Thompson will become lead independent director, a role he held previously from 2012 to 2014. He will “retain significant authority including providing input on behalf of the independent directors on board agendas, calling meetings of the independent directors, setting agendas for executive sessions, and leading performance evaluations of the CEO,” Microsoft said.

Nadella, 53, first joined Microsoft in 1992 and was [named CEO](https://www.geekwire.com/2014/microsoft-ceo-main/) in February 2014, at the same time that Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates stepped down as chairman of the board.

Gates left the board last March, 45 years after co-founding the software giant with childhood friend Paul Allen. Fallout from Gates’ recent divorce announcement [revealed that he left the board](https://www.geekwire.com/2021/gates-divorce-drama-bill-gates-alleged-affair-prompt-board-resignations/) after allegations surfaced that he had an inappropriate relationship with an employee.

Under Nadella, Microsoft has regained its stature as a tech powerhouse, making headlines for acquisitions of companies such as LinkedIn and GitHub, putting focus on the company’s cloud computing business, making accessibility and equity a leading platform of the company’s culture, and avoiding the antitrust scrutiny that has plagued rivals Amazon, Apple, Google and Facebook.

Microsoft is the second most valuable company in the world behind Apple.

“Success is important, but you have to remember that your success has to have come from some sense of purpose,” Nadella said [in an interview](https://www.geekwire.com/2019/interview-satya-nadella-microsofts-new-world-view-dual-screen-devices-pentagon-cloud-deal/) with GeekWire in 2019.

**Satya Narayana Nadella**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-2) (born 19 August 1967) is an [Indian-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Americans "Indian Americans") business executive. He is the chairman and [chief executive officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") (CEO) of [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), succeeding [Steve Ballmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ballmer "Steve Ballmer") in 2014 as CEO and [John W. Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_W._Thompson "John W. Thompson") in 2021 as chairman.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-6)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-autogenerated22-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-autogenerated12-8)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-10) Before becoming CEO, he was the executive vice president of Microsoft's cloud and enterprise group, responsible for building and running the company's computing platforms.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-11)

## Early life

Satya Narayana Nadella was born on 19 August 1967 in a [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_people "Telugu people")[Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindus "Hindus") family in [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad "Hyderabad").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-dnaindia-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-15) His father, Bukkapuram Nadella Yugandhar, was an [Indian Administrative Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Administrative_Service "Indian Administrative Service") officer of the 1962 batch.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-17)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-dnaindia-14) His mother Prabhavati was a [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") lecturer.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-18) Yugandhar hailed from Bukkapuram in [Anantapur district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anantapur_district "Anantapur district") of [Andhra Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh "Andhra Pradesh");[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-:0-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-20) his own father had migrated to Bukkapuram from Nadella village in [Guntur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guntur "Guntur") district (present-day [Palnadu district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palnadu_district "Palnadu district")) of Andhra Pradesh.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-22)

Nadella attended the [Hyderabad Public School, Begumpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hyderabad_Public_School,_Begumpet "The Hyderabad Public School, Begumpet")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-23) before receiving a [bachelor's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor's_degree "Bachelor's degree") in [electrical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_engineering "Electrical engineering") from the [Manipal Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manipal_Institute_of_Technology "Manipal Institute of Technology") in [Karnataka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karnataka "Karnataka") in 1988.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-24)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-25) He then traveled to the United States to study for an [MS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science") at the [University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wisconsin%E2%80%93Milwaukee "University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-26) receiving his degree in 1990.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-27) He received an [MBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration") from the [University of Chicago Booth School of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Booth_School_of_Business "University of Chicago Booth School of Business") in 1997.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-Time-29)

## Career

### Sun Microsystems

Nadella worked at [Sun Microsystems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Microsystems "Sun Microsystems") as a member of its technology staff before joining Microsoft in 1992.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-30)

### Microsoft

#### 1992–2014

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Satya_Nadella%2C_CEO_of_Microsoft%2C_with_former_CEOs_Bill_Gates%2C_and_Steve_Ballmer.jpg/250px-Satya_Nadella%2C_CEO_of_Microsoft%2C_with_former_CEOs_Bill_Gates%2C_and_Steve_Ballmer.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Satya_Nadella,_CEO_of_Microsoft,_with_former_CEOs_Bill_Gates,_and_Steve_Ballmer.jpg)

Nadella on his first day as CEO of Microsoft, with former CEOs [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") (left) and [Steve Ballmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ballmer "Steve Ballmer") (right)

At Microsoft, Nadella has led major projects that included the company's move to [cloud computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") and the development of one of the largest cloud infrastructures in the world.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-31)

Nadella worked as the senior vice-president of research and development (R&D) for the Online Services Division and vice-president of the Microsoft Business Division.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-32) Later, he was made the president of Microsoft's $19 billion Server and Tools Business and led a transformation of the company's business and technology culture from [client services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Client_(computing) "Client (computing)") to [cloud infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") and [services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_services "Cloud services"). He has been credited for helping bring [Microsoft's database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_SQL_Server "Microsoft SQL Server"), [Windows Server](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Server "Windows Server") and [developer tools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Studio "Visual Studio") to its [Azure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Azure "Microsoft Azure") cloud.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-Time-29) The revenue from Cloud Services grew to $20.3 billion in June 2013 from $16.6 billion when he took over in 2011.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-33) He received $84.5 million in 2016 pay.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-35)

In 2013, Nadella's base salary was reportedly $669,167. Including stock bonuses, the total compensation stood at around $7.6 million.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-36)

Previous positions held by Nadella include:[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-37)

*   President of the Server & Tools Division (9 February 2011 – February 2014)
*   Senior Vice-president of Research and Development for the Online Services Division (March 2007 – February 2011)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-38)
*   Vice-president of the Business Division
*   Corporate Vice-president of Business Solutions and Search & Advertising Platform Group
*   Executive Vice-president of Cloud and Enterprise group[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-Official_Bio-39)

#### Chief executive officer (2014–present)

On 4 February 2014, Nadella was announced as the new CEO of Microsoft,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-autogenerated2-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-41) the third CEO in the company's history, following [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") and [Steve Ballmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ballmer "Steve Ballmer").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-42)

In October 2014, Nadella attended an event on Women in Computing and courted controversy after he made a statement that women should not ask for a raise and should trust the system.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-43) Nadella was criticised for the statement and he later apologized on Twitter.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-44) He then sent an email to Microsoft employees admitting he was "Completely wrong."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-45)

[![Image 8](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Microsoft_Linux.jpg/250px-Microsoft_Linux.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Microsoft_Linux.jpg)

Nadella leads a live discussion on Microsoft's cloud strategy in 2014 in San Francisco.

Nadella's tenure at Microsoft has emphasized working with companies and technologies with which Microsoft also competes, including [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc."),[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-46)[Salesforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesforce "Salesforce"),[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-Wired-47)[IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM"),[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-48) and [Dropbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dropbox "Dropbox").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-49) In contrast to previous Microsoft campaigns against the [Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux "Linux") operating system, Nadella proclaimed that "Microsoft ❤️ Linux",[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-50) and Microsoft joined the [Linux Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux_Foundation "Linux Foundation") as a Platinum member in 2016.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-51)

Under Nadella, Microsoft revised its mission statement to "empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-52) He orchestrated a cultural shift at Microsoft by emphasizing empathy, collaboration, and 'growth mindset'.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-53)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-54) He has transformed Microsoft's [corporate culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organizational_culture "Organizational culture") into one that emphasizes continual learning and growth.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-55)

In 2014, Nadella's first acquisition with Microsoft was of [Mojang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojang_Studios "Mojang Studios"), a Swedish game company best known for the computer game _[Minecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minecraft "Minecraft")_, for $2.5 billion. He followed that by purchasing [Xamarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xamarin "Xamarin") for an undisclosed amount.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-56) He oversaw the purchase of professional network [LinkedIn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LinkedIn "LinkedIn")[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-57) in 2016 for $26.2 billion.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-58) On 26 October 2018, [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") acquired [GitHub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub "GitHub") for US$7.5 billion.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-59)

As of November 2023, Microsoft stock had increased nearly tenfold since Nadella became CEO in 2014, with a 27% annual growth rate, ending a 14-year period of near zero growth.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-60)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-61)

In 2024, Nadella's compensation from Microsoft totaled $79.1 million, an increase of 63% over his 2023 compensation of $48.5 million.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-62)

In January 2026, Nadella demanded that people stop calling [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence")["slop"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_slop "AI slop") and instead accept AI as the "new equilibrium" of human nature.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-microslop-63) The public reaction instead made people double down on the backlash, and the term "Microslop" became popular on social media, leading to it being labeled as a [Streisand effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streisand_effect "Streisand effect").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-microslop2-64)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-microslop3-65)

#### Sports

Nadella, Soma Somasegar, Samir Bodas, Ashok Krishnamurthi, [Sanjay Parthasarathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Parthasarathy "Sanjay Parthasarathy"), and the [GMR Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GMR_Group "GMR Group") purchased the [Seattle Orcas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Orcas "Seattle Orcas") cricket team which is a part of [2023 Major League Cricket season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Major_League_Cricket_season "2023 Major League Cricket season").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-66)

## Awards and recognition

In 2018 and 2024, Nadella was a [_Time_ 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") honoree.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-71)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-72)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-73) In 2019, he was named _[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial\_Times "Financial Times")_ Person of the Year and _[Fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune\_(magazine) "Fortune (magazine)")_ _Magazine_ Businessperson of the Year.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-75) In 2014, Nadella was awarded the [CNN-News18 Indian of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN-News18_Indian_of_the_Year "CNN-News18 Indian of the Year") and in 2020, was recognized as Global Indian Business Icon at [CNBC-TV18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNBC_TV18 "CNBC TV18")'s India Business Leader Awards.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-76) In 2015, the [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") awarded Nadella the [Pravasi Bharatiya Samman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pravasi_Bharatiya_Samman "Pravasi Bharatiya Samman") (awarded to [Overseas Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Indians "Overseas Indians")) and in 2022 the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan"), the third highest civilian award in India.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-77)

Nadella was awarded an honorary [PhD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy "Doctor of Philosophy") from the [Georgia Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Tech "Georgia Tech") in January 2024.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-78)

## Personal life

In 1992, Nadella married Anupama Priyadarshini, the daughter of his father's [Indian Administrative Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Administrative_Service "Indian Administrative Service") (IAS) [batchmate](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/en:batchmate "wikt:en:batchmate").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-79)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-80) Both Nadella and Anupama are the only children from their parents.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-81) She was his junior at [Manipal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manipal_Academy_of_Higher_Education "Manipal Academy of Higher Education") pursuing a [B.Arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Architecture "Bachelor of Architecture") in the Faculty of Architecture.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-82) The couple have three children, a son (deceased) and two daughters, and live in [Clyde Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Hill,_Washington "Clyde Hill, Washington")[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-83) and [Bellevue, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellevue,_Washington "Bellevue, Washington").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-POLITICO_04FEB14-84) His son Zain was a legally blind [quadriplegic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetraplegia "Tetraplegia") with [cerebral palsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_palsy "Cerebral palsy").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-85) Zain died in February 2022, at the age of 26.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-86) According to Nadella, being the father of a child with special needs was a turning point in his life.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-87)

Nadella is an avid reader of [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_poetry "American poetry") and [Indian poetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_poetry "Indian poetry") and enjoys [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket"), having played on his school team.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-88) He credits cricket for improving his leadership skills.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-89)

Nadella and his wife Anupama are part of the ownership group of [Seattle Sounders FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Sounders_FC "Seattle Sounders FC"), a [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") club.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-90)

In 2017, Nadella published a book titled _[Hit Refresh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit\_Refresh "Hit Refresh"),_ exploring his life and career at Microsoft.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-91) He announced that the profits from the book would go to Microsoft Philanthropies and through that to [nonprofit organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Nadella#cite_note-92)

Satya Narayana Nadella (born 19 August 1967 in Hyderabad, India) is an Indian-American business executive who serves as chairman and CEO of Microsoft, succeeding Steve Ballmer as CEO in 2014 and John W. Thompson as chairman in 2021. He is an American citizen of Telugu Hindu heritage, whose father Bukkapuram Nadella Yugandhar was an Indian Administrative Service officer and mother Prabhavati was a Sanskrit lecturer.

EDUCATION: Nadella attended Hyderabad Public School, Begumpet, earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Manipal Institute of Technology (1988), an MS in computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (1990), and an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business (1997).

CAREER: Before Microsoft, Nadella worked at Sun Microsystems. He joined Microsoft in 1992 and held several leadership roles including Senior VP of R&D for the Online Services Division, President of the Server & Tools Division, and Executive VP of the Cloud and Enterprise group. He led Microsoft's move to cloud computing and the development of one of the world's largest cloud infrastructures. Cloud Services revenue grew from $16.6 billion in 2011 to $20.3 billion by June 2013.

AS CEO: Nadella was announced as Microsoft's third CEO on 4 February 2014. His tenure emphasized collaboration with competitors (Apple, Salesforce, IBM, Dropbox) and famously declared "Microsoft ❤️ Linux," with Microsoft joining the Linux Foundation as a Platinum member in 2016. He revised the company mission to "empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more" and emphasized empathy, collaboration, and a 'growth mindset' culture. Notable acquisitions under his leadership include Mojang/Minecraft ($2.5 billion, 2014), Xamarin, LinkedIn ($26.2 billion, 2016), and GitHub ($7.5 billion, 2018). As of November 2023, Microsoft stock had increased nearly tenfold since 2014 with a 27% annual growth rate, ending a 14-year period of near zero growth. In 2024, his compensation was $79.1 million (up 63% from $48.5 million in 2023).

CONTROVERSIES: In October 2014, Nadella faced backlash after suggesting women should trust the system rather than ask for raises, later apologizing on Twitter and to employees. In January 2026, he asked people to stop calling AI "slop" and accept AI as the "new equilibrium," which backfired and led to the "Microslop" backlash described as a Streisand effect.

OTHER ACTIVITIES: He co-owns the Seattle Orcas Major League Cricket team and, with his wife, is part of the Seattle Sounders FC ownership group. He served on the Starbucks Board of Directors (2017-2024), was Chairman of The Business Council (2021-2022), and holds trustee positions at Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center and University of Chicago.

AWARDS: Time 100 honoree (2018, 2024), Financial Times Person of the Year (2019), Fortune Magazine Businessperson of the Year (2019), Pravasi Bharatiya Samman (2015), Padma Bhushan (2022), honorary PhD from Georgia Tech (2024), CNN-News18 Indian of the Year (2014).

PERSONAL LIFE: Married Anupama Priyadarshini in 1992; they have three children (a son and two daughters). His son Zain, who had cerebral palsy and was a legally blind quadriplegic, died in February 2022 at age 26. They live in Clyde Hill and Bellevue, Washington. He published the book "Hit Refresh" (2017) about his life and Microsoft career, with profits going to Microsoft Philanthropies.

URL: https://fortune.com/2022/07/15/ceo-board-chairman-losing-favor-independent-director-sp500

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is the web version of Fortune's "The Modern Board" newsletter, written by Aman Kidwai and published July 15, 2022, focusing on corporate leadership and board governance trends.

MAIN STORY - The dual CEO-chairman role is losing favor on public boards: According to a new survey from The Conference Board using data from ESGAUGE (shared exclusively with Fortune), the percentage of S&P 500 companies combining the board chair and CEO roles dropped from 49% in 2018 to 44% in 2022, while companies with an independent board chair increased from 30% to 37% in the same period. The trend toward separation is driven by board independence considerations and increased director workloads. Paul Washington, executive director of The Conference Board's ESG center, notes that separating the roles allows two people to manage board leadership and business operations, and "you get extra points with investors." However, many tech companies with founder-CEOs (like Facebook and Amazon) prefer combined roles. CEOs serve as board chairs at 55% of companies with annual revenue of $50 billion or more, but only 25% of companies with revenue under $100 million. Washington says the decision ultimately boils down to "the clear allocation of responsibilities between the CEO and the chair, and the chemistry between the two."

ADDITIONAL HEADLINES: (1) Euro and U.S. dollar reached parity for the first time since the euro's introduction ~20 years ago, signaling slowing European growth and potential recession; (2) Emirates Airlines criticized Heathrow Airport for lack of summer travel season preparation after the airport asked airlines to reduce daily passenger numbers; (3) Layoffs are often a sign of poor workforce planning, and employers should seek alternatives like employee-involved cost-cutting brainstorming; (4) JPMorgan missed Q2 estimates and halted share buybacks (stock down 33% YTD), while Morgan Stanley's investment bank revenue fell 55% and reported $400M+ in losses on corporate loans.

Written during the 2012 U.S. proxy season, the piece addresses the growing shareholder pressure for independent chairman roles and analyzes international variations in board leadership practices.

Key findings include:
- Board leadership structures depend on applicable laws/regulations and vary significantly across countries (Canada, Germany, UK, US), with no "one size fits all" solution to governance issues.
- Proponents of split CEO/chairman structures argue this model best positions companies for strong performance, while opponents note there is no irrefutable data proving split structures outperform combined ones and argue combination eliminates confusion and duplication.
- Spencer Stuart US Board Index data (2003–2011) shows a significant trend toward separation: companies combining CEO/chairman roles declined from 77% in 2003 to 59% in 2011, while those splitting roles rose from 23% to 41%. Independent non-executive chairmen increased from 9% (2004) to 21% (2011).
- Only 18 S&P 500 companies had a formal policy to separate the roles in 2011 (up from 6 in 2010).
- According to ProxyMonitor.org (May 2012), independent chairman proposals ranked third in proposal types for the 2012 proxy season. ISS 2012 Proxy Season Scorecard showed 48 independent chair proposals with an average support rate of 35.6% (compared to 26 proposals at 36.8% support in 2011).
- Deloitte's analysis of S&P 500 proxy statements (Jan 1–March 20, 2012) found only 20 companies had a current chairman emeritus designation. The chairman emeritus is an honorary title often granted to former chairmen to acknowledge contributions, maintain institutional knowledge, and preserve relationships—with duties varying by company and the title being rescindable at any time.
- The article advises boards to evaluate optimal leadership structures considering company circumstances, regulatory environment, costs/benefits, and recommends defining evaluation criteria, responsibilities, and compensation for independent chair roles and chairman emeritus positions at the time these roles are created.
- The article concludes that while most S&P 500 companies have historically combined CEO/chairman roles, the trend toward independent chairmanship is increasing, and the debate will likely continue given heightened shareholder focus and rising CEO turnover.

## BYD Ranks 91st in 2026 Fortune Global 500

2026/07/28

Shenzhen, China - July 28, 2026 - BYD ranked No. 91 on the 2026 Fortune Global 500 list released today, marking its fifth consecutive year on the prestigious index and firmly solidifying its position among the world’s top 100 enterprises.

![/material/__CN/byd-site/mea/news-list/fortune-global-91/500强-英文-4x5-2.jpg]()

In 2025, BYD delivered robust financial results and strong operational performance, reporting annual revenue of RMB 804 billion (USD 111 billion) and a net profit of RMB 32.6 billion (USD 4.5 billion). The company recorded annual New Energy Vehicle (NEV) sales of 4.6 million units, extending its leadership as the global top-selling NEV manufacturer and China’s leading automaker. This momentum continued into 2026, with cumulative sales exceeding 1.8 million units in the first six months. In July, BYD reached a major milestone as its 17-millionth NEV rolled off the production line, making it the first automaker worldwide to achieve this distinction.

Underpinning BYD’s performance is its strategic commitment to a “Technology-Based, Innovation-Oriented” philosophy. In 2025, the company allocated RMB 63.4 billion (USD 8.7 billion) to research and development—a 17% increase year-on-year—ranking first among China’s A-share listed companies for the second consecutive year. In Q1 2026, R&D expenditure reached RMB 11.3 billion (USD 1.6 billion), maintaining its lead over domestic mainstream automakers and emerging EV peers. To date, BYD’s cumulative R&D investment has surpassed RMB 250 billion (USD 34.5 billion). This continuous heavy investment has accelerated the deployment of disruptive technologies. In March 2026, BYD unveiled its 2nd Generation Blade Battery and FLASH Charging technology, with plans to deploy 20,000 FLASH Charging stations across China by year-end and 6,000 stations in international markets. In May, BYD pioneered advanced mobility standards by offering a one-year safety coverage commitment for its Urban Navigate on Autopilot and making its God’s Eye-B Intelligent Driving System LiDAR Version available across its entire vehicle portfolio, accelerating mainstream adoption of urban automated driving.

BYD’s global expansion gained significant momentum in 2025, with overseas sales surpassing 1 million units for the first time, reflecting a 145% year-over-year growth. International sales continued their upward trajectory in the first half of 2026, exceeding 780,000 units. The company’s globalization strategy has established strong market leadership in Latin America, key breakthroughs across Europe, and multi-market expansion in the Asia-Pacific region. Strategic developments this year include the opening of BYD’s first overseas SkyRail in Brazil and celebrating the 100,000th NEV produced at the BYD Brazil Factory; debuting the DENZA Z, Z9GT, and D9 models in Europe, establishing a new benchmark where technology drives elegance; introducing the BYD RACCO, its first model developed specifically for Japanese market; and marking the second anniversary of the BYD Thailand Factory. Today, BYD operates across 121 countries and regions, transitioning into a high-quality global enterprise rooted in localized operations.

BYD’s NEVs achieved cumulative carbon reduction of over 149.05 billion kilograms (149,057,400,317 kg) across energy production and vehicle lifecycle as of June 30, equivalent to planting more than 2.48 billion trees (2,484,290,005 trees).  Demonstrating its commitment to corporate social responsibility, BYD established a RMB 3 billion (USD 413 million) educational charity fund and finalized donation agreements with 127 universities across China, supporting over 6,000 students.

As a global leader in NEVs, BYD’s position among the world’s top 100 enterprises underscores the strength of its sustained technological innovation and expanding global presence. * # TSMC breaks into Fortune Global 500 top 100 for the first time

  + Staff writer, with CNA
  + - [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=taipeitimes.com)

  This year's Fortune Global 500 ranking listed Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電) among its top 100 companies for the first time.

  TSMC climbed 44 places to 82nd, with revenue of US$122.26 billion, a report published on Tuesday by New York-based *Fortune* magazine said.

  TSMC's entry into the top 100 for the first time underscored how surging demand for advanced chips is reshaping the scale and influence of companies in Asia and around the world, the report said.

  ![](https://img.taipeitimes.com/images/2026/07/30/p09-260609-321.jpg)

  Besides TSMC, Taiwanese electronics manufacturer Wistron Corp (緯創) climbed 298 places to 198th on this year's list — the largest jump among all companies ranked in this year’s Fortune Global 500 — with revenue of US$70.18 billion.

  Joining TSMC and Wistron on the Fortune Global 500 list were other Taiwanese companies, including Hon Hai Precision Industry Co (鴻海精密), Quanta Computer Inc (廣達電腦), Pegatron Corp (和碩) and WT Microelectronics Co Ltd (文曄科技).

  Amazon.com Inc topped this year's ranking of the world's largest companies by revenue, displacing Walmart Inc, which fell to second place after holding the top spot for 12 consecutive years, the report said.

  Other major technology companies, including Apple Inc and Nvidia Corp, ranked sixth and 28th, respectively.

  The Fortune Global 500 is an annual ranking of the world's 500 largest companies by revenue.

# TSMC and Tencent break into the top 100 of the Fortune Global 500 list, as Asia rides the AI boom

Angelica Ang

4 min read

* [TSM

  +0.71%](/quote/TSM/ "TSM")

The Fortune Global 500 has long been a scoreboard of corporate scale, reflecting the rise and fall of different industries and sectors. And in 2026, the ranking of the world's largest companies by revenue reflects just how much the AI boom is supercharging revenues across the tech and semiconductor supply chains.

For the first time, [Tencent](https://fortune.com/company/tencent-holdings/) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) have broken into the top 100, underscoring how surging demand for advanced chips and digital platforms is reshuffling corporate size and power across Asia and the wider world.

For the past year, [heightened global demand for AI](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/telcos-media-tech/tsmc-expects-strong-multi-year-demand-ai-chips-it-ramps-arizona-investment) has fueled stratospheric price jumps for semiconductors and other hardware and Asia—which forms the hardware backbone of the AI supply chain—is cashing in.

TSMC, which serves clients like [Apple](https://fortune.com/company/apple/) and [Nvidia](https://fortune.com/company/nvidia/), surged 44 spots, rising to No. 82. The chipmaker reported total revenue of $122.3 billion in 2025, up 35.6% from 2024. According to CNBC, Nvidia has reserved "the majority" of capacity at TSMC; last October, the two firms also partnered to [onshore advanced chip packaging capabilities to Phoenix, Arizona](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/tsmc-blackwell-manufacturing/).

Tencent also jumped 19 spots, just making the top 100 at No. 97. The software company, which is behind social media platforms like WeChat and QQ, and global gaming titles like *Honor of Kings* and *PUBG Mobile*, raked in [$104.6 billion in revenue](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tencentglobal_tencents-2025-financial-results-and-key-activity-7440037492076163072-Gz94/) in 2025, up 14% from the year before. While Tencent's gaming business grew in 2025, the company also reported strong growth in its advertising business, thanks to new AI-driven ad targeting. (Rumors of Tencent's falling gaming revenue, however, sparked a [Chinese gaming sell-off](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-22/tencent-slides-most-in-over-a-year-leading-china-gaming-selloff) last week; Tencent's own shares sank 7.1%, the most since April 2025.)

Tencent, much like its Chinese Big Tech peers, is investing in artificial intelligence. In March, the firm announced plans to [double AI-related spending to 36 billion yuan](https://www.forbes.com/sites/ywang/2026/03/19/tencent-to-double-ai-investments-to-52-billion-amid-chinas-openclaw-frenzy/), or $5.2 billion, to invest in model training and the hiring of talent.

Other Asian hardware firms also made huge leaps on the Global 500 list. [Wistron](https://fortune.com/company/wistron/), a Taiwan-based electronics manufacturer, rose 298 spots to No. 198, the largest jump by any company on this year's list. Wistron posted 2025 revenue of NT$2.19 trillion, or $70.18 billion, a 115% jump from the year before. Both Wistron and [Quanta Computer](https://fortune.com/company/quanta-computer/), along with Foxconn, are reporting surging revenue thanks to their new business assembling servers using AI processors from companies like Nvidia.

"In the past, one server generation typically lasted about two and a half to three years. You'd spend roughly a year designing a product, then it would stay in the market for about two years," Simon Lin, Wistron's chair, [told](https://fortune.com/2026/07/28/wistron-chair-simon-lin-nvidia-ai-boom-global-500) [*Fortune*](https://fortune.com/2026/07/28/wistron-chair-simon-lin-nvidia-ai-boom-global-500). "With AI, not only are there new products every year, but each generation is a meaningful technological leap."

Elsewhere in the AI supply chain, South Korean semiconductor firm [SK](https://fortune.com/company/sk-holdings/) Hynix rose 101 spots to No. 210, with revenue of $68.3 billion. [SK Hynix](https://fortune.com/company/sk-hynix/) has become the leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips, a key component of the AI processors produced by Nvidia and others. The company recently conducted [a $28.5 billion listing](https://fortune.com/2026/07/11/sk-hynix-us-stock-listing-nasdaq-second-largest-us-share-sale-ai-boom-hbw-memory/) in the U.S., the largest-ever share sale by a foreign company in U.S. markets.

## **Asia's new debuts**

Several Asia-based companies are making their debut on this year's Global 500 list.

Chery Automobile debuts at No. 383, with $41.8 billion in revenue. Chery has been China's top car exporter for 23 years, with overseas shipments making up 70% of its entire sales. It mostly exports internal combustion engine vehicles to markets like the Middle East, Africa, and Russia, though it is starting to export electric vehicles as well. Chinese car exports are a rare bright spot in the country's slumping car market; the country is on track to export [10 million cars this year](https://cnevpost.com/2026/05/13/china-auto-exports-seen-topping-10-million-2026/), up from 7.1 million last year.

WT Microelectronics debuts at No. 431, with $37.8 billion in revenue. The firm was established as a local semiconductor distributor in Taiwan in 1993, but has over the years grown into a major supply chain partner.

Finally, Daikin Industries enters the list at No. 498, with $33.3 billion in revenue. As the world's largest HVAC maker, Daikin has seen demand for its cooling products surge, as [Europe experienced one of its most intense heatwaves on record last month](https://fortune.com/2026/07/27/europe-employers-face-new-challenge-keeping-workers-safe-during-heatwaves/). According to the *Financial Times*, Daikin's European air conditioning and refrigeration sales [grew by almost 10% in the last financial year](https://www.ft.com/content/05d6b072-f480-45d3-9f00-1207fb2b75d2?syn-25a6b1a6=1), faster than in any other region.

There's one more Global 500 debut relevant to Asia: [Coupang](https://fortune.com/company/coupang/), often referred to as "South Korea's [Amazon](https://fortune.com/company/amazon-com/)," debuts on the Global 500 at No. 479 with $34.5 billion in revenue. The company is incorporated in Delaware and designates Seattle as its headquarters. Yet Coupang generates over 90% of its revenue from South Korea, where it operates one of the country's largest e-commerce and logistics networks.

This story was originally featured on [Fortune.com](https://fortune.com/2026/07/28/asia-global-500-tsmc-tencent-wistron-sk-hynix-chery-daikin-coupang/)

# CEO Message
