## A Global Market of Eight Billion

![Tadashi Yanai, Chairman, President and CEO](/jp/ir/direction/images/message_2026may.jpg)

Thanks to rising global support for LifeWear, Fast Retailing is on the cusp of what I would venture to call a boom in corporate growth. At last, I can confidently say that our goal of "becoming a truly global brand that customers across the globe love best" is no longer simply a dream, but a very real possibility.

In the six months from September 2025 through February 2026, Fast Retailing achieved its highest first-half performance on record by reporting revenue of 2.0552 trillion yen (+14.8% year on year) and business profit of 386.9 billion yen (28.3%). All UNIQLO operations continued to generate strong growth, with operations in North America, Europe, South Korea, and the Southeast Asia, India and Australia region all reporting double-digit revenue and profit growth, and Greater China markets achieving higher revenue and double-digit profit growth.

Today, people around the world are starting to recognize LifeWear as a new standard in clothing. What customers want and expect from their clothes has changed dramatically. Now, more and more people want to wear clothes carefully and for a long time. They also want those clothes to be attentively crafted in trusted factories, to be made from reliable materials that were procured safely and appropriately, and to be recycled and reused. These changing trends are driving the global boom for our business, and Fast Retailing is perfectly positioned to make the very most of the huge opportunities before us.

While unrelenting conflict continues around the world, cross-border corporate activities are becoming increasingly connected. As lifestyles converge globally, more and more products that sell well in a particular geographical area also sell well elsewhere, creating one single market. When we set out to become No.1 in Japan, our market was 120 million people. Today, we serve a global market with eight billion consumers, and it will be the companies with the courage to go out into the world and become best-loved brands that will triumph in the end. I am absolutely convinced about that.

In spring 2026, Fast Retailing formed a historic partnership with the Los Angeles Dodgers, channeling our mutual strengths into various community contribution activities to help create a better world. This is the first such partnership between the Dodgers and an overseas company, and we are determined to participate in even more activities that support local communities worldwide.

May 2026  
Tadashi Yanai

## Tadashi Yanai

Founder & President, Fast Retailing

Founder & President, Fast Retailing

Tadashi Yanai, is the Chairman, President, and CEO of FAST RETAILING CO., LTD., of which UNIQLO is a subsidiary. Since opening the first UNIQLO store in Hiroshima, Japan in 1984, the brand has become a global retailer with flagship stores from New York to Hong Kong. As the leader of UNIQLO Yanai‐san, oversees the business operations from designs, production to sales of his products. Tadashi Yanai’s philosophy of “changing conventional wisdom to change the world” and Japanese traditions has become UNIQLO’s central image.

Tadashi Yanai received his Bachelor’s degree in Economics and Politics from Waseda University in Tokyo, Japan. In 1984, he had taken over his father’s suite shop and transformed it into UNIQLO. Yanai‐san has since turned UNIQLO into a household name throughout Japan and Asia. Currently UNIQLO operates 1,020 retail outlets all over Asia, Europe, and North America. At 62 years old, Yanai‐san is ranked one of the wealthiest men in Japan and manages to maintain an altruistic side. He donated $12.2 million out of his personal fortune towards relief efforts for Japan after the 2011 tsunami. Yanai‐san also established a strong sense of corporate responsibility within his company; creating programs such has the Grameen Project, and All‐Product Recycling.

Over the years with him as president of Fast Retailing, the company has successfully acquired smaller foreign brands including France’s Comptoir des Cotonniers for women’s wear and Princesse Tam‐Tam lingerie, as well as America’s Theory. Yanai‐san’s has strong control over UNIQLO, with power to finalize all decisions, down to approving samples and colors, while keeping the consumers’ needs in mind.

Yanai was previously a member of the 21st Century Council.

This webpage is the official Fast Retailing corporate profile page for Tadashi Yanai, located on the company's investor relations/about us section. Tadashi Yanai serves as Chairman, President and CEO of FAST RETAILING CO., LTD., Chairman of the Fast Retailing Foundation, and Chairman of UNIQLO CO., LTD., in addition to holding director or executive officer positions at 15 other subsidiaries. He also serves as External Director of Nippon Venture Capital Co., Ltd. He was born on February 7, 1949.

- Aug 1972: Joined FAST RETAILING CO., LTD.

- Aug 1973: Senior Managing Director

- Nov 2002: Chairman and CEO, FAST RETAILING CO., LTD.
- Sep 2005: Chairman, President and CEO (current position)
- Nov 2005: Chairman, President and CEO, UNIQLO CO., LTD.
- Sep 2008: Chairman, G.U. CO., LTD. (current)
- Jun 2009: External Director, Nippon Venture Capital Co., Ltd. (current)
- Nov 2011: Director, LINK THEORY JAPAN CO., LTD. (current)
- Nov 2018: Chairman, Fast Retailing Foundation (current)
- Sep 2023: Chairman, UNIQLO CO., LTD. (current)

The native form of this [personal name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_name "Personal name") is *Yanai Tadashi*. This article uses [Western name order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_name#Western_name_order_(family_name_last) "Personal name") when mentioning individuals.

**Tadashi Yanai** (柳井 正, *Yanai Tadashi*; born 7 February 1949) is a Japanese [billionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire") businessman and the founder and president of [Fast Retailing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Retailing "Fast Retailing"), the parent company of [Uniqlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniqlo "Uniqlo") ("unique clothing").[[1]](#cite_note-1) As of May 2025, he is the richest person in Japan, with an estimated net worth of US$50.3 billion, and the 28th-wealthiest person in the world according to the *[Bloomberg Billionaires Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_Billionaires_Index "Bloomberg Billionaires Index")*.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Bloomberg-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tadashi_Yanai&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Yanai was born in [Ube, Yamaguchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ube,_Yamaguchi "Ube, Yamaguchi"), in February 1949.[[5]](#cite_note-nipponshacho-5) He attended Ube High School and later [Waseda University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waseda_University "Waseda University"), graduating in 1971 with a bachelor's degree in [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics") and [political science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_science "Political science").[[6]](#cite_note-frb-6) His uncle was an activist for the minority group known as *[Burakumin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burakumin "Burakumin")*, who have continued to suffer caste-based discrimination in employment and marriage in [modern Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Japan "History of Japan").[[7]](#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tadashi_Yanai&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In 1971, Yanai started in business by selling [kitchenware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchenware "Kitchenware") and men's clothing at a [JUSCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JUSCO "JUSCO") supermarket.[[8]](#cite_note-Fuels_J.Crew-8) After a year at JUSCO, he quit and joined his father's roadside tailor shop.[[8]](#cite_note-Fuels_J.Crew-8) Yanai opened his first [Uniqlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniqlo "Uniqlo") store in [Hiroshima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroshima "Hiroshima") in 1984,[[6]](#cite_note-frb-6) and changed the name of his father's company *Ogori Shoji* to [Fast Retailing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Retailing "Fast Retailing") in 1991.[[8]](#cite_note-Fuels_J.Crew-8) He has stated: "I might look successful, but I've made many mistakes. People take their failures too seriously. You have to be positive and believe you will find success next time."[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In 2019, Yanai stepped down from the board of [Softbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softbank "Softbank") after 18 years as an independent director at the Japanese technology conglomerate.[[10]](#cite_note-TadashiYanaiTheTimes-10)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tadashi_Yanai&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

In March 2011, Yanai donated 1 billion [yen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_yen "Japanese yen") to victims of the [2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Tōhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami "2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami").[[11]](#cite_note-11) In 2015, Yanai founded the Yanai Tadashi Foundation, which awards full scholarships and additional income to Japanese high school students admitted to selective colleges in the United States and the United Kingdom.[[12]](#cite_note-12) As of September 2025, 310 Japanese high schoolers have received the award.

Yanai is a major donor to the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles"). In 2014, he donated $2.5 million to establish the Yanai Initiative for Globalizing Japanese Humanities in partnership with Yanai's alma mater [Waseda University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waseda_University "Waseda University"). In 2020, he gave an additional $25 million to endow the initiative.[[13]](#cite_note-13) In 2024, he donated another $31 million to the initiative.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tadashi_Yanai&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Personal life")]

He is the son of Kanichi Yanai and Hisako Mori Yanai. Yanai is married and has two sons, Kazumi and Koji, and lives in Tokyo.[[15]](#cite_note-Forbes-15) In 2018, Yanai's son Koji launched the [Tokyo Toilet Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tokyo_Toilet "The Tokyo Toilet"), which later became the basis of the film [Perfect Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_Days "Perfect Days").[[16]](#cite_note-16)[[17]](#cite_note-17) He lives in a $50 million, 16,586-square-foot house outside of Tokyo and owns two golf courses in Hawaii.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tadashi_Yanai&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

* Yanai won the International Retailer of Year award for 2010 from the National Retail Federation in the US. He was the fourth Japanese national to win it, and the first since 1998, when it was won by [Masatoshi Ito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masatoshi_Ito "Masatoshi Ito"), owner and honorary chairman of the [Ito-Yokado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ito-Yokado "Ito-Yokado") retailing group. He was also chosen as best company president in a survey of Japanese corporate executives by Sanno Institute of Management in 2008 and 2009.[[19]](#cite_note-19)
* In 2012 he was included in the [50 Most Influential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_Most_Influential_(Bloomberg_Markets_ranking) "50 Most Influential (Bloomberg Markets ranking)") list of *[Bloomberg Markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_Markets "Bloomberg Markets")* Magazine.

## Published works

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Tadashi_Yanai&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Published works")]

args.summary:
This is a Wikipedia article about Tadashi Yanai (柳井 正, born 7 February 1949 in Ube, Yamaguchi, Japan), a Japanese billionaire businessman and the founder and president of Fast Retailing, the parent company of Uniqlo. As of May 2025, he is the richest person in Japan with an estimated net worth of US$50.3 billion and the 28th-wealthiest person in the world according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Early life and education: Yanai graduated from Waseda University in 1971 with a bachelor's degree in economics and political science. His uncle was an activist for the Burakumin minority group, who face caste-based discrimination in Japan.

Career: In 1971, he began selling kitchenware and men's clothing at a JUSCO supermarket. After a year, he joined his father's roadside tailor shop. He opened his first Uniqlo store in Hiroshima in 1984 and renamed his father's company Ogori Shoji to Fast Retailing in 1991. In 2019, he stepped down from Softbank's board after 18 years as an independent director.

Philanthropy: In March 2011, he donated 1 billion yen to victims of the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. In 2015, he founded the Yanai Tadashi Foundation, which awards full scholarships to Japanese high school students admitted to selective US and UK colleges (310 recipients as of September 2025). He is a major donor to UCLA, giving $2.5 million in 2014 to establish the Yanai Initiative for Globalizing Japanese Humanities (in partnership with Waseda University), $25 million in 2020, and an additional $31 million in 2024.

Personal life: He is the son of Kanichi Yanai and Hisako Mori Yanai. He is married with two sons (Kazumi and Koji) and lives in Tokyo. His son Koji launched the Tokyo Toilet Project in 2018, which became the basis of the film Perfect Days. Yanai lives in a $50 million, 16,586-square-foot house outside Tokyo and owns two golf courses in Hawaii.

Awards: Won the International Retailer of Year award for 2010 from the National Retail Federation (the fourth Japanese national to win it). Named best company president by Sanno Institute of Management in 2008 and 2009. Included in Bloomberg Markets' 50 Most Influential list in 2012.

Published works: "One Win, Nine Losses" (2003) and "Throw Away Your Success in a Day" (2009).

# Tadashi Yanai

## Founder & President, Fast Retailing & Uniqlo

He has grown his Japanese mass market clothing company into a group that has owns contemporary labels like J Brand and Theory.

![Tadashi Yanai](https://img.businessoffashion.com/resizer/v2/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-bof-media.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com%2Fimport%2Fprofiles%2Fasset%2F458%2F770x480-1530405148561710.jpg?auth=c464e53dc4b34154b6b2497f7f75fe2d7266383e3cc3314a61239380ebcee153&height=350)

Tadashi Yanai is the most successful businessman in Japan and the founder and president of Fast Retailing, now the world's fourth-largest apparel company, with over 2,000 retail stores and a portfolio of brands, including Uniqlo, Helmut Lang, Theory, Comptoir des Cotonniers, Princesse tam.tam, J Brand and GU. Uniqlo alone aims to increase sales to $50 billion by 2020, based largely on expansion in US, China and online.

In 1984, Yanai became president of his father’s clothing chain (which comprised 22 stores) and opened a new store in Hiroshima called the Unique Clothing Warehouse, later shortened to Uniqlo. By 1998, there were more than 300 Uniqlo stores across Japan.

Yanai is fond of saying that “Uniqlo is not a fashion company, it’s a technology company.” And indeed, the brand’s approach to making apparel has more in common with the iterative approach to product development embraced by the technology industry than the cyclical, trend-driven rhythm of the fashion industry.

In fact, despite the name of its parent company, it’s a misnomer to call Uniqlo a “fast fashion” company. While Zara has built the world’s largest apparel business based on rapidly responding to fast-changing fashion trends, getting items from factory to store in approximately two weeks, Uniqlo takes the exact opposite approach, planning production of its wardrobe essentials up to a year in advance.

Yanai is renowned as an inspirational leader, but is as humble as he is ambitious. He told Monocle magazine, "I might look successful but I've made many mistakes. People take their failures too seriously. You have to be positive and believe you will find success next time."

Yanai attended Ube High School and later Waseda University, graduating in 1971 with a Bachelor's degree in Economics and Politics. In March 2011 Yanai donated 1 billion Japanese yen to the victims of the Sendai earthquake.

# BYD to become world’s largest automaker by scale within five years, says chairman Wang Chuanfu

**3 min to read**

Jun 9, 2026 9:02 AM CEST

[Liu Miao](https://carnewschina.com/author/liumiaowriter/)
[4](#comments-261181)

![](https://carnewschina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/e59bbee78987-36-e1780987421690-800x451.png)

BYD's founder and chairman Wang Chuanfu. Credit: BYD

[# Understand China EV’s Market

During [BYD](https://carnewschina.com/topics/byd/)‘s 2025 annual general meeting held on June 9, 2026, Chairman and President Wang Chuanfu expressed strong confidence in the company’s future, projecting that BYD will achieve the status of the world’s largest automaker by scale within the next five years.

#### Strong overseas momentum

Wang highlighted the robust growth of Chinese automakers in international markets, noting that BYD’s products – characterised by competitive pricing, advanced technology, and superior user experience – are currently outperforming many local competitors.

While the company initially set an overseas sales target of 1.6 million vehicles for this year, Wang revealed that current trends suggest this figure will be surpassed. Emphasising a strategy of “long-termism,” Wang stressed the importance of localisation to ensure stable and sustainable growth, aiming for win-win outcomes in international markets.

#### Advancing intelligent driving

Addressing the future of automotive intelligence, Wang described the vehicle as a form of “embodied intelligence.” With 3.15 million intelligent driving-equipped vehicles already on the road globally, BYD is accumulating data at a rate of 200 million km per day. This dataset serves as a foundation for the company’s next-level autonomous driving capabilities.

Wang predicted that L3 and L4 autonomous driving technologies will reach the market sooner than expected. He confirmed that BYD is fully prepared across chips, algorithms, and data ecosystems. “Once the regulations are in place, BYD will quickly take off,” Wang stated, noting that the company has already established training centres in Europe, South America, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East to support this rollout.

#### Technology-Driven Premium Strategy

In response to shareholder concerns regarding domestic profit margins and brand image, Wang maintained that BYD’s path to high-end positioning lies in its core technology. He pointed out that in many international markets – such as Australia, Europe, and South America – BYD is already perceived as a premium brand.

“Automobiles are transportation tools that involve life safety, we must return to the essence of technology,” Wang said. He added that with a new wave of “stunning” technologies scheduled for release next year, the company expects to resolve challenges related to brand premiumization and per-vehicle profitability.

Looking ahead, Wang remains optimistic about the next three to five years. Supported by second-generation blade battery technology, rapid-charging innovations, and upcoming proprietary technologies, he expects BYD to benefit from a “dual-engine” drive of domestic and international growth, ultimately positioning the company to claim the top spot in the global automotive industry by 2030.

**Editor’s comment**

BYD’s brand image is indeed very different at home and abroad. In China, because a huge number of low-cost [ride-hailing](https://carnewschina.com/2026/01/10/byd-launches-sub-brand-to-mitigate-negative-sales-impact-from-ride-hailing-ties/) cars are BYDs, and many drivers work such long hours (even sleeping in their cars) that the vehicles end up smelly, it has had a bit of a negative impact on the brand’s reputation.

Wang Chuanfu, male, the Han nationality, was born on February 15, 1966, in Wuwei, Wuhu City, Anhui Province. He is a member of the Communist Party of China and currently serves as the Chairman of the board, Executive Director, and President of BYD Company Limited, as well as the Honorary President of the Huishang General Chamber of Commerce. He is known as a "Technology fanatic".

He graduated from Central South University in July 1987 with a degree in Metallurgical Physical Chemistry, and subsequently was admitted to the Beijing General Research Institute for Nonferrous Metals to pursue a master's degree in Materials Science. After obtaining his master's degree in 1990, he stayed at the institute to work, holding positions including Deputy Director, Director, Senior Engineer, and Associate Professor. In 1993, he became the General Manager of Shenzhen Bige Battery Co., Ltd. He resigned in 1995 to found BYD Company, whose business spans four major industries: automobiles, rail transit, new energy, and electronics. In July 2002, BYD was listed on the main board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. In 2003, BYD acquired Qinchuan Automobile, formally entering the automobile manufacturing industry. In 2009, he topped the Forbes China Rich List with a fortune of 39.6 billion yuan. In 2014, he led BYD in a comprehensive shift towards new energy vehicles, and in 2020, the company launched its Blade Battery technology. In March 2022, BYD announced the discontinuation of fuel-powered vehicle production. In August of the same year, he ranked first on the Forbes China Best CEO list. On November 16, 2022, BYD's 3 millionth new energy vehicle officially rolled off the production line. In October 2023, he stepped down as the legal representative and chairman of Shenzhen BYD Lithium Battery Co., Ltd. In January 2024, he presided over the ceremony for the first vehicle rolling off the production line at the BYD Uzbekistan Factory. In August 2025, he ranked 5th on the Fortune World's Most Influential Businesspeople list. In October 2025, he witnessed the production of BYD's 14 millionth new energy vehicle in Brazil.

In 2009, he was named the richest person in China by Forbes. In 2011, he topped the New Energy Rich List. In 2014, he received the individual Lifetime Achievement Award of the Zayed Future Energy Prize. In 2016, with a wealth of 15 billion yuan, he ranked 23rd on the Hurun IT Rich List. In 2018, he was selected as one of the "100 Outstanding Private Entrepreneurs in 40 Years of Reform and Opening-up". In 2021, he was recognized as the "Most Zero-Carbon Power Founder". In 2025, he launched the Megawatt-level flash charging technology and the Whole-domain kilovolt high-voltage architecture.

Life Experience

Early Life

Wang Chuanfu was born on February 15, 1966, into an ordinary farming family in Wuwei County, Anhui Province. At the age of thirteen, his father passed away, causing financial difficulties for the family. Two years later, his mother also passed away. At the time, he was taking his junior high school graduation exams, but he missed two subjects due to the circumstances and consequently failed to gain admission to a technical secondary school. He then attended a newly established Regular High Schools in Wuwei County. In 1983, with the support of his elder brother Wang Chuanfang and sister-in-law Zhang Juxiu, he was admitted to the Department of Metallurgical Physical Chemistry at the Central South Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, which was later renamed Central South University of Technology. In 1987, he graduated from Central South University with a major in Metallurgical Physical Chemistry. In the same year, he entered the Beijing General Research Institute for Nonferrous Metals to pursue a master's degree.

48

Research Experience

In 1990, after completing his Postgraduates studies, Wang Chuanfu stayed on to work in Room 301 of the Beijing General Research Institute for Nonferrous Metals under the Chinese Academy of Sciences. He presided over research on alkaline Nickel-cadmium secondary rechargeable Battery. During his research, he broke through technical bottlenecks related to battery electrode utilization efficiency and Battery capacity, while also investigating the optimization of inert anodes for Electrolyte. He published research reports on "Using Rare Earth Metal Neodymium as an Electrolytic Anode" and "The Influence of Yttrium Oxide (Y2O3) on Metal-Ceramic Structures," which attracted attention in academic circles. Subsequently, Wang Chuanfu developed a process for gemstone color enhancement using molten salt electrolysis, and the findings were published in the British journal "The Journal of Gemmology."

49

Career

* Battery Production

In 1993, the research institute established Big Power Battery Co., Ltd. in Shenzhen, and Wang Chuanfu was appointed as its general manager. In 1995, with the development of mobile phones, Wang Chuanfu focused on the Battery market and decided to resign and start his own business. He later registered and established BYD Industrial Company. Initially, BYD's main products were Nickel-Cadmium Batteries. As Japan ceased production of nickel-cadmium batteries starting from the mid-1990s, there remained a significant market demand for them. Wang Chuanfu led his employees in independently developing equipment and setting up manual assembly lines. They produced low-cost nickel-cadmium batteries, with costs 40% lower than those of Japanese manufacturers. In 1996, BYD became a Battery supplier for the Taiwanese cordless phone manufacturer DBTEL. In 1997, Wang Chuanfu successively developed nickel-cadmium batteries and Ni-MH battery. The sales volume of nickel-cadmium batteries reached 150 million units, ranking fourth globally and accounting for nearly 40% of the global market share. From 1998 to 2000, BYD established its European branch and American branch. In 2000, BYD invested heavily in Lithium Cell research and development, possessing its own core technology, and became Motorola's first Chinese lithium battery supplier. In 2001, BYD's sales revenue reached $155 million, with tax payments of $24 million, and it had 15,000 employees. In 2002, BYD was listed on the main board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

57

In 2008, BYD became China's largest mobile phone battery manufacturer with a global market share of nearly 15%. In 2014, BYD built the largest power battery production base at the time.

57

On March 29, 2020, BYD officially released its new-generation power battery product, the "The Blade Battery," which successfully passed the nail penetration test. This marked a milestone where China's New energy automobile power batteries successfully passed a global battery industry safety test. Wang Chuanfu stated that BYD uses the "Blade Battery" to defend the safety bottom line. In 2022, Wang Chuanfu stepped down as the legal representative, chairman, and general manager of Shenzhen BYD Battery Mold Co., Ltd. In 2023, he stepped down as the legal representative and chairman of Shenzhen BYD Lithium Battery Co., Ltd.

59

![Wang Chuanfu takes a photo with partners](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/b74124f3923c4969342acc52/b74124f3923c4969342acc52_url?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto/resize,m_lfit,h_400,limit_1)

Wang Chuanfu takes a photo with partners

Wang Chuanfu being interviewed

Wang Chuanfu delivers a speech

* Automotive Production

On January 23, 2003, Wang Chuanfu acquired a 77% stake in Xi'an Qinchuan Automobile Co., Ltd., announcing BYD's official entry into the automotive industry. In January, after announcing the acquisition of Qinchuan Automobile, BYD's Hong Kong stock price plummeted from HKD 18 to HKD 9. On September 22, 2005, BYD launched its first product, the mid-size family sedan F3, marking its debut on the Chinese automotive market stage. In 2006, BYD successfully developed the pure electric sedan F3e, equipped with its self-developed ET-POWER iron battery. In 2007, BYD Electronic (International) Company Limited was listed in Hong Kong. In 2008, BYD entered the New energy automobile track. In September, Warren Buffett purchased 225 million shares of BYD at HKD 8 per share, with a total transaction value of HKD 1.8 billion, accounting for 9.89% of the enlarged share capital. In 2009, BYD ventured into the pure electric bus sector. In 2010, 30 zero-emission, pollution-free BYD E6 pure electric taxis were deployed in Shenzhen. Wang Chuanfu introduced to a Xinhua News Agency reporter that the E6 pure electric vehicle uses the "green core" ET-POWER iron battery, which would not cause harm to the environment. In 2011, BYD K9 pure electric buses were put into service in Shenzhen. After 20 months of safe operation, the Shenzhen Municipal Government planned to purchase more pure electric buses to supplement the city's public transport capacity. In 2013, BYD announced that the BYD "Qin," equipped with the DMⅡ (second-generation dual-mode hybrid system), would be sold to the personal market. This established BYD's New energy vehicle strategy: promoting pure electric vehicles in the public transport and taxi sectors, and promoting DM dual-mode electric vehicles in the personal market. In 2014, Wang Chuanfu led BYD to shift its focus to new energy vehicles.

38

![Wang Chuanfu](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/35a85edf8db1cb1349545d3eef0d414e9258d109dddf/35a85edf8db1cb1349545d3eef0d414e9258d109dddf_url?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto/resize,m_lfit,h_1024,limit_1)

Wang Chuanfu

In 2015, BYD announced its "Full Industry Chain + Full Market" strategy for New energy vehicle, possessing technologies across the entire New energy automobile industry chain, including Power Battery, motors, and electronic controls. In 2016, Wang Chuanfu ranked 23rd on the Hurun IT Rich List with a wealth of 15 billion yuan. In January 2020, he stepped down as the legal representative of Shenzhen BYD Microelectronics. In 2021, BYD launched its DM series models, which used the more advanced DM-i Super Hybrid System compared to the single-motor mode used by traditional plug-in hybrid models. In August, Wang Chuanfu stepped down as chairman of BYD Property. On September 8, to address consumer concerns, BYD officially released its e-Platform 3.0 and unveiled the Ocean series concept car, Ocean-X, built on this platform. In November, Wang Chuanfu stepped down as chairman and legal representative of Wuhan BYD Company.

3

In March 2022, BYD Auto officially announced the cessation of production of internal combustion engine vehicles. In the same month, Wang Chuanfu stepped down as the legal representative of Shantou BYD and as chairman of Hangzhou BYD Auto Co., Ltd. On April 20, Wang Chuanfu stepped down as the legal representative of Nanjing BYD. On November 16, BYD's 3 millionth New energy automobile officially rolled off the production line.

5

In May 2023, Wang Chuanfu stepped down as the legal representative, chairman, and general manager of Shenzhen BYD Automotive Research and Development Co., Ltd. On the evening of August 9, BYD held a launch event for its 5 millionth new energy vehicle, with the Denza N7 being the model that marked this milestone. Wang Chuanfu announced: "Today, BYD has become the world's first automaker to achieve the production of 5 million New energy automobile. This is a highlight moment for BYD and also a highlight moment for Chinese brands." At the event, he stated that due to small market share and the need for further technological optimization and breakthroughs, the plug-in hybrid technology route had been abandoned by many automakers at that time, and there were also internal disputes within BYD, but the company still pursued the plug-in hybrid route. In December, Wang Chuanfu was elected as Honorary President of the Huishang General Chamber of Commerce.

36

On March 17, 2025, Wang Chuanfu announced the launch of BYD Megawatt Flash Charging at the BYD Super e-Platform Technology launch and the pre-sale event for the Han L and Tang L models, marking the world's first mass-produced passenger vehicle whole-domain kilovolt high-voltage architecture. On July 18, news emerged that Lei Jun accompanied BYD's Wang Chuanfu on a tour of Xiaomi's automobile factory. On December 5, BYD held an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders at its headquarters in Pingshan, Shenzhen. Wang Chuanfu (王传福) is a Chinese entrepreneur born on February 15, 1966, in Wuwei County, Anhui Province, who serves as Chairman, Executive Director, and President of BYD Company Limited. Known as a "technology fanatic," he is a member of the Communist Party of China and the Honorary President of the Huishang General Chamber of Commerce.

**Early Life and Education:** Born into an ordinary farming family, Wang lost both parents as a teenager (father at 13, mother at 15). With support from his elder brother Wang Chuanfang and sister-in-law, he graduated from Central South University in 1987 with a degree in Metallurgical Physical Chemistry, then earned a master's degree in Materials Science from the Beijing General Research Institute for Nonferrous Metals in 1990.

**Career Timeline:**
- 1990-1993: Researched alkaline nickel-cadmium batteries at the Beijing General Research Institute, publishing work on rare earth neodymium electrolytic anodes and yttrium oxide in metal-ceramic structures.
- 1993: Became General Manager of Shenzhen Bige Battery Co., Ltd.
- 1995: Resigned to found BYD, producing nickel-cadmium batteries at costs 40% lower than Japanese manufacturers.
- 1997: BYD ranked 4th globally in nickel-cadmium battery sales (~150 million units, nearly 40% global market share).
- 2000: Became Motorola's first Chinese lithium battery supplier.
- 2002: BYD listed on Hong Kong Stock Exchange main board.
- 2003: Acquired 77% of Xi'an Qinchuan Automobile, entering the automotive industry (stock briefly fell from HKD 18 to 9).
- 2005: Launched first car, the F3 sedan.
- 2006: Developed pure electric F3e with self-developed ET-POWER iron battery.
- 2008: Warren Buffett purchased 225 million BYD shares at HKD 8/share ($230 million, ~10% stake); BYD became Buffett's first privately-owned Chinese investment.
- 2009: Topped Forbes China Rich List with 39.6 billion yuan, becoming richest person in China.
- 2014: Led BYD's comprehensive shift to new energy vehicles.
- 2020: Launched "Blade Battery" technology; led mask production during COVID-19 (blueprints in 3 days, mask machine production in 7 days).
- March 2022: BYD discontinued fuel-powered vehicle production.
- August 2022: Ranked first on Forbes China Best CEO list.
- August 2023: 5 millionth new energy vehicle produced (world's first automaker to reach this milestone).
- 2025: Launched Megawatt-level flash charging and whole-domain kilovolt high-voltage architecture (world's first mass-produced passenger vehicle with this technology); ranked 5th on Fortune's Most Influential Businesspeople list; ranked 10th on World's 100 Best CEOs.
- October 2025: BYD's 14 millionth new energy vehicle produced in Brazil; Brazilian President Lula praised Wang as a "wizard in the field of electric vehicles."

**Personal Life:** Married to Li Ke with a daughter, Alice Wang. His elder brother Wang Chuanfang served as BYD Vice President.

**Philanthropy:** Donated 3 million yuan personally and 10 million yuan from BYD to Wenchuan earthquake relief (2008); established Central South University BYD Scholarship with 12.4 million yuan (2009); donated 1,000 household energy systems (25 million yuan) to Tibet (2010); donated 9 million yuan to BYD Charity Foundation (2011); donated 3 billion yuan for university scholarships on BYD's 30th anniversary.

**Wealth Rankings (selected):** 2026 Hurun Global Rich List: 160 billion yuan, 110th; 2025 Hurun Rich List: 180 billion yuan, 18th; 2024 Hurun Rich List: 135 billion yuan, 16th; 2009: 1st (richest in China); 2022 Forbes Global Billionaires: 19.5 billion USD, 83rd.

**Key Quotes and Evaluations:**
- Charlie Munger described Wang as "a combination of Thomas Edison and Jack Welch — he can solve technical problems like Edison and tackle corporate management issues like Welch."
- Forbes China called him "a persistent engineer and an adventurous entrepreneur."
- Wang stated: "BYD does not engage in marketing wars and does not disparage its competitors," emphasizing the company's strategy is "to focus on telling our own story well."

**Recent Activities (2024-2025):** Wang has maintained high-level engagement, meeting with Apple CEO Tim Cook (March 2024), launching BYD's fifth-generation DM hybrid technology (May 2024), attending the 2024 Beijing International Automotive Exhibition (shaking hands with Xiaomi's Lei Jun), responding to shareholder criticism of BYD's marketing at the 2024 AGM (June 2025), and addressing domestic sales decline and industry black PR at the December 2025 extraordinary general meeting. He delivered the 10,000th new energy vehicle in Uzbekistan (Yangwang U8) to President Mirziyoyev in January 2024.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Chinese chemist and businessman (born 1966)

In this [Chinese name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_name "Chinese name"), the [family name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_surname "Chinese surname") is  *[Wang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_(surname) "Wang (surname)")*.

| Wang Chuanfu |
| --- |
| 王传福 |
| Wang in 2023 |
| Born | (1966-04-08) 8 April 1966 (age 60)  [Wuwei County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuwei_County "Wuwei County"), Anhui, China |
| Education | [Central South University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_South_University "Central South University") ([BS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science")) Beijing Non-Ferrous Research Institute ([MS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science")) |

| Spouse | Married |

**Wang Chuanfu** ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 王传福; born 8 April 1966) is a Chinese chemist, billionaire entrepreneur, and the founder, chairman and CEO of the [BYD Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYD_Company "BYD Company").

Wang was born in [Anhui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhui "Anhui") to a poor farmer family. He then studied [metallurgy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallurgy "Metallurgy") and earned a [bachelor's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor's_degree "Bachelor's degree") and [master's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master's_degree "Master's degree"). After briefly managing a battery company, he founded BYD in 1995 with a loan from his cousin. BYD grew rapidly, and entered the automotive industry in 2003.

BYD Company is currently the world's largest mobile phone batteries manufacturer, and its subsidiary, BYD Auto is the world's largest [plug-in electric vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plug-in_electric_vehicle "Plug-in electric vehicle") manufacturer.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

## Early life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wang_Chuanfu&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Wang was born in [Wuwei County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuwei_County "Wuwei County"), Anhui, into a poor farming family with eight children. After the death of his parents, he was raised by his elder brother and sister while attending high school.[[2]](#cite_note-Fortune-2)

After graduating high school, he studied metallurgical [physical chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_chemistry "Physical chemistry") at the then Central South Industrial University (nowadays the [Central South University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_South_University "Central South University")) and graduated in 1987.[[3]](#cite_note-3) He went on to earn a master's degree in 1990 from the Beijing Non-Ferrous Metal General Research Institute (now GRINM Group).[[4]](#cite_note-Businessweek-4)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wang_Chuanfu&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Wang_Chuanfu_early_BYD_employee_card.png/250px-Wang_Chuanfu_early_BYD_employee_card.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wang_Chuanfu_early_BYD_employee_card.png)

BYD's first employee card issued to Wang Chuanfu in 1995, with the employee number 00001

In 1993, the Beijing Non-Ferrous Metal General Research Institute established a battery company called BAK Battery Co., Ltd. in [Shenzhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhen "Shenzhen"). Given Wang's academic background in related research fields, he was appointed as the general manager. During his tenure, he gained experience in business management and battery manufacturing.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

Seeing a market opportunity in mobile phones and anticipating industry shifts as Japan phased out [nickel-cadmium batteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickel–cadmium_battery "Nickel–cadmium battery"), Wang Chuanfu chose to leave BAK Battery in 1995 and founded his own company, BYD Company, outside of [Shenzhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhen "Shenzhen").[[4]](#cite_note-Businessweek-4) At 29 years old, he founded the company with his cousin [Lu Xiangyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Xiangyang "Lu Xiangyang"), who lent him CN¥250,000.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

In September 2008, [Warren Buffett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Buffett "Warren Buffett")'s [Berkshire Hathaway Inc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkshire_Hathaway_Inc. "Berkshire Hathaway Inc.") through [MidAmerican Energy Holdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MidAmerican_Energy_Holdings "MidAmerican Energy Holdings"), invested about US$230 million for a 9.89%[[7]](#cite_note-BYD_News1-7) share of BYD at [HK$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_dollar "Hong Kong dollar")8/[share](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Share_capital "Share capital").[[8]](#cite_note-chiu-8) Buffett credited this investment to [Charlie Munger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Munger "Charlie Munger"), Berkshire's vice chairman who saw the potential in the company.[[9]](#cite_note-9) Munger credited [Li Lu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Lu "Li Lu"), founder of Seattle-based asset manager Himalaya Capital, for introducing him to BYD and Wang. Munger spoke admiringly of Wang, saying that he came from a poor family but rose through hard work and talent.[[10]](#cite_note-10) Munger also called Wang a "genius" and a "workaholic".[[11]](#cite_note-11)

In early 2009, he was reportedly worth US$3.4 billion, placing him 408th on Hurun Report's Global Rich List 2014.[[12]](#cite_note-12) In late 2009, his net worth grew to $5.1 billion and was crowned China's richest man on the [Hurun Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Hoogewerf "Rupert Hoogewerf"). This was due largely to a five-fold increase in his company's value after [Berkshire Hathaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkshire_Hathaway "Berkshire Hathaway") bought 225 million new shares of BYD in 2008.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In 2008, Wang Chuanfu set a goal for BYD to become the leader in the Chinese automotive market by 2015, and to become the largest car manufacturer globally by 2025.[[14]](#cite_note-:02-14) He stated that electric vehicles would serve as BYD's "stepping stone" to skip the development of internal combustion engine vehicles and facilitate the company's entry into international markets.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

Around 2017 and 2019, BYD was heavily impacted by a reduction in electric vehicle government subsidies.[[16]](#cite_note-16)[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18) This led to a significant slowdown in sales volume and market share, with sharp decline in net profit over three consecutive years. Wang recalled that this was the company's "darkest moment", and at that time, the company's primary goal was merely "to survive".[[19]](#cite_note-19)

In November 2021, *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* reported that Wang's wealth had increased to $23.5 billion, making him the 14th richest person in China; this was due to a two-fold increase in BYD's share price over the previous year.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

Wang claims to spend 60-70% of his time on technology and [product development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_development "Product development").[[21]](#cite_note-21) He often implements minor design changes to bypass existing [patents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patents "Patents"). He once remarked that patents are static, stating, "In developing a new product, 60% comes from existing literature, 30% from sample analysis, and another 5% from raw materials and other external factors. Our own original research accounts for only about 5%."[[22]](#cite_note-22)

## Politics

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wang_Chuanfu&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Politics")]

Wang Chuanfu is a member of the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") (CCP).[[23]](#cite_note-23)[[24]](#cite_note-24)

In February 2025, Wang was among tech sector leaders to meet with [General Secretary of the CCP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party") [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") at the [Great Hall of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Hall_of_the_People "Great Hall of the People").[[25]](#cite_note-:0-25) Along with [Ren Zhengfei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren_Zhengfei "Ren Zhengfei"), Wang sat directly in front of Xi, in seats honoring their respective company's contributions as [national champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_champions "National champions").[[25]](#cite_note-:0-25)

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wang_Chuanfu&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Wang is married and lives in Shenzhen.[[26]](#cite_note-Forbes-26)

Wang Chuanfu (Chinese: 王传福; born 8 April 1966 in Wuwei County, Anhui, China) is a Chinese chemist, billionaire entrepreneur, and the founder, chairman, and CEO of BYD Company. He was born into a poor farming family with eight children and, after the death of his parents, was raised by his elder brother and sister. He studied metallurgical physical chemistry at Central South University (graduating 1987) and earned a master's degree in 1990 from the Beijing Non-Ferrous Metal General Research Institute (now GRINM Group).

In 1993, he was appointed general manager of BAK Battery Co., Ltd. in Shenzhen, a battery company established by his research institute. In 1995, at age 29, he left BAK Battery and founded BYD Company with a CN¥250,000 loan from his cousin Lu Xiangyang, seeing an opportunity in mobile phones as Japan phased out nickel-cadmium batteries.

In September 2008, Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway (through MidAmerican Energy Holdings) invested about US$230 million for a 9.89% stake in BYD at HK$8/share, a deal credited to Charlie Munger, who called Wang a "genius" and "workaholic." Following this, BYD's value increased five-fold, and by late 2009 Wang's net worth reached $5.1 billion, making him China's richest man on the Hurun Report. By November 2021, Forbes reported his wealth at $23.5 billion, making him the 14th richest person in China.

In 2008, Wang set goals for BYD to lead the Chinese automotive market by 2015 and become the world's largest car manufacturer by 2025, viewing electric vehicles as a "stepping stone" to bypass internal combustion engine development. Around 2017-2019, BYD was heavily impacted by reductions in electric vehicle government subsidies, causing three consecutive years of sharp profit decline—which Wang called the company's "darkest moment" when the primary goal was "to survive."

BYD is currently the world's largest mobile phone battery manufacturer, and its subsidiary BYD Auto is the world's largest plug-in electric vehicle manufacturer. Wang claims to spend 60-70% of his time on technology and product development, and has stated that only about 5% of his product development comes from original research, with 60% from existing literature and 30% from sample analysis.

Wang is a member of the Chinese Communist Party. In February 2025, he was among tech sector leaders who met with General Secretary Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People, seated directly in front of Xi alongside Ren Zhengfei in honor of their companies' contributions as national champions. Wang is married and lives in Shenzhen.

# BYD's chairman Wang aims high

By [Nick Carey](https://www.reuters.com/authors/nick-carey/)

June 16, 2026 4:00 PM UTC Updated June 16, 2026

*    
*    
*    

*    
*    
*    
*    
*    

![Image 2: Auto China show in Beijing](https://www.reuters.com/resizer/v2/MMJLNTCR4RDWNOXH4XUKG744X4.JPG?auth=36f4d257b29e3a2b336b69b253528063b6ca6813b9c4956a1e0d42ca63d0bb9e&width=1920&quality=80)

Wang Chuanfu, Chairman and CEO of Chinese automaker BYD, walks by a fur-covered car at the company’s booth at the Beijing International Automotive Exhibition (Auto China), in Beijing, China April 24, 2026. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersagency.com/en/licensereuterscontent/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

June 16 (Reuters) - Greetings from London!

While the [interim deal](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran-war-live-trump-says-us-tehran-have-reached-peace-deal-2026-06-15/) between the U.S. and Iran has been welcomed by markets, those hoping for less pain at the pump, including automakers, may find there is still a long road ahead.

Stay up to date with the latest news, trends and innovations that are driving the global automotive industry with the Reuters Auto File newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-auto-file/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fbusiness%2Fautos-transportation%2Fbyds-chairman-wang-aims-high-2026-06-16%2F)

It is [unclear](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-iran-deal-promises-end-war-how-it-will-work-remains-unclear-2026-06-16/) how and when the Strait of Hormuz will reopen, while shippers and their insurers will need to be confident in its reopening before they start using it again.

And besides high fuel prices, car owners from Tokyo to ​Detroit will find a [shortage](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/us-iran-deal-may-not-bring-quick-relief-auto-shops-2026-06-16/) of motor oil, paint and other products is not going to end any time soon.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

A fix to all these roadblocks could yet be a long way off.

Which brings us ‌to today’s Auto File…

BYD wants to be [top dog](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/byd-chairman-says-firm-will-be-worlds-biggest-automaker-5-years-shares-slide-2026-06-10/)

[Fain](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/united-auto-workers-fain-seeks-reelection-buoyed-by-strike-wins-2026-06-15/) tries again

Pain at the pump for the [RV industry](https://www.reuters.com/business/americas-rv-industry-feels-chill-war-high-gas-prices-2026-06-15/)

BYD’s No. 1 target

About two decades ago when BYD’s soft-spoken chairman Wang Chuanfu first said the Chinese automaker aimed to become the world’s largest automaker, there was laughter from assembled media, a Reuters colleague who was in the room recalls.

Back then, BYD was a minnow in the auto industry.

But a lot has changed as BYD’s sales grew from around 400,000 new cars in 2020 to 4.6 million last year, making it the world’s No. 6 automaker by sales ​in 2025.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Wang told investors at BYD’s annual shareholder meeting that the automaker aims to become world [No. 1 within five years](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/byd-chairman-says-firm-will-be-worlds-biggest-automaker-5-years-shares-slide-2026-06-10/).

BYD has struggled recently in its home market, which it says is partly due to ramping up ​production of its super-fast charging cars.

It is also pursuing a global expansion plan that saw its exports from China grow 65% in the first five months of 2026, with ⁠Brazil, Britain and Australia its largest markets.

To get to No. 1 will be harder than getting to No. 6. Toyota held the top spot last year with global sales of 11.3 million vehicles. That will require BYD to almost triple ​its sales in five years.

Yet after what BYD achieved in just five years, few in the industry will be laughing at that goal now.

Recommended reading:

Tesla’s [self-reported](https://www.reuters.com/world/tesla-presented-misleading-full-self-driving-safety-data-european-regulators-2026-06-15/) safety stats in European FSD push

Global electrified vehicle sales [up 3%](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/global-ev-registrations-rise-3-globally-may-bmi-data-shows-2026-06-15/) in May

The world’s first [trillionaire](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/spacex-ipo-makes-elon-musk-worlds-first-trillionaire-2026-06-11/)

UAW’s Fain runs ​again

United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain is seeking re-election as the head of the 400,000-member union, but as Reuters colleagues Kalea Hall and Nora Eckert report, his mixed record could make winning a second four-year term a bit of a tough sell.

You can read all about it [here](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/united-auto-workers-fain-seeks-reelection-buoyed-by-strike-wins-2026-06-15/).

In his early days as UAW president, Fain seemed unstoppable.

He led a six-week simultaneous strike against the Detroit Three automakers in 2023, notching up historic 25% wage increases for UAW workers and unionized Volkswagen’s Chattanooga plant, a victory in the U.S. South that had eluded the ​union for decades.

But despite spending $40 million to organize more plants in the South, the unionization push came to naught after [losing a vote](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/uaws-influence-tested-pivotal-alabama-mercedes-benz-factory-union-vote-2024-05-17/) at Mercedes-Benz’s Alabama plant.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Rivals are seeking to turn the race into a referendum on Fain's leadership.

A federal ​watchdog, appointed in 2021 to oversee union management after a corruption scandal, has accused Fain of retaliating against other UAW leaders and of a lack of transparency. Fain responded by saying every board has its challenges. "Everything we've done, we've done by putting this membership ‌first," he said, ⁠adding that the UAW has “adopted almost every reform suggested by the monitor”.

Fuel spike hurts RV industry

Spring is usually prime selling season for U.S. recreational vehicles, but thanks to high gas prices driven by the Iran war, this year is turning into a dud.

As Reuters colleague Timothy Aeppel reports, RV registrations by consumers fell 22% in March and nearly 17% in April. You can read all about it [here](https://www.reuters.com/business/americas-rv-industry-feels-chill-war-high-gas-prices-2026-06-15/).

The RV industry has struggled in recent years, with sales crashing after COVID-19, leaving the industry with a huge inventory overhang that has taken years to work down.

As one industry consultant told Reuters, the Iran conflict and high gas prices have "killed whatever speed there was" in the market.

Scrambling for China imports

Ford and other automakers are rushing ​to get U.S. government approval to keep on importing models ​from China ahead of a ban on its software ⁠in connected vehicles.

As Reuters colleague Nora Eckert reports, Ford has asked the U.S. Commerce Department for authorization to keep importing its China-built Lincoln Nautilus SUV.

You can read all about it [here](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/us-connected-car-rule-prompts-ford-other-automakers-seek-licenses-china-built-2026-06-15/).

Ford is among a group of automakers navigating a complex and opaque licensing process, which is exposing the extent to which the U.S. auto industry has intertwined its supply chains with ​China.

The rules include a ban on most Chinese-developed and -maintained software and cover companies with significant Chinese ownership. Lawmakers [have proposed](https://www.reuters.com/world/house-lawmakers-introducing-bill-toughen-us-ban-chinese-vehicles-2026-05-11/) making the rules even tougher.

Software prohibitions take effect for model ​year 2027 and separate restrictions ⁠on hardware kick in for model year 2030. Ford said it will likely start importing 2027 model year Nautilus vehicles in January, so has several months to secure an authorization.

Fast Laps

Volkswagen will shrink its workforce in Germany by [19,000 people](https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/volkswagen-reduce-workforce-by-19000-by-end-year-ceo-says-2026-06-11/) by the end of the year, CEO Oliver Blume is set to tell investors at its June 18 AGM.

Renault's EV order book is [up by 50%](https://www.reuters.com/business/renault-electric-vehicle-orders-have-surged-since-start-iran-war-says-ceo-2026-06-10/) in some markets, such as France and Germany, since the [Iran](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran/) war started, the carmaker's CEO Francois Provost told Reuters.

China’s BYD is looking to take over an ⁠existing factory in [southern ​Europe](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/byd-looking-take-over-existing-factory-second-european-ev-plant-executive-says-2026-06-10/) for its second assembly plant on the continent, with Spain among the countries on its shortlist, a top executive said.

General Motors may [scrap plans](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/gm-may-ditch-lfp-batteries-future-evs-2026-06-10/) to ​use a lower-cost, iron-based battery chemistry that many automakers are using to cut EV costs, its head of battery technology said.

Aluminum supplier Novelis has [restarted production](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/novelis-restarts-production-new-york-plant-key-ford-trucks-2026-06-10/) at its Oswego, New York facility, a plant key to Ford's F-150 pickup truck line, months after [two fires halted operations](https://www.reuters.com/world/another-fire-ignites-ford-aluminum-supplier-novelis-2025-11-20/).

Volkswagen, Stellantis and Renault, which account for about 60% ​of Europe's car output, are [urging the EU](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/europes-top-carmakers-urge-simple-made-europe-rules-2026-06-12/) to adopt a simple "[Made in Europe](https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/what-is-eus-draft-made-europe-law-2026-02-17/)" rule and stronger incentives to boost local production.

Please follow these guidelines to create your summary:

1. Identify and preserve the main topic or purpose of the webpage.
2. Retain key facts, statistics, and data points that are central to the content's message.
3. Keep important quotes from credible sources or experts.
4. Maintain the chronological order of events if the content is time-sensitive or historical.
5. Preserve any lists or step-by-step instructions if present.
6. Include relevant dates, names, and locations that are crucial to understanding the content.
7. Summarize lengthy explanations while keeping the core message intact.

When handling different types of content:

- For news articles: Focus on the who, what, when, where, why, and how.
- For scientific content: Preserve methodology, results, and conclusions.
- For opinion pieces: Maintain the main arguments and supporting points.
- For product pages: Keep key features, specifications, and unique selling points.

Your summary should be significantly shorter than the original content but comprehensive enough to stand alone as a source of information. Aim for about 25-30 percent of the original length, unless the content is already concise.

Present your summary in the following format:

```
{
   "summary": "Your summary here, structured with appropriate paragraphs or bullet points as needed",
   "key_excerpts": "First important quote or excerpt, Second important quote or excerpt, Third important quote or excerpt, ...Add more excerpts as needed, up to a maximum of 5"
}
```

Example 1 (for a news article):

This mission is a crucial step in NASA's plans to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon by 2030.",

The mission will test critical systems for future long-duration stays on the Moon, explained Lead Engineer Sarah Johnson. }

Example 2 (for a scientific article):

Researchers analyzed satellite data from 1993 to 2022 and found that the rate of sea-level rise has accelerated by 0.08 mm/year² over the past three decades. This acceleration is primarily attributed to melting ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica. The study projects that if current trends continue, global sea levels could rise by up to 2 meters by 2100, posing significant risks to coastal communities worldwide.",
```json
   "key_excerpts": "Our findings indicate a clear acceleration in sea-level rise, which has significant implications for coastal planning and adaptation strategies, lead author Dr. Emily Brown stated. The rate of ice sheet melt in Greenland and Antarctica has tripled since the 1990s, the study reports. Without immediate and substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, we are looking at potentially catastrophic sea-level rise by the end of this century, warned co-author Professor Michael Green."
```

This is a Reuters "Auto File" newsletter (dated June 16, 2026) authored by Nick Carey, covering multiple stories in the global automotive industry. The lead story focuses on BYD Chairman Wang Chuanfu's ambition to make the Chinese automaker the world's No. 1 automaker within five years. About two decades after Wang first made this claim (to laughter from media), BYD has grown from ~400,000 new cars sold in 2020 to 4.6 million in 2025, making it the world's No. 6 automaker. To reach No. 1, BYD would need to nearly triple sales to surpass Toyota's 2025 global sales of 11.3 million vehicles. BYD has struggled recently in its home market (partly due to ramping up super-fast charging car production) but exports grew 65% in the first five months of 2026, with Brazil, Britain, and Australia as its largest markets.

Other stories covered include: (1) UAW President Shawn Fain seeking re-election, with a mixed record including historic 25% wage increases from the 2023 Detroit Three strike and a victory at VW's Chattanooga plant, but a failed $40 million unionization push in the South after losing a vote at Mercedes-Benz's Alabama plant, plus accusations from a federal watchdog of retaliation and lack of transparency; (2) The U.S. RV industry suffering from high gas prices driven by the Iran war, with registrations down 22% in March and nearly 17% in April; (3) Ford and other automakers rushing to secure U.S. government approval to keep importing China-built models (like the Lincoln Nautilus SUV) ahead of a ban on Chinese software in connected vehicles—software prohibitions take effect for model year 2027 and hardware restrictions for model year 2030; and (4) Various "Fast Laps" briefs including VW cutting 19,000 German jobs by year-end, Renault's EV orders up 50% since the Iran war began, BYD seeking a second European plant in southern Europe (Spain on shortlist), GM possibly dropping LFP battery plans, and Novelis restarting production at its Oswego, New York plant key to Ford's F-150 line.

The newsletter also notes the U.S.-Iran interim deal has been welcomed by markets but that Strait of Hormuz reopening timing remains unclear, with shortages of motor oil, paint, and other automotive products persisting.
args.key_excerpts: "Wang told investors at BYD's annual shareholder meeting that the automaker aims to become world No. 1 within five years."

# Hermès CEO Axel Dumas explains how he's preserving desirability as group tops €16bn revenue

**By**   
  [![](https://media.fashionnetwork.com/m/572e/7d61/e19a/199f/651b/af09/ba10/b0b6/e424/bbac/60x60/bbac.png)   
 Olivier Guyot](/auteur/Olivier-Guyot.html "Olivier Guyot")

**Translated by**   
 Nicola Mira

**Published**   
  February 13, 2026

Luxury consumption in China is slumping? Far from it. [Hermès](/tags-hermes "Hermès") once again recorded revenue growth in Asia in 2025, making strong progress in the ever-crucial Greater China region. \  
  
The French luxury giant topped the €16 billion revenue mark in 2025, despite unfavourable exchange rates, and continues to grow in the region. As though changes in consumption behaviour had no impact on Hermès.  
  
The family-owned group, headed since 2013 by CEO [Axel Dumas](/tags-axel-dumas "Axel Dumas"), has always occupied a unique place in the world of luxury, something that seems to be currently protecting its business in China and the world at large.

![Axel Dumas (right), CEO of Hermès, with CFO Eric du Hagoüet at the presentation of the group’s results](https://media.fashionnetwork.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=contain,width=1000,height=1000,format=auto/m/6b6b/dc7c/e658/a5d4/4459/fd51/045c/6a5a/36fe/6f4b/6f4b.jpg)

Axel Dumas (right), CEO of Hermès, with CFO Eric du Hagoüet at the presentation of the group’s results - Screenshot presentation Hermes

On February 12, speaking at the presentation of the group’s annual results, Dumas illustrated his approach to making Hermès desirable. He also emphasised the luxury label’s uniqueness, a by-product of Dumas’s constant vigilance in controlling output volumes to ensure rarity.  
  
“The first, very important element for me is balancing our lines of business. When I started as CEO, our leather products accounted for 55% of sales. Nowadays, their share is approximately 45%. This means we don’t depend on one business line only, and we have greatly expanded in other fields,” said Dumas, underlining the growth of Hermès’s ready-to-wear, jewellery, footwear and home decoration lines.

**Ads**

![](https://media.fashionnetwork.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto/pb-assets/12/12272_1784193366.jpg)

He also emphasised how each division adopts a specific approach.  
  
“I ask each business line to be well-balanced. We don’t sell just one leather goods item, nor a single model of shoes, etc. It’s important for our collections to have a very broad appeal. This means having ambitious goals in terms of new products and creativity. We don’t have a marketing department. Each business line puts forward its creations. This can sometimes spark fruitful discussions between those who have the right to buy and those who have the right to create. In the end they must find a common ground,” he said.  
  
Dumas pointed out that this leads to a highly diversified product range, making catalogue management sometimes complex, but also giving the label the platform to stand out on the market.  
  
“We have approximately 50,000 active SKUs. The number usually recommended is 7,000,” he said. He underlined that "We're not ready to go there, In fact, we're not heading in that direction at all.”   
  
According to Dumas, this diversity goes hand in hand with the effort to promote all the group's many products. The group has drawn attention to the fact that in 2025 it opened its 24th leather goods factory, and product expertise is the foundation of Hermès’s desirability, according to Dumas.  
  
“The third key element is that we’re an artisanal company. A Hermès handbag needs 16 hours of manual work. In a country where the working week is 35 hours. Our volumes are therefore pretty low. And this protects us. I believe that what makes our products desirable is our expertise, the quality of our materials, and our creativity. As long as we do well in these three areas, we will be desirable.”

![Hermès has developed a range of product categories](https://media.fashionnetwork.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=contain,width=1000,height=1000,format=auto/m/2e9e/7f31/0866/0358/4be0/cbdd/0b70/14d8/2d5d/45b4/45b4.jpg)

Hermès has developed a range of product categories - Hermès

It is this desirability that is currently allowing Hermès to increase its prices by an average of 5% to 6% at the start of the year, to offset the impact of unfavourable exchange rates and rising manufacturing costs.  
  
This is why the group is continuing to boost its output capacity even if volumes are limited. In 2025, the group allocated investments worth €226 million to strengthen its production capacity, chiefly by opening new leather goods factories in France: in Loupes, where it is set to open in 2026, in Charleville-Mézières, scheduled for 2027, and in Colombelles, planned for 2028. A few weeks ago, the group also announced plans for an opening in 2030 in Les Andelys.  
  
But Hermès is investing in its other business lines too. It has started work on enlarging its watch-making site in Noirmont, Switzerland, and on setting up a tableware factory in Couzeix, France. The group is also discreetly buying stakes in companies in a number of sectors, in order to safeguard its industrial know-how and its access to specific materials.  
  
“We’ve started to integrate more know-how within the group, buying stakes in other companies. We now own tanneries in France, it's great. Our goal is simple. When we need to preserve unique know-how, we do it. This is the case in jewellery, where we have acquired stakes in some jewellery companies. It’s a fragmented, artisanal sector. And if you lose a good crimper …,” said Dumas. “We’re investing in footwear in Italy. We have Hermès watches, in which we keep investing to develop our capabilities. We have ambitious plans for fragrances,” he added.

![Leather remains the group’s flagship business, but Hermès is developing new categories](https://media.fashionnetwork.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=contain,width=1000,height=1000,format=auto/m/37d0/53b2/d5fe/0b3b/5d58/4b37/51d8/fef3/6ed0/91cf/91cf.jpg)

Leather remains the group’s flagship business, but Hermès is developing new categories - Hermès

The group is keen to expand in the beauty category and, while developing its fragrance range to reach critical mass, it also sells cosmetics and is about to launch into skincare.  
  
In what is a closely scrutinised project, Dumas also said that Hermès has reached out into new areas of expertise in order to extend its future haute couture offering. “We’ve brought new ateliers on board. We’ve hired dressmakers. What I’ve seen is great. I’m extremely excited and proud of the work done by our staff. But we'll present it when we're ready. It has to be complete, and the time must be right,” he said.  
  
We, therefore, need to wait to find out when Hermès will unveil its first haute couture line, which will play its part in boosting the desirability of the label as a whole.

**Axel Dumas** (born 3 July 1970) is a French billionaire heir and business executive. He is the chief executive officer (CEO) of [Hermès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermès "Hermès"), and a sixth-generation member of the Hermès-Dumas family.

## Early life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Axel_Dumas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Axel Dumas was born on 3 July 1970 in [Neuilly-sur-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuilly-sur-Seine "Neuilly-sur-Seine") near Paris.[[1]](#cite_note-lechohermesne-1)[[2]](#cite_note-lemondeuniederriere-2) His ancestor five times removed, [Thierry Hermès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Hermès "Thierry Hermès"), founded Hermès in 1837.[[3]](#cite_note-ftlunchwithaxeldumas-3)[[4]](#cite_note-fthermescountson-4) His paternal uncle, [Jean-Louis Dumas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Louis_Dumas "Jean-Louis Dumas"), was the CEO of Hermès.[[5]](#cite_note-ftnamedashermeschief-5) His father, [Olivier Dumas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Dumas?action=edit&redlink=1 "Olivier Dumas (page does not exist)"), is a physician and the author of many articles about [Jules Verne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jules_Verne "Jules Verne").[[6]](#cite_note-parismatchsuccession-6) His mother died in 2003.[[2]](#cite_note-lemondeuniederriere-2) His cousin, [Pierre-Alexis Dumas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre-Alexis_Dumas "Pierre-Alexis Dumas"), is Hermes's artistic director.[[7]](#cite_note-wmagamanwithaclan-7) He is a sixth-generation member of the Hermès-Dumas family.[[8]](#cite_note-Business_of_Fashion-8)

Dumas earned a bachelor's degree in philosophy from [Paris-Sorbonne University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris-Sorbonne_University "Paris-Sorbonne University") and a master of Laws.[[2]](#cite_note-lemondeuniederriere-2) He graduated from [Sciences Po](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sciences_Po "Sciences Po"),[[2]](#cite_note-lemondeuniederriere-2) and he attended an executive program at the [Harvard Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School").[[6]](#cite_note-parismatchsuccession-6)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Axel_Dumas&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Dumas was an investment banker for [Paribas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paribas "Paribas") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), China from 1995 to 1997, in Paris from 1997 to 1999, and in New York City from 1999 to 2003.[[2]](#cite_note-lemondeuniederriere-2)[[4]](#cite_note-fthermescountson-4)

Dumas joined Hermès as an auditor in 2003.[[2]](#cite_note-lemondeuniederriere-2)[[4]](#cite_note-fthermescountson-4) He became the CEO of its jewellery division in 2006, and the CEO of its leather goods division in 2008.[[2]](#cite_note-lemondeuniederriere-2)[[4]](#cite_note-fthermescountson-4) He was appointed as chief operating officer of the company in June 2013,[[9]](#cite_note-voguehermesmoves-9) supervised by [Patrick Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Thomas_(businessman) "Patrick Thomas (businessman)") until his departure in January 2014.[[5]](#cite_note-ftnamedashermeschief-5)[[7]](#cite_note-wmagamanwithaclan-7)

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Axel_Dumas&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Dumas is married to [Elisabeth Franck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisabeth_Franck?action=edit&redlink=1 "Elisabeth Franck (page does not exist)"), a journalist for *[Libération](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libération "Libération")*.[[10]](#cite_note-acrimedreymondliberationmodedemploi-10)

With his family, Dumas is an heir to a 30 billion € fortune, making them France's third richest family as of 2017.[[11]](#cite_note-challengesles500plusdumas-11)

Axel Dumas is a French billionaire heir and business executive who serves as the CEO of Hermès, the luxury goods company. Born on 3 July 1970 in Neuilly-sur-Seine, France, he is a sixth-generation member of the Hermès-Dumas family, with his five-times-removed ancestor Thierry Hermès having founded Hermès in 1837. His uncle, Jean-Louis Dumas, was a former CEO of Hermès, and his cousin Pierre-Alexis Dumas serves as the company's artistic director.

Dumas earned a bachelor's degree in philosophy from Paris-Sorbonne University, a master of Laws, graduated from Sciences Po, and attended an executive program at Harvard Business School. He began his career as an investment banker for Paribas in Beijing (1995-1997), Paris (1997-1999), and New York City (1999-2003). He joined Hermès as an auditor in 2003, became CEO of its jewellery division in 2006, CEO of its leather goods division in 2008, and was appointed chief operating officer in June 2013 under supervisor Patrick Thomas. He became CEO in June 2013, succeeding Patrick Thomas who departed in January 2014.

Dumas is married to Elisabeth Franck, a journalist for Libération. His family is heir to a €30 billion fortune, making them France's third richest family as of 2017. His father, Olivier Dumas, is a physician and author on Jules Verne.

# Axel Dumas

## Executive Chairman, Hermès

As a sixth-generation member of the family that founded Hermès, he ran its crucial jewellery and leather goods divisions before becoming executive chairman.

![Axel Dumas](https://img.businessoffashion.com/resizer/v2/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-bof-media.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com%2Fimport%2Fprofiles%2Fasset%2F55%2Fe423629dae1404209bab13fc847257b5c37e575f.jpeg?auth=164b8d64a2b4a5e20e805ae559a3d68eb90727748f4dd2379d70452b4fc718ec&height=350)

A sixth-generation member of the Hermès family and Jean Louis Dumas’ nephew, Axel Dumas took over as executive chairman of his family’s Paris listed company in 2014. Previously, he was co-chief executive and head of operations of Hermès International Société, Europe’s third-largest luxury goods group, founded as a saddle and harness maker in 1837.

Dumas was appointed in challenging times for the company. Speaking to the Financial Times he described the spar between Hermès and LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault as “the battle of our generation,” which resulted in Arnault relinquishing his 23 percent stake in the company. Aside from the “neither desired nor desirable” attentions of Arnault, Hermès is on extremely sure commercial footing. Dumas oversees the company at a time of record profitability, as Hermès is a globally regarded company positioned at the pinnacle of the luxury market.

He served as the managing director of operations, chief operating officer, and head of operations & sales at Hermès for three years, from May 2011. Dumas joined Hermès in 1993, having worked for Paribas, now part of BNP Paribas, as a banker in Beijing and New York. Previously, he has held the position of brand commercial director of France, the group’s biggest market accounting for 17 percent of total sales. In the past, he has headed the jewellery department and the leather goods division, the group’s most lucrative division, which contributes half of Hermès’ sales.

Hermès posted a 15 percent rise in net profit for 2018, with its operating income rising 6 percent to €2 billion. In March 2019, the house announced its expansion into skincare and cosmetics by 2020. As a result, Dumas stepped down from his position on L'Oréal's board of directors, with the cosmetics giant citing "a possible conflict of interest."

He studied at Sciences Po in Paris and at Harvard University in the United States.
