# TotalEnergies

## TotalEnergies in Fortune Rankings

* About
* Change The World

TotalEnergies is a global energy company based in France, operating across the entire energy value chain. Originally focused on oil and gas, it has expanded into electricity, renewables, and low-carbon solutions. Its strategy combines continued growth in oil and gas production, particularly LNG, with investment in lower-carbon electricity and fuels; it targets 100 gigawatts of gross renewable-generation capacity and 100–120 terawatt-hours of annual electricity production by 2030.

Change the World 2025 

TotalEnergies is perhaps the least known of the five so-called Big Oil giants, in large part because it doesn’t own U.S. gas stations. But, as the oil and gas industry more broadly retrenches from renewable power and doubles down on fossil fuels, the French energy behemoth has quietly emerged as the industry’s clean energy leader.

In less than 15 years, Total has built or acquired more than 30 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity—mostly solar power—with the aim of hitting 100 gigawatts by 2030 amid a rapid global buildout from the U.S. to Europe to India. That goal is enough to power roughly 75 million homes annually.

Earlier this year, Total paid nearly $2 billion to acquire the German renewables developer VSB Group. Chairman and CEO Patrick Pouyanné has called the integrated power business—led by renewables—the “second pillar” and fastest-growing part of the company, even as its oil and gas production volumes continue to rise.

Together, the companies on the list combined for $21.0 trillion in revenue and $2.1 trillion in profits last year, while employing 30.5 million people worldwide. These figures represent roughly two-thirds of U.S. GDP.

Amazon recorded **$716.9 billion in revenue for 2025 (a 12.4% jump), narrowly edging out Walmart at $713.2 billion.** Only four companies have ever claimed the No. 1 spot in 72 years: **General Motors, ExxonMobil, Walmart**, and **now Amazon**.

This webpage from demandsage.com presents the complete Fortune 500 Companies List for 2026 (the 72nd edition of the ranking), updated June 25, 2026. Key highlights: Amazon has ended Walmart's 13-year winning streak to become the new No. 1 company, recording $716.9 billion in revenue for 2025 (a 12.4% jump), narrowly edging out Walmart at $713.2 billion. Only four companies have ever held the No. 1 spot in 72 years: General Motors, ExxonMobil, Walmart, and now Amazon.

Collectively, the 500 companies generated $21.0 trillion in revenue and $2.1 trillion in profits, employing 30.5 million people worldwide—representing roughly two-thirds of U.S. GDP. The top 10 companies alone generated $4.48 trillion in revenue.

Top 10 Companies (2026): 1) Amazon ($716,924M, Internet Services, WA, CEO Andrew R. Jassy), 2) Walmart ($713,163M, General Merchandisers, AR, John R. Furner), 3) UnitedHealth Group ($447,567M, Healthcare Insurance, MN, Stephen J. Hemsley), 4) Apple ($416,161M, Computers, CA, Tim Cook), 5) Alphabet ($402,836M, Internet Services, CA, Sundar Pichai), 6) CVS Health ($402,067M, Healthcare Pharmacy, RI, David Joyner), 7) Berkshire Hathaway ($371,444M, Insurance, NE, Greg Abel), 8) McKesson ($359,051M, Healthcare Wholesalers, TX, Brian Tyler), 9) Exxon Mobil ($332,238M, Petroleum Refining, TX, Darren Woods), 10) Cencora ($321,332.8M, Healthcare Wholesalers, PA, Robert Mauch).

Tesla is noted as the third leading motor vehicle manufacturer in the US, growing from $7 billion in revenue in 2015 to $94.8 billion in 2025.

Companies in ranks 101-500 include notable entries such as Netflix (105), Salesforce (114), Visa (119), Starbucks (127), AMD (131), PayPal (139), Mastercard (141), McDonald's (170), Adobe (192), Carvana (220, noted as biggest rank jump at +94), Intuit (231), DoorDash (329), Chipotle (374), Airbnb (357), Vertex Pharmaceuticals (370), Intuitive Surgical (418), Palo Alto Networks (437), and Monster Beverage (469). Sources cited include Fortune 500 US (2026) and 50pros.com.

# Samsung Electronics C-Suite Executive Leadership Team [2026]

[Team DigitalDefynd](https://digitaldefynd.com/IQ/author/digitaldefynds/ "Team DigitalDefynd")

**Samsung Electronics**, a global leader in technology and innovation, continues to shape the future of consumer electronics, semiconductors, and digital infrastructure. From its iconic Galaxy smartphones to industry-leading memory and display technologies, Samsung operates at the intersection of cutting-edge research and large-scale manufacturing. With operations spanning over 70 countries and innovation hubs across the globe, Samsung’s influence is felt in nearly every facet of modern life.

As of 2025, the company’s leadership is undergoing a strategic evolution under the guidance of Vice Chairman and CEO **Jun Young-hyun**, and Executive Chairman **Lee Jae-yong**. With a focus on sustainable growth, artificial intelligence, next-gen chipmaking, and eco-conscious product development, Samsung’s C-suite is navigating an increasingly complex global landscape. Their collective mission: maintain technological dominance while transforming Samsung into a truly future-ready, software-integrated company.

At **DigitalDefynd**, we bring you closer to the world’s most influential executive teams—offering rich profiles, leadership insights, and connections to executive learning programs that mirror the journeys of industry leaders. Join us as we dive into the power players behind Samsung’s global success story.

## Samsung Electronics C-Suite Executive Leadership Team [2026]

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 2 | Lee Jae-yong | Executive Chairman | Oversees long-term vision, governance, and strategic investments. |

| 4 | Tae-Moon Roh | President & Head of Mobile eXperience (MX) | Oversees smartphone, tablet, and wearable product strategy and development. |
| 5 | Jung-Bae Lee | President & Head of Memory Business | Leads DRAM, NAND, and next-gen memory technology development. |
| 6 | Han Jin-man | President & Head of Foundry Business | Manages semiconductor foundry operations and customer relationships. |
| 7 | KS Choi | President & CEO, Samsung Electronics North America | Oversees all business operations across the U.S. and Canada. |
| 8 | Mark Lippert | EVP, North American Public Affairs | Leads U.S. government relations, policy strategy, and public affairs. |
| 9 | Dave Das | EVP, Mobile eXperience Business, Samsung Electronics America | Manages mobile product sales, marketing, and carrier partnerships in the U.S. |
| 10 | Shane Higby | SVP, Consumer Electronics Business, Samsung Electronics America | Oversees home appliances, TV, and audio product strategy in the U.S. |
| 11 | James Fishler | SVP, Home Entertainment & Display Division, Samsung Electronics America | Leads TV and display product innovation and market strategy. |

### 1. Jun Young-hyun – Vice Chairman & CEO

Jun Young-hyun was appointed CEO of Samsung Electronics in 2024, bringing with him extensive experience from his previous leadership roles in Samsung’s memory and battery businesses. Known as a turnaround specialist, Jun previously served as President of Samsung SDI and helped revitalize the company’s energy storage division. As CEO, he now leads Samsung’s global strategy across semiconductors, consumer electronics, and mobile communications. Jun’s leadership is focused on expanding Samsung’s dominance in chip technology, enhancing ESG performance, and accelerating AI-powered innovation across all business units. His appointment marks a significant generational and strategic shift in Samsung’s top leadership structure.

### 2. Lee Jae-yong – Executive Chairman

Lee Jae-yong, also known globally as Jay Y. Lee, is the Executive Chairman of Samsung Electronics and the de facto leader of the Samsung Group. He officially took on the chairman title in 2022 and has since been instrumental in shaping the company’s long-term strategy. Under his vision, Samsung is making bold bets in advanced semiconductors, biotech, and next-generation telecommunications. Lee also oversees major investments in AI, robotics, and sustainability initiatives. A firm believer in global collaboration, he represents Samsung’s interests at the highest levels of government and industry, guiding its evolution from a manufacturing powerhouse to a global innovation leader.

### 3. Hark-Kyu Park – President & Chief Financial Officer (DX Division)

Hark-Kyu Park is the President and CFO of Samsung’s Device eXperience (DX) Division, which encompasses consumer electronics and mobile devices. With decades of experience within Samsung’s financial leadership, Park is responsible for managing the company’s capital structure, overseeing earnings performance, and ensuring financial resilience. He plays a crucial role in aligning Samsung’s fiscal policy with its R&D-heavy innovation model. Under his leadership, Samsung has increased its transparency in investor communications and emphasized sustainable financial practices in pursuit of long-term value creation.

### 4. Tae-Moon Roh – President & Head of Mobile eXperience (MX)

Tae-Moon Roh heads Samsung’s Mobile eXperience business, which includes smartphones, tablets, wearables, and related services. Widely regarded as the architect behind the Galaxy line’s global success, Roh has driven major innovations in foldable devices, mobile AI, and camera systems. Under his leadership, Samsung has maintained its position as the world’s largest smartphone manufacturer while introducing game-changing features like Galaxy AI and Knox Vault for enhanced privacy. Roh’s current focus is on creating more integrated software-hardware ecosystems and expanding premium device market share through design innovation and customer-centric experiences.

### 5. Jung-Bae Lee – President & Head of Memory Business

Jung-Bae Lee leads one of Samsung’s most profitable divisions: the Memory Business. A veteran of Samsung’s semiconductor operations, Lee is responsible for driving advances in DRAM, NAND flash, and emerging memory technologies like MRAM and HBM. Under his direction, Samsung continues to lead the global memory market despite intense competition and cyclical demand fluctuations. Lee’s strategic priorities include scaling next-gen memory for AI and hyperscale data centers, improving power efficiency, and advancing EUV-based production. His leadership is critical to maintaining Samsung’s technological edge in a market that underpins everything from smartphones to cloud infrastructure.

**Related: [CEOs Guide to Geographic Expansion](https://digitaldefynd.com/IQ/the-ceo-guide-to-market-geographic-expansion/?wsiqsamsungexecutives)**

### 6. Han Jin-man – President & Head of Foundry Business

Han Jin-man oversees Samsung’s Foundry Business, a key component of its semiconductor strategy focused on contract manufacturing for global chipmakers. With over 30 years of experience at Samsung, Han has served in various leadership roles within memory and logic divisions. As head of the Foundry unit, he is responsible for advancing Samsung’s cutting-edge process nodes (including 3nm GAA technology), expanding global fab capacity, and securing long-term partnerships with clients such as Qualcomm, NVIDIA, and Tesla. Han’s leadership is instrumental in positioning Samsung as a formidable rival to TSMC in the global foundry race.

### 7. Yong-In Park – President & Head of System LSI Business

Yong-In Park leads Samsung’s System LSI Business, which designs and develops mobile processors (Exynos), image sensors (ISOCELL), modems, and other key semiconductor components. With a background in engineering and product development, Park has been pivotal in Samsung’s push toward advanced SoCs for AI, automotive, and mobile applications. His leadership is focused on developing high-performance, energy-efficient chips and strengthening Samsung’s competitiveness in logic semiconductors. Park also oversees custom silicon solutions for clients, expanding Samsung’s presence in both premium and mid-range processor markets.

### 8. Joo Sun Choi – President & CEO, Samsung Display

Joo Sun Choi is the CEO of Samsung Display, which supplies OLED and QD-OLED screens to Samsung’s own divisions and external clients like Apple, Google, and Sony. A former memory engineer, Choi brings a deep understanding of material science and manufacturing optimization. Under his leadership, Samsung Display has maintained its lead in flexible and foldable screen technologies while expanding applications into automotive and industrial sectors. His focus includes next-gen MicroLED, energy-efficient panels, and expanding OLED production lines in South Korea and abroad.

### 9. Jong-Hee Han – Vice Chairman & CEO, DX Division

Jong-Hee Han serves as CEO of the Device eXperience (DX) Division and Vice Chairman of Samsung Electronics. He oversees consumer electronics including TVs, digital appliances, and mobile devices. Han is credited with revitalizing Samsung’s visual display business, particularly in premium TV segments like Neo QLED and MicroLED. His strategic focus is on connected living, smart homes, and building a seamless ecosystem across devices using SmartThings and AI integration. Under his leadership, Samsung has increased its commitment to sustainability, aiming for carbon neutrality across its DX operations by 2030.

### 10. Sungchul Roh – President & Head of Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology (SAIT)

Sungchul Roh leads the Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology (SAIT), the company’s central R&D hub. SAIT is responsible for foundational research in quantum computing, next-generation materials, biotechnology, and AI. Roh’s leadership helps bridge academic partnerships and early-stage innovation with commercial applications across Samsung’s various business units. He oversees strategic initiatives in carbon capture technologies, neuromorphic computing, and battery breakthroughs. His role ensures Samsung remains at the forefront of long-term technology evolution beyond traditional product cycles.

**Related: [Difference Between CEO and President](https://digitaldefynd.com/IQ/ceo-vs-president/?wsiqsamsungexecutives)**

### 11. Jeong Wook Tak – Executive Vice President, Head of Mobile R&D Office

Jeong Wook Tak leads Samsung’s Mobile R&D Office, a central division responsible for research and development of Galaxy smartphones and connected devices. His team is at the forefront of innovations in camera technology, AI-based user experiences, and foldable display mechanics. Tak plays a pivotal role in integrating One UI features across devices and advancing Samsung’s ambitions in generative AI on mobile platforms. Under his leadership, Samsung continues to push the boundaries of device form factors, software performance, and seamless ecosystem connectivity.

### 12. Inyup Kang – President, Samsung Semiconductor (Formerly System LSI)

Inyup Kang has previously held top roles at Qualcomm before joining Samsung, where he played a crucial part in developing the Exynos chipset line. While currently operating in a more strategic capacity, Kang remains influential in shaping the future of Samsung’s semiconductor portfolio, particularly in high-performance mobile chipsets, 5G modems, and custom solutions for flagship smartphones. His experience bridges both technical excellence and international business development, positioning Samsung to compete globally with other fabless and vertically integrated chipmakers.

### 13. Young Hyun Jun – President, Memory Global Manufacturing

Young Hyun Jun is responsible for Samsung’s global memory chip manufacturing operations. With oversight of fabs in South Korea, China, and the U.S., Jun ensures that production aligns with global demand for DRAM, NAND, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). He also plays a strategic role in capacity planning, supply chain resilience, and advancing sustainable manufacturing practices. A former CEO of Samsung SDI, Jun brings a deep understanding of both semiconductors and energy systems, supporting Samsung’s broader ambitions in AI, automotive, and data center markets.

### 14. Kyehyun Kyung – CEO, Samsung Device Solutions Division (DS)

Kyehyun Kyung leads the Device Solutions Division, which encompasses memory, logic chips, and foundry services—Samsung’s most lucrative and technologically intensive business unit. Formerly the head of Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Kyung now oversees a vast engineering and operations network driving advanced chip design and manufacturing. He focuses on AI-optimized chips, HBM for generative AI models, and diversification of Samsung’s customer base beyond mobile. Kyung is at the center of Samsung’s strategy to integrate semiconductor leadership with long-term platform growth across industries like automotive and healthcare.

### 15. Hee-Chan Roh – Chief Financial Officer, Samsung Device Solutions (DS) Division

Hee-Chan Roh oversees financial strategy, investment planning, and profitability management for Samsung’s Device Solutions Division. With semiconductors representing a large portion of Samsung’s revenue, Roh plays a vital role in aligning capital expenditures with innovation in fabrication technologies and global fab expansion. He ensures financial discipline while supporting aggressive growth in AI chip development, foundry competitiveness, and next-gen memory infrastructure. His oversight is critical in maintaining Samsung’s position as a leader in the high-stakes semiconductor landscape.

**Related: [Vice President Interview Questions](https://digitaldefynd.com/IQ/top-vice-president-interview-questions-and-answers/?wsiqsamsungexecutives)**

### 16. Hee-Jin Choi – Executive Vice President, Corporate Strategy Office

Hee-Jin Choi leads Samsung’s Corporate Strategy Office, which serves as the internal consulting and planning arm responsible for identifying long-term growth opportunities, strategic partnerships, and investment ventures. His team supports cross-divisional synergy, especially across semiconductors, electronics, and emerging platforms like digital health and mobility. Choi plays a central role in Samsung’s M&A strategy, joint ventures, and next-generation market entry initiatives—ensuring the company remains agile in a rapidly shifting technological and geopolitical environment.

### 17. Jiyoung Sohn – Chief Sustainability Officer (CSO)

Jiyoung Sohn spearheads Samsung’s global sustainability initiatives, including carbon neutrality, ethical sourcing, energy efficiency, and circular economy programs. She works closely with engineering, operations, and product teams to ensure ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) goals are embedded in every stage of the company’s value chain. Her leadership is key to Samsung’s pledge to achieve net-zero carbon emissions across its consumer electronics business by 2030 and semiconductor operations by 2050. Sohn also coordinates Samsung’s global sustainability reporting and compliance with evolving international standards.

### 18. Sangho Jo – President & CEO, Samsung Southeast Asia & Oceania

Sangho Jo leads Samsung’s business in the Southeast Asia and Oceania region, managing operations in over 14 countries. He focuses on driving regional growth, local innovation, and expanding Samsung’s consumer and enterprise market presence. With a strong background in sales and marketing, Jo ensures Samsung’s product localization strategies meet diverse consumer needs and regional regulatory requirements. His leadership supports Samsung’s efforts in digital transformation and smart city collaborations across Asia-Pacific economies.

### 19. Grace Yi – EVP, Global Communications

Grace Yi serves as Executive Vice President of Global Communications, leading Samsung’s worldwide brand messaging, media relations, crisis communications, and executive visibility efforts. She plays a vital role in shaping public perception of the company during product launches, geopolitical developments, and strategic announcements. Her focus is on aligning Samsung’s external voice with its innovation narrative while proactively managing brand reputation in a complex, global media landscape. Yi also supports internal communication strategies to foster a unified corporate culture across Samsung’s global workforce.

### 20. Hong Seokwoo – EVP, AI Center & Future Platform Development

Hong Seokwoo leads Samsung’s AI Center, where cutting-edge research meets real-world applications across Samsung’s product ecosystem. His team focuses on large language models (LLMs), computer vision, edge AI, and privacy-preserving machine learning. Seokwoo is also in charge of Samsung’s long-term future platform development—ranging from voice assistants and smart home orchestration to context-aware services. Under his leadership, Samsung has released Galaxy AI features, strengthened SmartThings integration, and initiated foundational AI partnerships to enhance both user experience and device intelligence across form factors.

### Conclusion

Samsung Electronics’ executive leadership team reflects a powerful blend of engineering excellence, global strategy, and future-facing innovation. From semiconductors and mobile experiences to next-gen displays and AI ecosystems, each executive plays a mission-critical role in ensuring Samsung remains one of the world’s most technologically advanced and operationally disciplined enterprises. Leaders like Jun Young-hyun, Tae-Moon Roh, and Jong-Hee Han embody Samsung’s dual commitment to both world-class hardware innovation and sustainable business growth.

The company’s focus on semiconductors, foldables, and connected ecosystems is closely mirrored by its growing investments in AI, foundry competitiveness, and environmental stewardship. It’s this unique blend of scale, speed, and visionary leadership that allows Samsung to set trends rather than follow them—shaping the future of how people live, work, and connect.

# Samsung Electronics names Jay Y. Lee executive chairman

[WATCH LIVE](/live-tv/)

Key Points

* Samsung Electronics' de facto leader Jay Y. Lee was named executive chairman on Thursday, a symbolic move confirming that South Korea's most valuable company will be officially run by the third generation of its founding family.
* The change reflects a role Lee, 54, has held since his father, the late patriarch and Samsung Group chairman Lee Kun-hee, was hospitalized in 2014, analysts said. The elder Lee died in 2020.

In this article

* [SSNHZ](/quotes/SSNHZ)
* [SSNLF](/quotes/SSNLF)

Samsung Electronics' de facto leader Lee Jae-yong during U.S. President Joe Biden's visit on May 20, 2022 in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.

Kim Min-Hee | Pool | Getty Images News | Getty Images

[Samsung Electronics](/quotes/SSNLF/)' de facto leader Jay Y. Lee was named executive chairman on Thursday, a symbolic move confirming that South Korea's most valuable company will be officially run by the third generation of its founding family.

The change reflects a role Lee, 54, has held since his father, the late patriarch and Samsung Group chairman Lee Kun-hee, was hospitalized in 2014, analysts said. The elder Lee died in 2020.

Lee has been vice chairman of Samsung Electronics, the crown jewel of South Korea's biggest business conglomerate, since 2012.

"The Board cited the current uncertain global business environment and the pressing need for stronger accountability and business stability in approving the recommendation," Samsung said in a statement.

The appointment comes as Samsung, the world's biggest maker of memory chips and smartphones, faces mounting business headwinds amid a sharp downturn in worldwide tech demand, caused by soaring inflation, interest rates and a gloomy economic outlook.

![The chip industry is facing an inventory correction that is expected to intensify in 2023: Analyst](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/107086008-16572538911657253888-24177089838-1080pnbcnews.jpg?v=1657253890&w=750&h=422&vtcrop=y)

# Struggle, Try, Make Mistakes, Grow--Chairman Toyoda & President Sato's 2026 New Year's Messages

2026.01.19

![](/en/toyota_news/upload_images/toyota_news_1093_1280_720.jpg) 

In their New Year's greetings to employees, Chairman Akio Toyoda and President Koji Sato spoke of creating an environment where people come together to take on challenges, make mistakes, struggle, try again, and in the end, say "thank you" to one another.

![](/en/toyota_news/upload_images/toyota_news_1093_1280_720.jpg) 

On January 7, Chairman Akio Toyoda and President Koji Sato delivered their New Year’s greetings to employees at the company’s head office in Toyota City, Aichi.

An audience of 1,480 was there to hear the message in person, with others joining in remotely.

How would the company’s leaders go about inventing Toyota’s path forward, together with those present?

We share the messages of Chairman Toyoda and President Sato.

### 2025: A year of gratitude

“As always, the words of Chairman Toyoda and President Sato are sure to ignite a fire in each of our hearts.” Following this introduction by General Administration & Human Resources Group Chief Officer Masahiro Yamamoto, the first to take the stage before the assembled employees was President Sato.

Upon taking the reins in 2023, President Sato acknowledged Chairman Akio’s efforts in restoring “what makes us Toyota,” and pledged that his team would focus on “inheritance and evolution.” How is he approaching his fourth year in office? His address began with a look back over 2025.

**President Sato**

![](/en/toyota_news/upload_images/toyota_news_1093_01.jpg)

Happy New Year to you all.

I am truly delighted to be able to welcome the new year in good health with all of you.

I will do my best to make sure this message speaks to the heart.

Last year, **we began by reflecting on the meaning of the word “arigato” and by resolving to make it a year in which we value smiles and gratitude.**

In December, as an opportunity to express gratitude to our colleagues and stakeholders around the world, we held TOYOTA ARIGATO FEST.2025.

![](/en/toyota_news/upload_images/toyota_news_1093_02.JPG)

“We should never take for granted what we have today.” “The future is ours to create together.”

Guided by Chairman Toyoda’s beliefs, Toyota united globally, sharing countless thank yous and smiles.

![](/en/toyota_news/upload_images/toyota_news_1093_03.JPG)

I was reminded of how grateful I am to have colleagues around the world who demonstrate being “Best in Town” and how important it is to turn our appreciation into action.

So, today, I would like to begin by expressing my gratitude to all of you.

We faced many hardships over the past year.

Even so, to everyone across the company who worked so hard for our customers and for one another, thank you very much.

**“Let’s focus on making and delivering quality cars.”**

With that single goal in mind, I believe that we have all worked together to move forward, step by step.

In regards to certification work, all of us have continued striving to improve individual awareness and work processes so that we can stand at the starting line of consistently carrying out correct work.

With the many changes related to certification and quality, I believe that launching new cars was truly challenging.

We were able to launch new cars because everyone on the front lines kept things moving forward by working urgently until the very end.

Overseas, the competitive environment in many regions grew even more severe.

Even so, we remained committed to putting the customer first and repeatedly pursued better quality and services, from production to sales.

And then in September, our Porto Feliz Plant in Brazil was hit by a tornado. At that time, I truly felt the strength of our global Toyota team.

![](/en/toyota_news/upload_images/toyota_news_1093_04.JPG)

As soon as the news came in, teams in Japan and Indonesia immediately sprang into action to launch backup production. Across regions, they gave it their all to support their colleagues in Brazil.

I would like to thank everyone who rushed to Porto Feliz and worked with our suppliers to support the plant’s recovery and all those who are still working toward the resumption of local production.

The passion and actions of everyone on the front lines, as well as the hard work of our suppliers and dealers, **enabled us to produce 9.94 million vehicles last year and deliver them to our customers.**

I would like to express my sincere gratitude.

![](/en/toyota_news/upload_images/toyota_news_1093_05.JPG)

On the other hand, we still face many challenges.

Although last year’s production downtime was less than the year before, downtime due to quality or equipment issues is on the increase.

Customers continue to experience various inconveniences both in sales and services. For example, in Japan, the reality is that customers still cannot even enter into discussions to purchase the cars they want.

**We must all keep making improvements together to properly make and deliver quality cars.**

With that, President Sato wrapped up his recap of 2025 and began sharing his outlook for the year ahead.

**Akio Toyoda** (豊田 章男, *Toyoda Akio*; born 3 May 1956) is a Japanese business executive who is the [chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman "Chairman") of [Toyota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota "Toyota"). He was previously the company's [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_(corporate_title) "President (corporate title)") and [chief executive officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") (CEO).[[1]](#cite_note-1) Toyoda is a grandson of the founder of Toyota Motors, [Kiichiro Toyoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiichiro_Toyoda "Kiichiro Toyoda"), and a great-grandson of both the industrialist, [Sakichi Toyoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakichi_Toyoda "Sakichi Toyoda"), and the founder of the [Takashimaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takashimaya "Takashimaya") department stores corporation, Shinshichi Iida.

On 1 April 2023, Toyoda stepped down as Toyota president and became chairman of the board.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Toyota's chief branding officer and president of the [Lexus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexus "Lexus") division, [Koji Sato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koji_Sato_(engineer) "Koji Sato (engineer)"), succeeded Toyoda as CEO.

## Early life and education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Akio_Toyoda&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Toyoda is the great-grandson of the [Toyoda Automatic Loom Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Industries "Toyota Industries") founder [Sakichi Toyoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakichi_Toyoda "Sakichi Toyoda"), and grandson of [Toyota Motor Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota "Toyota") founder [Kiichiro Toyoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiichiro_Toyoda "Kiichiro Toyoda"). He was born 3 May 1956, in [Nagoya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagoya "Nagoya"), to [Shoichiro Toyoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoichiro_Toyoda "Shoichiro Toyoda") and Hiroko (née Mitsui). Toyoda's family line have long dominated the upper management of the family businesses since the days his carpenter-farmer great-great-grandfather, Ikichi Toyoda, taught his son fabrication and carpentry. Akio Toyoda was the chief contender for the family business when [Katsuaki Watanabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katsuaki_Watanabe "Katsuaki Watanabe") was reassigned as Vice-Chairman in the wake of the quality control crisis.[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Toyoda completed his undergraduate degree in law at [Keio University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keio_University "Keio University") and was awarded his Masters of Finance at [Babson College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babson_College "Babson College"), Massachusetts.[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) He would join the family business in 1984.

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Akio_Toyoda&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

As grandson of the company's founder, Toyoda joined Toyota's board of directors in 2000.[[8]](#cite_note-8) In 2005, Toyoda was promoted to the position of executive vice president.[[9]](#cite_note-9) In January 2009, it was announced that Toyoda was chosen as the forthcoming president of the company.[[10]](#cite_note-rowley2009-10) On 23 June 2009, he was confirmed as the new president, along with four new executive vice presidents and eight new board members.[[11]](#cite_note-11)[[12]](#cite_note-12) The previous president and CEO [Katsuaki Watanabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katsuaki_Watanabe "Katsuaki Watanabe") became [vice chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_chairman "Vice chairman"), replacing [Katsuhiro Nakagawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katsuhiro_Nakagawa "Katsuhiro Nakagawa").[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In 2012, he was named Autocar's Man of the Year.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

### Master driver "Morizo"

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Akio_Toyoda&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Master driver ")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Morizo_sign.png/250px-Morizo_sign.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Morizo_sign.png)

Akio's signature as a racing driver "Morizo"

As an avid auto racing fan and driver himself, Toyoda has participated in several auto races under the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") **Morizo Kinoshita**.[[15]](#cite_note-15) At the [2009 24 Hours of Nürburgring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_24_Hours_of_Nürburgring "2009 24 Hours of Nürburgring"), he finished 81st overall and third in class in a [Lexus IS F](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexus_IS_F "Lexus IS F"), and 87th overall and fourth in class with a [Lexus LF-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexus_LF-A "Lexus LF-A").[[16]](#cite_note-adac-results-2009-16)[[17]](#cite_note-17) At the [2014 24 Hours of Nürburgring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_24_Hours_of_Nürburgring "2014 24 Hours of Nürburgring"), he finished 13th overall and first in class with a Lexus LF-A.[[18]](#cite_note-18) At the [2019 24 Hours of Nürburgring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_24_Hours_of_Nürburgring "2019 24 Hours of Nürburgring"), he finished 40th overall and third in class with a [Toyota GR Supra GT4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_GR_Supra_GT4 "Toyota GR Supra GT4").

In 2016, Toyota approved the project that would result in the [GR Yaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GR_Yaris "GR Yaris"); during the development of that car, Toyoda (as Morizo) served as a test driver. Morizo crashed the first test car during a mid-winter test drive at a [Hokkaido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hokkaido "Hokkaido") track; after exiting the car on his own, he remarked that he did not "like the feel of it". As Morizo, Toyoda continued to drive development prototypes, and since the car's release, has campaigned the car in races.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

### Toyota global recalls and Congressional Statement

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Akio_Toyoda&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Toyota global recalls and Congressional Statement")]

Main article: [2009–2010 Toyota vehicle recalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009–2010_Toyota_vehicle_recalls "2009–2010 Toyota vehicle recalls")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Toyota_Yaris_WRC_2016-09-29_001.jpg/250px-Toyota_Yaris_WRC_2016-09-29_001.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Toyota_Yaris_WRC_2016-09-29_001.jpg)

The brand new [Toyota Yaris World Rally Car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Yaris_WRC "Toyota Yaris WRC"), set to compete in the [2017 WRC season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Rally_Championship "2017 World Rally Championship"), at the 2016 Paris Motor Show. On the left is Akio Toyoda, CEO of Toyota Motor Corporation, next to four time World Rally Drivers' Champion [Tommi Mäkinen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommi_Mäkinen "Tommi Mäkinen")

In the wake of massive global recalls ballooning to 8.5 million vehicles, Toyoda was invited to testify before the [U.S. Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") on 17 February 2010,[[20]](#cite_note-20) which he accepted. A week later, he issued a prepared statement to the Congress.[[21]](#cite_note-21) He focused on three key issues: Toyota's basic philosophy regarding quality control, the cause of the recalls, and "how we will manage quality control going forward".[[22]](#cite_note-22) On 24 February 2010, accompanied by president and COO of Toyota Motor North America, Yoshimi Inaba, Toyoda testified before the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives")' Oversight and Government Reform Committee. As the scion of a family known for their contributions to automated manufacturing, Toyoda was personally affected by the quality control crises.[[23]](#cite_note-23) In his comments he is quoted as being "deeply sorry" and highlighted the relations between Toyota vehicles in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and Americans for fifty years.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

### Direction of Toyota

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Akio_Toyoda&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Direction of Toyota")]

At a press event held on 14 December 2021, Toyota unveiled [multiple concept cars with battery electric drivetrains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_concept_vehicles_(2020–2029)#Battery_electric_vehicles_(2021) "Toyota concept vehicles (2020–2029)"), a sign of faith in the future of the technology.[[25]](#cite_note-25) In a later interview, he said "“People are finally seeing reality."[[26]](#cite_note-26) *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* assessed his bet on hybrid vehicles is how the company achieved its 2023 profit of 4.9 trillion yen—the highest in the company's history.[[27]](#cite_note-27)[[28]](#cite_note-:0-28) Also in 2023, Toyoda stepped down from his role as CEO to become chairman.[[28]](#cite_note-:0-28)

In November 2025, Toyoda was seen at the [Fuji Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuji_Speedway "Fuji Speedway") wearing a "[Make America Great Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_America_Great_Again "Make America Great Again")" hat and a shirt with the pictures of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance").[[29]](#cite_note-akiotrump-29)

args.summary:
Akio Toyoda (豊田 章男), born 3 May 1956 in Nagoya, Japan, is a Japanese business executive who currently serves as Chairman of Toyota. He previously served as the company's President and CEO from 2009 to 2023. Toyoda is the grandson of Toyota Motors founder Kiichiro Toyoda and great-grandson of both industrialist Sakichi Toyoda and Takashimaya department stores founder Shinshichi Iida.

EDUCATION & EARLY CAREER: Toyoda earned his undergraduate degree in law at Keio University and a Masters of Finance at Babson College in Massachusetts. He joined the family business in 1984, joined Toyota's board of directors in 2000, and was promoted to executive vice president in 2005. In January 2009 he was announced as the next president, and was confirmed on 23 June 2009, succeeding Katsuaki Watanabe who became vice chairman.

MASTER DRIVER "MORIZO": As an avid racing driver, Toyoda races under the pseudonym "Morizo Kinoshita." Notable results include finishing 81st overall and third in class at the 2009 24 Hours of Nürburgring in a Lexus IS F, 13th overall and first in class at the 2014 race in a Lexus LF-A, and 40th overall at the 2019 race in a Toyota GR Supra GT4. In 2016, Toyota approved the GR Yaris project, during which Toyoda (as Morizo) served as a test driver; he crashed the first test car during a mid-winter test in Hokkaido but continued developing prototypes and campaigned the car in races.

2009-2010 RECALLS: Following global recalls ballooning to 8.5 million vehicles, Toyoda was invited to testify before the U.S. Congress on 17 February 2010. On 24 February 2010, he testified before the House of Representatives' Oversight and Government Reform Committee, where he focused on Toyota's quality control philosophy, the cause of the recalls, and future quality management. He was quoted as being "deeply sorry" for the crisis.

RECENT DEVELOPMENTS: At a December 2021 press event, Toyota unveiled multiple battery electric concept cars, signaling faith in EV technology; Toyoda commented "People are finally seeing reality." The New York Times credited his bet on hybrid vehicles for Toyota's record 2023 profit of 4.9 trillion yen. On 1 April 2023, Toyoda stepped down as CEO to become chairman, succeeded by Koji Sato (former Lexus division president and chief branding officer). In November 2025, Toyoda was seen at Fuji Speedway wearing a "Make America Great Again" hat and a shirt featuring Donald Trump and JD Vance. He was named Autocar's Man of the Year in 2012.

# Akio Toyoda Steps Aside from Toyota’s CEO Role

The Toyota boss moves on to chairman of the board and is replaced by Koji Sato.

By [Wesley Wren](/author/224138/wesley-wren/ "Wesley Wren")

Toyota

* **Toyota CEO and President Akio Toyoda steps out from the role that he held since 2009.**
* **Koji Sato takes the helm at Toyota but moves up from his spot as president of Lexus and Gazoo Racing.**
* **Toyoda’s edict of “no more boring cars’’ worked wonders for the automaker’s product development.**

---

The man behind “[no more boring cars](https://www.autoweek.com/news/a1813761/toyota-president-declares-no-more-boring-cars/)” is stepping aside from his role as president and CEO of [Toyota](https://www.autoweek.com/toyota) and focusing his time as the chairman of the board of directors. Filling his role in Toyota’s corporate hierarchy is the current [Lexus](https://www.autoweek.com/lexus) and Gazoo Racing boss Koji Sato.

Toyoda joined Toyota in 1984 and later ascended to his spot on the board of directors. Along the way, he moved up to regional management and directorial roles before reaching the top of the executive ladder in 2009, when he was named president of the company.

Toyoda’s replacement followed a slightly different path. Sato joined the company as an engineer in 1992. Though, like Toyoda, Koji worked his way up through Toyota’s ranks as an engineer, and in 2017 he became executive general manager in charge of the Lexus luxury brand. After another bump to the Lexus vice presidency, Koji became the president of Lexus and Gazoo Racing in 2020.

While announced today, this shakeup won’t take effect until April of this year, and it seems likely that Toyoda’s product directive will live on with the Gazoo Racing boss at the helm. TOYOTA CITY, Japan, June 17 (Reuters) - Toyota Motor [(7203.T), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/7203.T) shareholders re-elected Akio ​Toyoda as chairman and backed new ‌CEO Kenta Kon as a board member on Tuesday, endorsing the automaker's leadership ​at the first annual meeting ​held during Kon's tenure.

Shareholders also approved ⁠the re-election of four other ​directors.

Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Kon said the company would continue to invest steadily in growth areas such as AI, robotics, and its multi-pathway strategy utilizing various powertrains without "hitting the brakes suddenly." Kon, who previously worked as Toyoda's secretary and became CEO in April, formally took his seat on the board. Former CEO Koji Sato, now vice chairman, stepped down from the board. The article was reported by Maki Shiraki and published under Reuters' Legal/Transactional section with corporate governance as a suggested topic.
args.key_excerpts: Toyota shareholders re-elected Akio Toyoda as chairman and backed new CEO Kenta Kon as a board member on Tuesday, endorsing the automaker's leadership at the first annual meeting held during Kon's tenure.

industry](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/news/car-industry/) # Akio Toyoda, president and CEO of Toyota, has retired from his positions 3 years ago [![](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Zak-160x160-1.jpg) Zak Adkins Contributor](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/about-us/zak/) The former president of Toyota will still be involved with the company, however, taking on the role of chairman of the board of directors --- Akio Toyoda, the president and chief executive officer of [Toyota Motor Corporation](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/toyota/), has stepped down from his roles, becoming the chairman of the board of directors from April 1 onwards. Toyoda became president of the company back in 2009, making his time in the role a 14 year tenure. Akio Toyoda’s replacement will be Koji Sato, the current president of [Lexus](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/lexus/) and Gazoo Racing, as well as Toyota’s chief operating officer. Sato will not continue his role as chief branding officer of Toyota. ![2023 Akio Toyoda with the AE86 electric car]() Akio Toyoda will step down from president duties on April 1 While Akio Toyoda’s reign was a long one, the biggest tenure was in fact Eiji Toyoda who was president from 1967 to 1982, and chairman from 1982 to 1994. Eiji died in 2013 at the age of 100. ## **Akio Toyoda is not just a corporate figure, but a racing fan, too** As the great-grandson of industrialist Sakichi Toyoda and the grandson of Toyota Motors founder Kiichiro Toyoda, Akio was bound to become part of the family business. ![2023 Akio Toyoda with GR presentation]() Akio Toyoda is a massive car racing enthusiast However, during his 14 year tenure, Akio Toyoda spent a lot of time behind the wheel rather than sitting behind a desk. As an avid fan of autosports and racing, Toyoda helped to promote models in the Toyota family, including the Lexus IS-F and LFA sports cars. Toyoda actually gave himself an on-track persona, ‘Morizo’, a name that can now be found gracing a variant of the new [GR Corolla](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/news/future-cars/toyota-gr-corolla-2023-australian-release-date-confirmed-with-500-units-locked-in/). ![2022 Toyota EV range lineup]() The 2022 Toyota EV range lineup presented by Akio Toyoda Akio Toyoda was also responsible for overseeing what could become the [GR Yaris](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/news/future-cars/toyota-gr-yaris-2022-orders-resume-for-australia-with-160-cars-on-their-way/) all-wheel-drive hatchback, the first GR-branded product to be launched by Toyota’s Gazoo Racing arm. Toyoda was also a pivotal spokesperson and advocate for [Toyota’s battery-electric vehicle plan](https://www.chasingcars.com.au/news/car-industry/toyota-to-reportedly-revise-ev-strategy-and-accelerate-electric-model-development/) that was announced to the public in 2022. As the core of the EV strategy, Toyota plans to inject over $70 billion into electrification – both BEV and hybridisation – over a nine-year period, lagging somewhat behind other major automakers on the fully electric front. ## Chasing more Toyota? args.summary:
Akio Toyoda, president and CEO of Toyota Motor Corporation, has stepped down from his roles, effective April 1, and will become chairman of the board of directors. Toyoda held the presidency for 14 years, having taken the role in 2009. His replacement is Koji Sato, who was president of Lexus and Gazoo Racing, as well as Toyota's chief operating officer. Sato will not continue as Toyota's chief branding officer.

The article highlights that Toyoda is the great-grandson of industrialist Sakichi Toyoda and grandson of Toyota Motors founder Kiichiro Toyoda. During his tenure, he was known as an avid racing enthusiast who used the on-track persona 'Morizo' (now featured on a GR Corolla variant), helped promote models including the Lexus IS-F and LFA sports cars, oversaw the GR Yaris (the first GR-branded product from Gazoo Racing), and was a pivotal spokesperson for Toyota's battery-electric vehicle plan announced in 2022. As part of that EV strategy, Toyota plans to invest over $70 billion into electrification (both BEV and hybridisation) over a nine-year period.

The article notes that the longest presidential tenure at Toyota was Eiji Toyoda, who served as president from 1967 to 1982 and chairman from 1982 to 1994, dying in 2013 at age 100.
args.key_excerpts: "Akio Toyoda, the president and chief executive officer of Toyota Motor Corporation, has stepped down from his roles, becoming the chairman of the board of directors from April 1 onwards." "Akio Toyoda's replacement will be Koji Sato, the current president of Lexus and Gazoo Racing, as well as Toyota's chief operating officer." "As the core of the EV strategy, Toyota plans to inject over $70 billion into electrification – both BEV and hybridisation – over a nine-year period, lagging somewhat behind other major automakers on the fully electric front." "Toyoda actually gave himself an on-track persona, 'Morizo', a name that can now be found gracing a variant of the new GR Corolla."

# Volkswagen AG’s Supervisory Board appoints Oliver Blume as CEO until the end of 2030

[Download](/en/press-releases/volkswagen-ags-supervisory-board-appoints-oliver-blume-as-ceo-until-the-end-of-2030-19896/download?disposition=attachment "Download")

[+49 (0) 152 0166 0713](tel:+49-152-0166-0713)   [michael.brendel@volkswagen.de](mailto:michael.brendel@volkswagen.de)

![Abstract wave shape in dark blue tones.](https://uploads.vw-mms.de/system/production/images/cws/081/255/images/58535d186d993ddf7197e56d10ee14bad022ed8d/B2024CW00084_web_1600.jpg?1739540401)

* Dual role in Volkswagen Group and Porsche AG will cease as of 1 January 2026

Wolfsburg. Oliver Blume will remain at the helm of the Volkswagen Group in the coming years. The Supervisory Board of Volkswagen Aktiengesellschaft resolved on Friday to conclude a new agreement with Mr. Blume for a term of five years, starting on 1 January 2026. This means Mr. Blume will continue as Volkswagen AG’s CEO until the end of 2030. Mr. Blume has held this post since 1 September 2022.

“In the last three years, Oliver Blume has impressively demonstrated his ability to advance and develop the Volkswagen Group’s strategy and business operations in a challenging environment. The Supervisory Board is confident that, with Mr. Blume on board, it will continue to successfully tackle the tasks ahead together with the Board of Management team,” said the Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Hans Dieter Pötsch.

The Supervisory Board resolved on a Friday to conclude a new five-year agreement with Blume, effective from 1 January 2026 through the end of 2030. # Dr. Michael Leiters will become CEO of Porsche AG on 1 January 2026

The Supervisory Board of Porsche AG has appointed Dr. Michael Leiters as CEO of Porsche AG, effective as of 1 January 2026. Dr. Oliver Blume, who has led Porsche AG as CEO for ten years, will continue to serve as CEO of Volkswagen Group.

Dr. Wolfgang Porsche, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Porsche AG: “As CEO of Porsche AG, Dr. Oliver Blume has taken great responsibility in challenging times and successfully managed the company. The Supervisory Board of Porsche AG would like to thank Dr. Blume for his strong commitment. We look forward to continuing to work closely and trustingly with him as CEO of Volkswagen Group.”

As CEO of Porsche AG, Oliver Blume paved the way for record financial years, the IPO of Porsche AG, and the expansion into further international markets, as well as historic motorsport successes. He prepared the generational change in the Porsche Executive Board in a long-term and strategic manner.

Dr. Oliver Blume, Chairman of the Board of Management of Volkswagen Group and Porsche AG: "After ten years of responsibility for Porsche AG, I have decided to hand over my duties to my successor at the end of the year in the interests of Volkswagen Group. I have had the privilege of developing a great company with a fantastic team. I am delighted that Michael Leiters, an experienced professional in the sports car business, is taking on this role. He and the new management team have my full confidence. I wish them every success.”

With regards to the current situation of the company, Oliver Blume says: "Massive changes in what are by far Porsche's largest single markets, the USA and China, have placed new demands on our business model. That is why we have structurally realigned the company this year and comprehensively expanded our product strategy. With full flexibility in drivetrain and an improved cost structure, Porsche is now robustly positioned for the future. In my role for Volkswagen Group, I will closely accompany and support the further development of Porsche."

![Oliver Blume, Chairman of the Executive Board of Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG, 911 GT3, Annual Press Conference, 2021, Porsche AG](/.imaging/mte/porsche-templating-theme/image_690x388/dam/pnr/2021/Company/annual-press-conference-2020/gallery/_F1A0231.jpg/jcr:content/_F1A0231.jpg)

Dr. Oliver Blume’s successor will be Dr. Michael Leiters. Leiters has been CEO of McLaren Automotive since July 2022, having previously served as CTO for Ferrari for more than eight years. Leiters is no stranger to Porsche AG. Before taking up his position at Ferrari, he held positions at Porsche for more than 13 years, most recently with responsibility for the Porsche Macan and Porsche Cayenne series.

![Dr. Michael Leiters, 2025, Porsche AG](https://porschepictures.flowcenter.de/pmdb/thumbnail.cgi?id=326265&w=1035&h=582&crop=1&public=1&cs=4f7eee9d5e80aa17)

“Dr. Michael Leiters has decades of experience in the automotive industry. His leadership style and in-depth expertise are ideal prerequisites for successfully chairing the Executive Board of Porsche AG. He and the entire Executive Board team at Porsche AG enjoy the confidence of the Supervisory Board in overcoming the current challenges,” says Dr. Wolfgang Porsche.

# VW: Blume to step down from Porsche post in 2026, Leiters to take over

**Oliver Blume's dual role as head of Volkswagen and Porsche has been the subject of criticism for some time, especially since things have not been running smoothly at Porsche. Porsche has now confirmed that talks are underway with a successor to Blume as Porsche CEO – Michael Leiters.**

![Oliver blume michael leiters collage](https://www.electrive.com/media/2025/10/oliver-blume-michael-leiters-collage-2025-1400x933.jpg)

Initially, the German publications *Der Spiegel* and *Bild* reported, citing insider sources, that the manager would step down as CEO of Porsche in 2026. The supervisory board had already agreed on a successor, though the name was not mentioned in the reports. The individual was said to be technically proficient and experienced within the Volkswagen Group.

Shortly after, Porsche confirmed that Michael Leiters could be the next CEO. Negotiations with him are set to begin, the company announced on Friday. “Today, the Executive Committee of the Supervisory Board of Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche Aktiengesellschaft (“Porsche”) authorized the Chairman of the Supervisory Board to enter into discussions with Dr. Oliver Blume, Chairman of the Executive Board, in relation to a mutually agreed early termination of his appointment as member of the Executive Board of Porsche,” the statement said. “Dr. Michael Leiters, former Chief Executive Officer of McLaren Automotive Limited, is available as a potential successor as Chairman of the Executive Board. Negotiations with Dr. Leiters will be initiated. Dr. Blume would continue to serve as the Chairman of the Executive Board of Volkswagen AG.”

Leters worked for Porsche from 2000 to 2013, serving as assistant to the CEO, project manager for the Cayenne, and most recently as product line director. From 2014, he spent over eight years at Ferrari as CTO, driving the development of sports cars – including the upcoming electric Ferrari. In mid-2022, he became CEO at McLaren Automotive but left the British manufacturer in April this year. McLaren had fallen into crisis during the coronavirus pandemic, even laying off 1,000 employees at one point, but under Leiters, the company stabilised.

Reports of the succession circulated [in the summer](https://www.electrive.com/2025/08/27/will-porsche-ceo-blume-step-down-to-focus-on-volkswagen-role/), suggesting an appointment in autumn, which now appears to be confirmed. The planned transition at the start of 2026 aligns with these reports. Blume has led Porsche for ten years and has also headed the VW Group since 2022, taking over from Herbert Diess in [September 2022](https://www.electrive.com/2022/09/01/oliver-blume-suceeds-herbert-diess-as-volkswagen-ceo/). Blume has stated several times that the dual role is “not intended to last forever,” although he recently defended it, saying the arrangement had been deliberately chosen and brought significant advantages during the group’s restructuring.

With the impending leadership change, the major restructuring of the Porsche Executive Board would continue and possibly come to an end for the time being. [In February](https://www.electrive.com/2025/02/26/porsche-appoints-new-chief-financial-officer-and-chief-sales-officer/), the German carmaker parted ways with Chief Financial Officer Lutz Meschke and Chief Sales Officer Detlev von Platen. Jochen Breckner assumed responsibility for finance and IT, while Matthias Becker took over sales and marketing. Both were internal succession solutions. With Leiters, a manager who has not been with Porsche or the VW Group for over a decade, is now likely to take the reins in Zuffenhausen.

This dual responsibility has been a point of contention among stakeholders since Porsche became a separately listed entity in 2022. Investors have been vocal about their governance concerns, advocating for Blume to step down from one of his roles. Since taking over Porsche’s leadership in 2015 and subsequently Volkswagen in 2022, Blume’s dual role has been scrutinised, especially as both companies face obstacles such as US tariffs, declining profits, and reduced sales in China.

The Supervisory Board of Volkswagen Aktiengesellschaft resolved on Friday to conclude a new agreement with Blume for a term of five years, starting on 1 January 2026. This means Blume will continue as Volkswagen AG’s CEO until the end of 2030.

 “In the last three years, Oliver Blume has impressively demonstrated his ability to advance and develop the Volkswagen Group’s strategy and business operations in a challenging environment. The Supervisory Board is confident that, with Mr. Blume on board, it will continue to successfully tackle the tasks ahead together with the Board of Management team,” said the Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Hans Dieter Pötsch.

**New Porsche CEO**

At the same time as the Blume announcement, the Supervisory Board of Porsche AG has appointed Dr. Michael Leiters as CEO of Porsche AG, also effective as of January 1, 2026.

Dr. Michael Leiters has been CEO of McLaren Automotive from July 2022 until April 2025, having previously served as CTO for Ferrari for more than eight years. Before taking up his position at Ferrari, he held positions at Porsche for more than 13 years, most recently with responsibility for the Porsche Macan and Porsche Cayenne series.

Dr. Wolfgang Porsche, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Porsche AG, said: “As CEO of Porsche AG, Dr. Oliver Blume has taken great responsibility in challenging times and successfully managed the company. The Supervisory Board of Porsche AG would like to thank Dr. Blume for his strong commitment. We look forward to continuing to work closely and trustingly with him as CEO of Volkswagen Group.”

With regards to the current situation of Porsche, Oliver Blume said: “Massive changes in what are by far Porsche’s largest single markets, the USA and China, have placed new demands on our business model. That is why we have structurally realigned the company this year and comprehensively expanded our product strategy. With full flexibility in drivetrain and an improved cost structure, Porsche is now robustly positioned for the future. In my role for Volkswagen Group, I will closely accompany and support the further development of Porsche.”

Volkswagen Group has resolved its CEO "dual role" problem by deciding that CEO Oliver Blume will, from January 1, 2026, focus solely on his role as CEO of Volkswagen AG and step down as CEO of Porsche AG. The dual responsibility had been a point of contention among stakeholders since Porsche became a separately listed entity in 2022, with investors voicing governance concerns. Both companies have faced obstacles including US tariffs, declining profits, and reduced sales in China.

The Supervisory Board of Volkswagen AG resolved on Friday to sign a new five-year agreement with Blume starting January 1, 2026, extending his tenure as Volkswagen AG's CEO until the end of 2030.

At the same time, Porsche AG's Supervisory Board appointed Dr. Michael Leiters as the new CEO of Porsche AG, also effective January 1, 2026. Leiters was CEO of McLaren Automotive from July 2022 until April 2025, previously served as CTO for Ferrari for over eight years, and held positions at Porsche for more than 13 years (most recently overseeing the Porsche Macan and Cayenne series).

Hans Dieter Pötsch, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Volkswagen, praised Blume's performance over the past three years in advancing the Group's strategy in a challenging environment. Dr. Wolfgang Porsche, Chairman of Porsche AG's Supervisory Board, thanked Blume for his commitment and looked forward to continued collaboration. Blume noted that massive changes in Porsche's largest markets (USA and China) have driven a structural realignment and expanded product strategy, with full flexibility in drivetrain and improved cost structure positioning Porsche for the future.
args.key_excerpts: "In the last three years, Oliver Blume has impressively demonstrated his ability to advance and develop the Volkswagen Group's strategy and business operations in a challenging environment. The Supervisory Board is confident that, with Mr. Blume on board, it will continue to successfully tackle the tasks ahead together with the Board of Management team," said Hans Dieter Pötsch, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Volkswagen.

**Sten Ola Källenius** (born 11 June 1969)[[1]](#cite_note-:2-1) is a Swedish-German business executive. He serves as the Chairman of the Board of Management and [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Executive_Officer "Chief Executive Officer") of the [Mercedes-Benz Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group "Mercedes-Benz Group"). Källenius was the first non-German to hold both positions prior to obtaining German citizenship.

## Early life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ola_K%C3%A4llenius&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Källenius was born in [Västervik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Västervik "Västervik"), by the age of one the family moved to [Malmö](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malmö "Malmö"), later living in various places throughout Sweden, Germany, and Switzerland. The family spent summers at [Scania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scania "Scania")'s countryside, where his father's family owned a [summer house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_house#In_the_Nordic_countries "Summer house") next to his maternal grandparent's farm. When Ola was 16, the family moved to Stockholm, living across the road from the [Stockholm School of Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_School_of_Economics "Stockholm School of Economics"). Before starting university, he completed his military service at [Tolkskolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tolkskolan?action=edit&redlink=1 "Tolkskolan (page does not exist)") – the Swedish Armed Forces Interpreter School – which he called 'the most intense 15 months of my life'.[[2]](#cite_note-:3-2)

## Education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ola_K%C3%A4llenius&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Education")]

Originally planning to follow his older brother's footsteps in studying at [KTH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KTH_Royal_Institute_of_Technology "KTH Royal Institute of Technology"), Källenius instead graduated from [Stockholm School of Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_School_of_Economics "Stockholm School of Economics") with a master's degree, including an [exchange semester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_exchange_program "Student exchange program") at [University of St. Gallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_St._Gallen "University of St. Gallen"). He also earned a[CEMS Master in International Management (CEMS MIM)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Alliance_in_Management_Education "Global Alliance in Management Education") and Finance and Accounting.[[2]](#cite_note-:3-2)[[3]](#cite_note-:0-3)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ola_K%C3%A4llenius&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Career")]

Källenius began his career in 1993 at the former Daimler-Benz AG, where he worked in the "International Junior Research Group". His first major project was in the finance team for setting up production of the [Mercedes M-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes_M-class "Mercedes M-class") at a [new Alabama plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_U.S._International "Mercedes-Benz U.S. International").[[2]](#cite_note-:3-2) After other early assignments in management control, he assumed various management positions within Daimler AG, including head of the "Powertrain" purchasing department of the Mercedes-Benz Cars group.

In 2003, he became director of operations at [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Automotive "McLaren Automotive"). Two years later he became managing director of Mercedes-Benz High Performance Engines Formula 1 engine factory.[[1]](#cite_note-:2-1)

He moved back to the US in 2009, where he would head the US division of Mercedes-Benz. In 2010, he returned to Germany, taking over the chairmanship of the management of [Mercedes-AMG GmbH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-AMG "Mercedes-AMG"), which he relinquished to [Tobias Moers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobias_Moers "Tobias Moers") on 1 October 2013.[[4]](#cite_note-4) Since October 2013, he has been a member of the executive board of Mercedes-Benz Cars and was responsible for marketing and sales.[[1]](#cite_note-:2-1)

He was appointed to the board of management of Daimler AG on 1 January 2015.[[3]](#cite_note-:0-3) On 1 January 2017, he took over the management of the "Group Research and Mercedes-Benz Cars Development" division as a member of the executive board.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He became the successor to [Thomas Weber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Weber_(engineer) "Thomas Weber (engineer)"), who had been responsible for this division since 2004.[[6]](#cite_note-6) [Britta Seeger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britta_Seeger "Britta Seeger") succeeded Källenius as board member for Mercedes-Benz Cars Sales.

Källenius succeeded [Dieter Zetsche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dieter_Zetsche "Dieter Zetsche") as the Chairman of the Board of Management of Mercedes-Benz Group AG in May 2019.[[7]](#cite_note-7) In 2023, Mercedes-Benz extended his contract until mid-2029.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/K%C3%A4llenius_China_2024.jpg/250px-K%C3%A4llenius_China_2024.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Källenius_China_2024.jpg)

Källenius (left) visit [Chongqing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chongqing "Chongqing"), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), 2024

In his capacity as CEO, Källenius accompanied [Chancellor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor_of_Germany "Chancellor of Germany") [Olaf Scholz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olaf_Scholz "Olaf Scholz") on a state visit to China in 2024.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

## Positions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ola_K%C3%A4llenius&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Positions")]

Källenius is a strong advocate of [plug-in hybrids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plug-in_hybrid "Plug-in hybrid") and [electric vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_vehicle "Electric vehicle") within Daimler. He has pushed the new electric model initiative, product and technology brand EQ, along with a $12 billion investment into Mercedes-Benz's new line of battery-powered vehicles.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11) Within the initiative he has proposed and advocated for a series of ten new and purely electric Mercedes-Benz models to be launched by 2022.[[12]](#cite_note-12) The first car was the [Mercedes-Benz EQC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_EQC "Mercedes-Benz EQC") SUV, launched in the first half of 2019.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-10)

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ola_K%C3%A4llenius&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Källenius is married to Sabine;[[2]](#cite_note-:3-2) the couple have three sons. His wife is an environmental activist (part of the Green Globe Organisation) who according to Källenius requested that he transition the entire Mercedes-Benz range, including the flagship [G-Wagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_G-Class "Mercedes-Benz G-Class"), to fully plug-in electric vehicles.[[13]](#cite_note-13) In July 2023 Källenius obtained German citizenship.[[14]](#cite_note-14) He is fluent in English, Swedish and German.[[2]](#cite_note-:3-2)

During his studies at the Stockholm School of Economics, he was a member of the [Danderyd Mean Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_Mean_Machines "Stockholm Mean Machines") [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") team.[[2]](#cite_note-:3-2)

args.summary:
Ola Källenius (born Sten Ola Källenius, 11 June 1969, in Västervik, Sweden) is a Swedish-German business executive who serves as the Chairman of the Board of Management and CEO of the Mercedes-Benz Group. He was the first non-German to hold both positions prior to obtaining German citizenship.

EARLY LIFE & EDUCATION: Born in Västervik, Sweden, his family moved to Malmö when he was one, and later lived throughout Sweden, Germany, and Switzerland. At 16, his family moved to Stockholm. He completed military service at the Swedish Armed Forces Interpreter School (Tolkskolan) before university. He graduated from the Stockholm School of Economics with a master's degree (including an exchange semester at University of St. Gallen) and earned a CEMS Master in International Management and Finance and Accounting.

CAREER: He began his career in 1993 at Daimler-Benz AG, working on the finance team for setting up production of the Mercedes M-class at a new Alabama plant. In 2003, he became director of operations at McLaren; in 2005, he became managing director of Mercedes-Benz High Performance Engines (F1 engine factory). He moved back to the US in 2009 to head Mercedes-Benz's US division, returned to Germany in 2010 to chair Mercedes-AMG GmbH (relinquished to Tobias Moers on 1 October 2013). He joined the executive board of Mercedes-Benz Cars in October 2013 (marketing and sales), was appointed to the Daimler AG board of management on 1 January 2015, and took over Group Research and Mercedes-Benz Cars Development on 1 January 2017. He succeeded Dieter Zetsche as Chairman of the Board of Management in May 2019. In 2023, Mercedes-Benz extended his contract until mid-2029. As CEO, he accompanied Chancellor Olaf Scholz on a state visit to China in 2024.

POSITIONS: Källenius is a strong advocate of plug-in hybrids and electric vehicles. He pushed the EQ electric model initiative and a $12 billion investment into battery-powered vehicles, advocating for ten new purely electric models by 2022. The first was the Mercedes-Benz EQC SUV, launched in the first half of 2019.

PERSONAL LIFE: He is married to Sabine, an environmental activist with the Green Globe Organisation, who urged him to transition the entire Mercedes-Benz range (including the G-Wagon) to fully plug-in electric vehicles. They have three sons. He obtained German citizenship in July 2023. He is fluent in English, Swedish, and German. During his studies he was a member of the Danderyd Mean Machines American football team.
args.key_excerpts: "Källenius was the first non-German to hold both positions prior to obtaining German citizenship."
