UnitedHealth Group’s (NYSE: UNH) Chairman and President Stephen J. Hemsley will become the insurance and health care giant’s CEO, effective immediately.

Previous CEO Andrew Witty stepped down on Tuesday for personal reasons, according to a statement from UnitedHealth Group. The company is the third largest hospice provider in the nation, primarily through its subsidiary Optum, according to [research](https://hospicenews.com/flagship-report/hospicenews50/) by Hospice News. This was achieved largely through the company’s 2023 acquisition of LHC Group for $5.4 billion.

“We are grateful for Andrew’s stewardship of UnitedHealth Group, especially during some of the most challenging times any company has ever faced,” Hemsley said in a statement. “The Board and I have greatly valued his leadership and compassion as chief executive and as a director and wish him and his family the best.”

Advertisement

This will be Hemsley’s second stint as UnitedHealth Group’s CEO. He previously served in the role from 2006 to 2017. He will remain chairman of the company’s board of directors, and Witty will become a senior advisor to Hemsley.

The move follows l[eadership changes](https://hospicenews.com/2025/05/01/new-ceo-at-optum-as-unitedhealth-group-revamps-c-suite/) at Optum on May 1, in which Dr. Patrick Conway became the subsidiary’s CEO.

The transition follows a [rough quarter](https://hospicenews.com/2025/04/17/optum-bolsters-unitedhealth-group-during-rough-first-quarter/) for UnitedHealth Group. Government funding reductions, transitions to a new Medicare Advantage risk adjustment model and heightened care activity led UnitedHealth Group to reduce its 2025 performance outlook to $24.65 to $25.15 earnings per share, down from a previously anticipated $26 to $26.50. The company has now suspended its 2025 outlook.

Advertisement

Optum’s $3.3 billion purchase of Amedisys (Nasdaq: AMED) is currently pending a [court decision](https://hospicenews.com/2025/04/14/dojs-lawsuit-against-amedisys-unitedhealth-group-set-for-mediation/) following antitrust concerns raised by the U.S. Department of Justice.

Hemsley has pledged that the company will “return to growth” in 2026, according to the company’s statement.

“UnitedHealth Group has tremendous opportunities to grow as we continue to help improve health care and to perform to our potential — and, in so doing, return to our long-term growth objective of 13 to 16%,” Hemsley said.

Stephen J. Hemsley, Chairman and President of UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH), has become the company's CEO effective immediately, replacing Andrew Witty who stepped down on Tuesday, May 13, 2025, for personal reasons. This is Hemsley's second stint as CEO; he previously served in the role from 2006 to 2017 and will remain chairman of the board. Witty will transition to a senior advisor role to Hemsley.

UnitedHealth Group is the third largest hospice provider in the nation, primarily through its subsidiary Optum, a position largely achieved through its 2023 acquisition of LHC Group for $5.4 billion. The leadership change follows the May 1 appointment of Dr. Patrick Conway as Optum's CEO amid a broader C-suite revamp.

The transition comes after a difficult first quarter for the company, which faced government funding reductions, a transition to a new Medicare Advantage risk adjustment model, and heightened care activity. UnitedHealth Group reduced its 2025 performance outlook to $24.65–$25.15 earnings per share (down from $26–$26.50) and has since suspended its 2025 outlook. Optum's $3.3 billion purchase of Amedisys (Nasdaq: AMED) is pending a court decision following antitrust concerns from the U.S. Department of Justice.

Hemsley pledged the company will "return to growth" in 2026 and reiterated the long-term growth objective of 13–16%.

# Shareholder group calls on UnitedHealth to decouple CEO from board chair

Stephen Hemsley is the chairman of UnitedHealth’s board and its CEO. The Accountability Board says that undercuts corporate governance at a turbulent time for the company.

### Dive Brief:

### Dive Insight:

UnitedHealth is facing a sea of recent difficulties, including a [massive cyberattack](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/change-healthcare-cyberattack-affects-190-million-unitedhealth/738351/) requiring billions of dollars in response costs, [rising medical expenses shrinking the profitability](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicare-advantage-plans-2026-unitedhealthcare-humana-aetna/801761/) of its insurance division and [antitrust probes from federal regulators](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealth-under-investigation-department-of-justice-medicare/753913/). The massive healthcare company is also embroiled in a [public relations crisis following the killing of its top insurance executive](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealthcare-ceo-brian-thompson-shooting-reactions/734707/) late last year.

UnitedHealth’s stock has plummeted as the string of crises make investors less bullish on the company, despite its broad market power and [record $400.3 billion in revenue](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealth-unh-2024-record-revenue/737477/) last year.

#### UnitedHealth's stock has fallen 29% this year

[Witty stepped down as CEO in May](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/andrew-witty-unitedhealth-ceo-steps-down-hemsley/747945/), citing personal reasons. In his place, the board appointed Hemsley, the 73-year-old chairman of UnitedHealth’s board and its CEO from 2006 to 2017.

Analysts said the move would likely restore some confidence in UnitedHealth, given Hemsley built the company into the diversified healthcare behemoth it is today during his first tenure as CEO. However, not everyone is so sure that handing the reins over to Hemsley was a good idea.

The Accountability Board,which invests in upwards of 100 of the largest publicly traded companies in the U.S., is now calling for a policy to keep the CEO and board chair roles separate. The reform would restore trust in UnitedHealth’s board by ensuring it can provide objective oversight of management, the activist group said.

The Accountability Board engaged with UnitedHealth before filing the proposal, and found its rationale for combining the CEO and board chair roles “deeply flawed,” Matt Prescott, the president and chief operating officer of the group, told Healthcare Dive over email.

The proposal points to UnitedHealth’s Corporate Governance Principles, which were issued six months before Hemsley was named CEO. The principles say the rolesshould be autonomous “as an aid in the Board’s oversight of management and to allow the Chief Executive Officer to focus primarily on management responsibilities,” according to the proposal.

“In our view, independent Chairs are like seatbelts: it’s easy to forget you might need one when the road is smooth but once the storm rolls in, you’re sure glad it’s there,”  Prescott said. “UnitedHealth has been in the middle of a storm and needs the added guardrail of an independent Chair — someone who can challenge management’s assumptions and ensure senior executives are acting in the best interests of shareholders.”

The Accountability Board’s proposal isn’t the first push for reform from investors concerned about UnitedHealth’s trajectory.

In January, [a faith-based group of investors asked UnitedHealth](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealth-shareholder-proposal-delayed-denied-care-outcomes/737075/) to analyze the impact of healthcare delays and denials on the company and U.S. patients. Though, following multiple challenges from UnitedHealth, the group [withdrew the proposal in April](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealth-shareholders-withdraw-proposal-healthcare-delays-denials/744582/) before it had a chance to come to a shareholder vote.

A group of [investors also sued UnitedHealth](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealth-shareholder-lawsuit-thompson-denials-impacts/747499/) in May, arguing that the company didn’t properly disclose to shareholders how the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson impacted the company.

Amid the turmoil, in August [UnitedHealth formed a new public responsibility board committee](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealth-board-committee-reputational-regulatory-risks/758246/) in a bid to improve corporate governance. Hemsley has also pledged to [increase public transparency](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealth-2025-outlook-lower-earnings/754243/) moving forward.

This is a Healthcare Dive news article reporting that The Accountability Board, an activist shareholder group investing in over 100 of the largest publicly traded U.S. companies, is calling on UnitedHealth to separate the CEO and board chair roles. Stephen Hemsley, the 73-year-old chairman of UnitedHealth's board, was appointed CEO in May after Andrew Witty stepped down citing personal reasons. Hemsley previously served as CEO from 2006 to 2017.

The article details UnitedHealth's recent difficulties, including a massive cyberattack requiring billions in response costs, rising medical expenses shrinking the profitability of its insurance division, antitrust probes from federal regulators, a public relations crisis following the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson late last year, and a 29% stock decline this year despite record $400.3 billion in revenue last year.

The Accountability Board engaged with UnitedHealth before filing the proposal and found the company's rationale for combining the roles "deeply flawed," according to Matt Prescott, the group's president and COO. The proposal cites UnitedHealth's own Corporate Governance Principles, issued six months before Hemsley was named CEO, which state the roles should be autonomous to aid board oversight.

The article also notes this isn't the first investor push for reform: a faith-based group withdrew a January proposal in April about healthcare delays and denials, investors sued UnitedHealth in May over disclosure regarding Thompson's killing, and UnitedHealth formed a new public responsibility board committee in August to improve corporate governance. Hemsley has pledged to increase public transparency moving forward.

URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IPMZuC2FktI

SUMMARY:
<summary>
## JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon Speaks at Reagan National Economic Forum (May 29, 2026)

This is a CNBC Television video featuring a full-length interview between JPMorgan Chase Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon and CNBC's Morgan Brennan at the Reagan National Economic Forum. The event took place on Friday, May 29, 2026, and was introduced by Susan McCaw, a member of the board of trustees of the Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute. The forum marked Dimon's second appearance at the event.

### Key Topics and Positions:

**Geopolitical Tectonic Plates:** Dimon emphasized that global geopolitical shifts (the war in Ukraine, Middle East terrorism, the Iranian war, global deficits, remilitarization, and trade restructuring) "dwarf the short-term economy." He expressed that the U.S. should have been more supportive of Ukraine and criticized tolerating Iranian aggression for 47 years, suggesting the U.S. should have acted decisively against Iran decades ago. He called an Iranian nuclear weapon "the biggest threat facing mankind" due to nuclear proliferation risks.

**Alliances and Trade:** Dimon argued that economic allies are critical and advocated for deeper trade relationships with Europe, Canada, Mexico, Australia, Japan, South Korea, and the Philippines. He proposed offering Europe "one big beautiful free trade deal" conditional on implementing the Draghi report recommendations. He supports countering unfair trade with tariffs but wants USMCA and other trade negotiations concluded.

**Dollar Dominance:** Dimon dismissed de-dollarization fears, calling it an "IQ test" — the dollar will remain the reserve currency as long as the U.S. maintains preeminent military and economic positions. He noted that unlike China (which has capital controls), U.S. dollars can be used freely.

**Security and Resiliency Initiative:** Dimon detailed JPMorgan's $1.5 trillion, 10-year Security and Resiliency Initiative (likely to far exceed that amount), investing in military equipment, productive capability, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), rare earths, and semiconductors. The bank hired investor Todd Combs for direct investments. Dimon advocated for "smart industrial policy" including tariffs or barriers to prevent importing rare earths from China (U.S. currently imports only $200 million in rare earths; quadrupling costs would have minimal economic impact). He admitted the U.S. was "asleep at the switch" for 10-15 years on critical supply chain dependencies.

**Permitting and Bureaucracy:** Dimon strongly criticized the U.S. permitting system and bureaucracy across infrastructure, housing, grids, and sewers, calling it "a disgrace." He proposed a 6-month Congressional session focused purely on policy changes (housing, permitting, education) without revenue or spending debates, estimating this could drive 1% higher growth.

**Affordability and the American Dream:** Dimon rejected the "K-shaped economy" narrative, arguing the top 70% are doing fine (middle class has grown richer) while the bottom 30% have seen stagnant wages for 25 years and can no longer earn living wages without college. He emphasized fixing this through good policy (education, housing, infrastructure, crime) rather than government spending, noting "trillions of dollars" have been spent without results.

**American Dream Initiative:** JPMorgan announced this initiative covering affordable housing mortgages, small business support (expanding from 7 million to 10 million small business clients), financial education, and work skills. Dimon emphasized teaching American values and the Constitution's founding principles (freedom, liberty, pursuit of happiness defined as having purpose).

**Tax Policy:** Dimon praised Jeff Bezos for engaging in the tax debate. He proposed reforming the Earned Income Tax Credit — eliminating the child requirement, changing the income threshold from $14,000 to $12,000 for single parents, which would give working recipients about $26,000 ($52,000 for two-parent households). He argued this would pay for itself through workforce participation, dignity, reduced crime, and better social outcomes, costing roughly $50 billion.

**Monetary Policy and New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh:** Dimon expressed support for new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (calling him "high quality, experienced"), noting the Fed overstepped into regulatory policy (climate, DEI) and violated constitutional requirements by skipping cost-benefit analyses. He supports reducing the Fed's balance sheet but cautioned Warsh faces 12 committee members and "almost no chance" of changing anything within 6 months.

**Inflation:** Dimon believes inflationary forces are stronger than generally perceived — ticking up from Iran conflict, food, healthcare (up 10% annually), remilitarization, AI spending, trade restructuring, immigration restrictions, and cumulative effects of $2 trillion annual government spending. He suggested inflation could hit 4%, and the 10-year Treasury at 4.5% may be at equilibrium.

**Markets:** Dimon called the equity market "exuberant," noting hype in AI-related stocks and low credit spreads as risks. He said JPMorgan can handle rates at 2% or 8% and isn't betting the company on either scenario. He praised SpaceX as "extraordinary" and supportive of the IPO environment, though noted ECM (equity capital markets) can close and open quickly (citing 400 IPOs in 2022 vs. 20 the next year).

**Biggest Risk:** Dimon identified "the geopolitics of how the free world plays out in the next 20 years" as the biggest underappreciated risk.

**Crypto/Blockchain:** Dimon remains pragmatic — JPMorgan is one of the biggest blockchain users, has a JPMorgan deposit coin moving money 24/7, and believes blockchain will replace financial market infrastructure. On stablecoins, he only asks for a level playing field with the same rules as AML, BSA, KYC, insurance, disclosures, and liquidity requirements.

**M&A:** Dimon addressed his earlier comments about $10-20 billion of potential acquisitions, saying the bank has excess capital and should always consider acquisitions. He joked about buying CNBC ("Versant"), noting they look "cheap." He emphasized using competitive analysis (asking why JPMorgan didn't build Stripe, why Chase UK isn't like Revolut, which is worth $75 billion) as a management tool.

**Private Credit:** Dimon downplayed systemic risks — private credit is $1.7 trillion versus investment-grade at $15 trillion and mortgages at $13 trillion — but warned that weakening underwriting standards and transparency will cause credit to perform worse than expected in the next credit cycle.

**Legacy:** Dimon said his legacy priorities are family first, country second, then Chase. He described his values (purpose, hard work, making the world better, not allowing bullies, treating people with respect) and quoted his brother's teaching. He wants his gravestone to say people are "better off" because of him. He has eight grandchildren, three children, and a wife.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Those tectonic plates, they are still shifting. They're still moving. They're still the most important thing that's taking place in the world. They dwarf the short-term economy and that's the war in Ukraine." — Jamie Dimon
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: JPMorgan loses a key figure in the race to succeed CEO Jamie Dimon ---
URL: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jpmorgan-loses-a-key-figure-in-the-race-to-succeed-ceo-jamie-dimon-123901072.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
JPMorgan Chase announced a major reshuffling of top management under CEO Jamie Dimon on Thursday, in the latest development in the race to succeed the country's largest bank's longtime leader. The co-CEOs of the bank's commercial and investment bank, Doug Petno (61) and Troy Rohrbaugh (56), have been elevated to co-presidents effective immediately. Marianne Lake, CEO of JPMorgan's consumer and community bank, will retire after more than 25 years at the company. 

The moves narrow the succession race down to Petno or Rohrbaugh, according to an executive familiar with the matter. Petno becomes sole CEO of the commercial and investment bank, while Rohrbaugh replaces Lake as CEO of the consumer bank. Since neither has worked within the consumer bank, Bank of America analyst Ebrahim Poonawala said the moves set up Rohrbaugh as the lead candidate. Lake will stay for the coming weeks to smooth Rohrbaugh's transition.

The board granted "one-time retention" equity awards worth $30 million each to Petno and Rohrbaugh, and $20 million each to COO Jennifer Piepszak and asset & wealth management CEO Mary Erdoes.

The 70-year-old Dimon, the longest-serving big bank CEO and the only remaining CEO from the 2008 financial crisis, is expected to stay for three more years. In May 2024, Dimon said his exit timetable is "not five years anymore" and that succession was "well on the way." In January 2026, when asked how much longer he wanted to be CEO, Dimon replied "at least" five more years. Dimon previously interviewed Elon Musk earlier this month as part of JPMorgan's promotion of the SpaceX IPO.

For years, Lake and Jennifer Piepszak were viewed as the frontrunners, but Piepszak pulled herself out of the running in January 2025 after being elevated to COO. Up until the announcement, a Kalshi prediction market contract had placed majority odds on Lake as the most likely successor. RBC analyst Gerard Cassidy said the reshuffling "comes as a surprise," while Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo noted that investors may want Dimon to stay, "but this comes with a cost of loss of talent" in reference to Lake's departure.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"The changes announced today mark an important step in our Board's thoughtful process around succession planning and development of our top leaders," Dimon said in a statement with the release.
</key_excerpts>

URL: https://kevinmullin.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Meta-Election-Integrity-Letter-8.17.26.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a formal letter dated August 17, 2026, from 18 U.S. Members of Congress (led by Kevin Mullin, Joseph D. Morelle, Debbie Dingell, Nikema Williams, Shri Thanedar, Seth Magaziner, Yassamin Ansari, Greg Casar, Nancy Pelosi, Madeleine Dean, Dan Goldman, Terri A. Sewell, Adam Smith, Lateefah Simon, Sylvia R. Garcia, Valerie P. Foushee, Adelita S. Grijalva, Donald S. Beyer Jr., and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez) addressed to Mark Zuckerberg, Chairman and CEO of Meta Platforms, Inc., expressing serious concern over Meta's rollback of misinformation safeguards and the risk this poses to the 2026 U.S. elections.

Key concerns raised in the letter include:
1. In January 2025, Meta discontinued its third-party fact-checking program (which had partnered with 90+ independent organizations) while reportedly continuing fact-checking partnerships in other countries. The program was launched in 2016 amid election concerns, and Zuckerberg had described it to Congress in March 2021 as "unprecedented" and "industry-leading."
2. Meta rolled back automated enforcement systems for removing mis/disinformation and hate speech, replacing them with "Community Notes" — which only act as unobtrusive disclosures and do not stop the spread of underlying content. Zuckerberg acknowledged the change would lead to Meta "catch[ing] less bad stuff."
3. Following the change, white supremacist propaganda and Holocaust denial clips circulated on Instagram Reels with millions of views before Meta intervened.
4. Internal documents revealed up to 90% of privacy and integrity risk assessments at Meta could now be automated, meaning critical algorithm updates and safety features could be approved by AI without human review — raising concerns about election-integrity risks going live with less oversight.
5. Generative AI has made deepfake production dramatically easier. Specific examples cited include: a 22-year-old medical student in India fabricating "Emily Hart," a fake conservative MAGA influencer with millions of views; confirmed deepfake incidents in Texas and Georgia Senate races (including a fabricated video of Texas Senate candidate James Talarico); and a deepfake news bulletin before Ireland's October 2025 presidential election falsely depicting candidate Catherine Connolly withdrawing.

The letter acknowledges Meta's economic contributions and past leadership on election integrity (including hosting legislators in Menlo Park and election war rooms) but argues the current approach is inadequate. It poses nine detailed questions requesting responses by Friday, September 18, 2026, covering: (1) election integrity staffing/budget comparisons (2026 vs 2020/2024); (2) policies on non-advertising AI-generated political content and removal times; (3) disclosure requirements for paid influencers; (4) disclosure requirements for AI-generated political ads; (5) dedicated reporting channels for election officials and response times; (6) real-name policy enforcement and bot prevention; (7) disclosure requirements for non-paid pages and third-party accounts; (8) measured impact of Community Notes since January 2025; and (9) content takedown volumes since January 2025 compared to 2023-2024 by platform.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 7: Meta's Zuckerberg adds UFC's Dana White, two others to board | Fortune ---
URL: https://fortune.com/2025/01/06/meta-board-mark-zuckerberg-ufc-dana-white-trump-charlie-songhurst-john-elkann

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Fortune news article (via Bloomberg) reporting that Meta Platforms elected three new directors to its board on January 6, 2025. The three new members are:
- Dana White, CEO of Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), a high-profile campaigner for President-elect Donald Trump and a personal friend of Mark Zuckerberg.
- Charlie Songhurst, an investor and former Microsoft Corp. executive who already advised Meta on AI products and will leave that advisory council to take the board seat.
- John Elkann, CEO of Exor NV (the Agnelli family holding company with stakes in Ferrari NV and Juventus FC), who is also executive chairman of Stellantis NV and Ferrari.

These additions bring Meta's board to 13 directors, including CEO Mark Zuckerberg, who retains majority voting control through dual-class stock structure. Zuckerberg has largely remade Meta's board in the past five years — all but two current directors have joined since 2019 — coinciding with his pivot toward AI and the metaverse. Other recent board additions include DoorDash CEO Tony Xu and Dropbox CEO Drew Houston.

The article notes the political context: White was a vocal Trump supporter during the 2024 campaign (speaking at the RNC and Trump's election-night event), and Zuckerberg has been working to improve his relationship with Trump, including dining at Mar-a-Lago in November and naming Joel Kaplan, an executive with deep GOP ties, as policy chief the previous week. Zuckerberg and White have a personal friendship — Zuckerberg is an avid MMA fan and recreational fighter, and White sought his advice on incorporating AI into UFC's rankings system last year. Songhurst was involved in Microsoft's $8.5 billion acquisition of Skype. The article also promotes Fortune Daily, Fortune's new video show.
</summary>

"Charlie, Dana and John will add a depth of expertise and perspective that will help us tackle the massive opportunities ahead with AI, wearables and the future of human connection," Zuckerberg said in a statement., The additions bring Meta's board to 13 directors, including CEO Mark Zuckerberg, who holds the title of chairman and retains majority voting control through the company's dual-class stock structure., All but two of Meta's current directors have joined since 2019., White was also a vocal supporter of Trump during his 2024 campaign, speaking at the Republican National Convention in the summer and at Trump's election-night event., Songhurst was previously general manager of global corporate strategy at Microsoft, where he was involved in some of the company's biggest deals, including its $8.5 billion acquisition of Skype.

Stephen J. Hemsley (born June 4, 1952) is an American businessman who is the board chairman and chief executive officer of UnitedHealth Group Inc. A lawsuit was filed against Hemsley, UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, and two other senior executives in May 2024 for alleged fraud and insider trading related to failing to disclose a DOJ antitrust investigation and selling stock before the probe became public. Compensation highlights: Business Week reported his 2009 salary as $14,518,164; 2016 compensation was estimated at $31.3 million (a 55.8% increase from 2015's ~$14.5 million); he was paid $102 million in 2009 per SEC filings; Forbes named him the highest paid CEO in 2011. SUMMARY:

This is a Healthcare Dive news article reporting that The Accountability Board, an activist shareholder group investing in over 100 of the largest publicly traded U.S. companies, is calling on UnitedHealth to separate the CEO and board chair roles. Stephen Hemsley, the 73-year-old chairman of UnitedHealth's board, was appointed CEO in May after Andrew Witty stepped down citing personal reasons. Hemsley previously served as CEO from 2006 to 2017.

The article details UnitedHealth's recent difficulties, including a massive cyberattack requiring billions in response costs, rising medical expenses shrinking the profitability of its insurance division, antitrust probes from federal regulators, a public relations crisis following the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson late last year, and a 29% stock decline this year despite record $400.3 billion in revenue last year.

The Accountability Board engaged with UnitedHealth before filing the proposal and found the company's rationale for combining the roles "deeply flawed," according to Matt Prescott, the group's president and COO. The proposal cites UnitedHealth's own Corporate Governance Principles, issued six months before Hemsley was named CEO, which state the roles should be autonomous to aid board oversight.

The article also notes this isn't the first investor push for reform: a faith-based group withdrew a January proposal in April about healthcare delays and denials, investors sued UnitedHealth in May over disclosure regarding Thompson's killing, and UnitedHealth formed a new public responsibility board committee in August to improve corporate governance. Hemsley has pledged to increase public transparency moving forward.

**Kenichiro Yoshida** (born 20 October 1959) is a Japanese businessman currently serving as executive chairman of [Sony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony "Sony"). He previously served as president and CEO from April 2018 to April 2025, succeeding [Kazuo Hirai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazuo_Hirai "Kazuo Hirai"), prior to which Yoshida was the company's chief financial officer.[[1]](#cite_note-FT1-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kenichiro_Yoshida&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Yoshida was born in [Kumamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumamoto "Kumamoto") in 1959, where his father, a court judge, was posted at the time.[[3]](#cite_note-:0-3) Immediately after graduating from the [University of Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tokyo "University of Tokyo") with a B.A. in economics in 1983, Yoshida joined Sony, and worked across the company's subsidiaries in the US and Japan.[[1]](#cite_note-FT1-1)

In the year 2000, he worked for Sony subsidiary [So-net](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So-net "So-net"), which he took public in 2005. He rejoined Sony in 2013 as deputy chief financial officer and was promoted to chief financial officer the following year.[[1]](#cite_note-FT1-1) In his role as CFO, he was credited with pushing the company through an extensive restructuring which turned around Sony's losses from consumer electronics.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[1]](#cite_note-FT1-1)[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kenichiro_Yoshida&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Yoshida has an autistic son and makes it a point to spend at least one entire day a week with him. He has been active in raising awareness about autism.[[3]](#cite_note-:0-3)

Kenichiro Yoshida is a Japanese businessman born on October 20, 1959, in Kumamoto, Japan. He is currently serving as executive chairman of Sony, having previously served as the company's president and CEO from April 2018 to April 2025, succeeding Kazuo Hirai. Before becoming CEO, Yoshida served as Sony's chief financial officer.

Yoshida graduated from the University of Tokyo with a B.A. in economics in 1983 and joined Sony immediately after graduation, working across the company's subsidiaries in the US and Japan. In 2000, he worked for Sony subsidiary So-net, which he took public in 2005. He rejoined Sony in 2013 as deputy chief financial officer and was promoted to CFO the following year. As CFO, he was credited with leading the company through extensive restructuring that turned around Sony's losses from consumer electronics.

In his personal life, Yoshida has an autistic son and dedicates at least one full day per week to spending time with him. He has been active in raising awareness about autism.

January 29, 2025

# Changes to Sony Group's Management Structure

Hiroki Totoki appointed as President and CEO effective April 1, 2025

January 29, 2025  
Revised on April 1, 2025

Tokyo, Japan - Sony Group Corporation ("Sony") today announced that Hiroki Totoki, currently Director, Representative Corporate Executive Officer, President, COO and CFO, has been newly appointed as Director, Representative Corporate Executive Officer, President and Chief Executive Officer, effective April 1, 2025. Kenichiro Yoshida, currently Director, Representative Corporate Executive Officer, Chairman and CEO, will become Director, Representative Corporate Executive Officer, Executive Chairman, also effective April 1, 2025. These appointments were proposed by Kenichiro Yoshida to the Nominating Committee, and following deliberation by the Committee, were approved unanimously at the Board meeting held today.

Also effective April 1, 2025, Sony will implement changes to its management structure to clarify management roles according to their responsibilities for the management of the entire Group or of each business, and make further appointments, as outlined below.

In terms of the management structure changes, each of the Chief Executive Officers of the Sony Group's major businesses will be designated as a "Business CEO"; each of those assisting the CEO who oversees the entire Group's management, and has responsibility for wide-ranging headquarters functions, will be designated as a "Chief Officer"; and each of the executives in charge of functions at the Group headquarters will be designated as a "Corporate Executive."

The following Chief Officers have been appointed: Toshimoto Mitomo as Chief Strategy Officer (current position), Tsuyoshi Kodera as Chief Digital Officer (current position), Yasuhiro Ito as Chief People Officer (new position), and Lin Tao as Chief Financial Officer (newly appointed). In addition, in the technology field, Hiroaki Kitano has been appointed as Chief Technology Fellow.

## Comment from Kenichiro Yoshida

"To ensure that my succession contributes to Sony's future long-term growth, I have been in discussion with the Nominating Committee and the Board of Directors for some time. Based on Hiroki Totoki's contributions to Sony, including his achievements since being appointed as President and COO in April 2023, I proposed to them that he succeed me as CEO this April. I am grateful to the Nominating Committee and the Board for their support of this proposal. Totoki has been a key member of the management team ever since I became President and CEO in April 2018. He spearheaded growth strategies for the Sony Group, such as our investments in content IP and semiconductors, and is a leader capable of shaping our vision and strategy for future growth. Going forward, I will support Totoki as he leads his new management team."

## Comment from Hiroki Totoki

"I am incredibly honored and humbled to have been entrusted with the important role of President and CEO. At the same time, I am looking forward to working as CEO with our approximately 110,000 employees to further evolve and grow Sony. My predecessors as CEO, Kazuo Hirai and Kenichiro Yoshida, have greatly enhanced Sony's value, and I will do my utmost to further build on this success and pass on an even better Sony to the next generation. At our Corporate Strategy Meeting in May of last year, we newly announced our `Creative Entertainment Vision,' which outlines where we want Sony to be in 10 years, with our Purpose as the guiding principle. Our greatest driver in achieving this is the diversity of our businesses and people, which is part of Sony's DNA, and our boundary spanners that transcend organizational barriers and organically connect that diversity to create new value. Together with our employees, creators, partners, and our new leadership team, I will work to create a bright future filled with a boundless sense of Kando (emotion)."

## Comment from Yoshihiko Hatanaka, Chair of the Board and Chair of the Nominating Committee

"As CEO, Kenichiro Yoshida has led Sony's evolution and growth through the establishment of Sony's Purpose and implementation of management initiatives centered around a `Creation Shift.' We are extremely grateful for his significant contributions. Hiroki Totoki has served as CFO since 2018 and as President, COO and CFO from 2023, and the Board of Directors highly values his achievements and leadership driving Sony's growth strategies, together with current CEO Yoshida. The Nominating Committee is continuously discussing succession plans for the management team and Totoki was evaluated as a strong candidate for CEO. With Yoshida's proposal, the Committee conducted a multifaceted review, and the Board, taking into consideration the views of the Committee, today unanimously approved Totoki's appointment as President and CEO. The Board will fully support the new management team together with Yoshida, who continues as Executive Chairman."

**Lei Jun** (born 16 December 1969) is a Chinese [billionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire") [entrepreneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneur "Entrepreneur") and [computer engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_Engineer "Computer Engineer"). He is known for being the founder, chairman, and CEO of the consumer electronics company [Xiaomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiaomi "Xiaomi"). He also is the chairman of [Kingsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsoft "Kingsoft") and [Shunwei Capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shunwei_Capital "Shunwei Capital"). Lei has been a deputy to the [National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_People's_Congress "National People's Congress") since 2013.

As of May 2025, Lei's net worth was estimated at US$42.6 billion by *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")*, ranking him 33rd worldwide.[[2]](#cite_note-forbesprofile-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Lei_Jun&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Lei was born on 16 December 1969 in the city of [Xiantao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiantao "Xiantao"), [Hubei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubei "Hubei"), China.[[3]](#cite_note-3) Both of his parents were teachers;[[4]](#cite_note-4) his father made $7 a month.[[5]](#cite_note-5) As a child, he was interested in electronics and liked disassembling and re-assembling radios, which was encouraged by his father.[[6]](#cite_note-6) He made the first [electric lamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_lamp "Electric lamp") in his village using two batteries, a bulb, a self-made wooden box, and some wires.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

In 1987, he graduated from Hubei Provincial Mianyang High School (湖北省沔阳中学) and started to attend [Wuhan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan_University "Wuhan University"). He graduated from Wuhan University and received a Bachelor of Science degree with a major in Computer Science in 1991.[[1]](#cite_note-founder-1)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Lei_Jun&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In 1992, Lei joined [Kingsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsoft "Kingsoft") as an engineer. He became the CEO of the company in 1998 and led it towards an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") on the [Hong Kong Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_Stock_Exchange "Hong Kong Stock Exchange") in 2007. On 20 December 2007, he resigned as president and CEO of Kingsoft for "health reasons".[[8]](#cite_note-twisting-8)

In 2000, Lei founded [joyo.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_China "Amazon China"), an online retailing platform,[[9]](#cite_note-9) which he sold for US$75 million to [Amazon.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon.com "Amazon.com") in 2004.[[10]](#cite_note-10) In 2005, he made a $1 million investment in [YY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YY_(social_network) "YY (social network)"); those shares were worth $129 million when the company became a [public company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_company "Public company") via an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") in 2012.[[11]](#cite_note-11) In 2008, he became a chairman of [UCWeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCWeb "UCWeb").[[12]](#cite_note-12)

In 2010, Lei founded Xiaomi with multiple partners, including former Google executive [Lin Bin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Bin "Lin Bin").[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In 2011, he co-founded [Shunwei Capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shunwei_Capital "Shunwei Capital") ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 顺为资本), an investment company, via which he invests in companies in the e-commerce, [social networking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_networking "Social networking"), and mobile industries.[[14]](#cite_note-14) Also in 7 July 2011, he rejoined Kingsoft as chairman.[[8]](#cite_note-twisting-8)

In 2012, Lei Jun was elected as a deputy to the Beijing Municipal People’s Congress. In 2013, he was elected as a delegate to the 12th National People’s Congress representing Guangdong Province.

On 26 December 2013, he founded "Beijing Xiaomi Payment Technology Co., Ltd." with a registered capital of 50 million RMB. Lei Jun was the company’s legal representative and chairman.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

On 24 February 2018, he was elected as a deputy to the 13th National People’s Congress.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

On 21 June 2018, Lei Jun, along with Xiaomi’s core executives, began the IPO roadshow in Hong Kong. Xiaomi’s stock code was 01810.HK. According to the prospectus, Xiaomi planned to issue 2.18 billion shares with a pricing range between 17 and 22 HKD per share, aiming to raise up to 6.1 billion USD. The authorized share capital had a total nominal value of 675,000 USD, consisting of 70 billion Class A shares and 200 billion Class B shares. Based on this, Xiaomi’s adjusted market value was estimated between 53.9 and 69.7 billion USD.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

On the morning of 9 July 2018, at 9:30 AM, Lei Jun rang the gong for Xiaomi’s listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, officially bringing the eight-year-old company to the capital market. Xiaomi became the first company listed under the "weighted voting rights" structure on the exchange, prompting the HKEX to specially commission a new copper gong for the occasion.

In 2019, Xiaomi was named a Fortune Global 500 company, becoming the youngest company on the list at the time.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

In 2020, Xiaomi fully entered the high-end smartphone market by launching the Xiaomi 10 series, signaling a brand shift toward "technology and quality."[[19]](#cite_note-19)

In March 2021, Lei Jun officially announced Xiaomi’s entry into the smart electric vehicle industry. He personally took charge of the project and planned to invest 10 billion USD over the next decade.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

In March 2024, Xiaomi’s first electric vehicle, the [Xiaomi SU7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiaomi_SU7 "Xiaomi SU7"), was officially unveiled.[[21]](#cite_note-21) The model, focused on high performance and smart features, drew widespread attention, with Lei Jun personally hosting the launch event. The first batch of models received strong market response, with pre-orders exceeding 100,000, marking a successful initial step in Lei Jun’s automotive strategy.[[22]](#cite_note-22)

### Politics

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Lei_Jun&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Politics")]

He was elected to serve as a deputy to the [Twelfth National People's Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12th_National_People's_Congress "12th National People's Congress") for the Guangdong congressional district in 2013.[[23]](#cite_note-23) He was elected to serve as a deputy to the [Thirteenth National People's Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13th_National_People's_Congress "13th National People's Congress") for the Beijing congressional district in 2018.[[24]](#cite_note-24) He was re-elected to serve as a deputy to the [Fourteenth National People's Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/14th_National_People's_Congress "14th National People's Congress") for the Beijing congressional district in 2023.[[25]](#cite_note-25)

### Philanthropy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Lei_Jun&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

By 2017, Lei had donated $1 billion to charity, starting with a ¥140,000 donation in 1997 to his [alma mater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alma_mater "Alma mater"), [Wuhan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan_University "Wuhan University"). He later made donations to Zhuhai Charity, an organization that funds schools for migrants, the villagers of [Yangchun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangchun "Yangchun") for the renovation of schools and [mudbrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudbrick "Mudbrick") houses and construction of cultural buildings, the victims of the [2013 Lushan earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Lushan_earthquake "2013 Lushan earthquake"), and was a participant in the [Ice Bucket Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_Bucket_Challenge "Ice Bucket Challenge") to raise funds for [amyotrophic lateral sclerosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amyotrophic_lateral_sclerosis "Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis").[[26]](#cite_note-26) In 2021, he donated over $2.2 billion worth of Xiaomi shares to charity.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

In 2023, Lei Jun donated 1.3 billion yuan to [Wuhan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan_University "Wuhan University"), the largest individual donation the university has ever received.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29)

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Lei_Jun&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Lei and his wife Zhang Tong (张彤) have two children.[[2]](#cite_note-forbesprofile-2)

## Awards and recognition

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Lei_Jun&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Awards and recognition")]

In 2014, Lei was named Businessman of the Year by *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")*.[[30]](#cite_note-30) In 2015, he was named to the [Time 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").[[31]](#cite_note-31)

In 2019, Lei was recognized as an "Outstanding Builder of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics" ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): 优秀中国特色社会主义事业建设者). The recognition was used by the [United States Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense") as one of the reasons to add Xiaomi Corporation to a list of companies that support China's military in January 2021.[[32]](#cite_note-32) Later, the blacklisting of Xiaomi was blocked by a United States federal court and was removed by the United States Department of Defense after an agreement with Xiaomi was reached.[[33]](#cite_note-33)[[34]](#cite_note-34)

args.summary:
Lei Jun (born 16 December 1969) is a Chinese billionaire entrepreneur and computer engineer, best known as the founder, chairman, and CEO of Xiaomi. As of May 2025, Forbes estimated his net worth at US$42.6 billion, ranking him 33rd worldwide.

EARLY LIFE & EDUCATION: Lei was born in Xiantao, Hubei, China. Both parents were teachers; his father earned $7 a month. As a child he showed interest in electronics, disassembling and reassembling radios. He graduated from Hubei Provincial Mianyang High School in 1987 and earned a BS in Computer Science from Wuhan University in 1991.

CAREER HIGHLIGHTS:
- 1992: Joined Kingsoft as an engineer; became CEO in 1998, leading its IPO on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2007. Resigned as president/CEO in December 2007 for "health reasons."
- 2000: Founded joyo.com, an online retail platform, sold to Amazon.com for US$75 million in 2004.
- 2005: Invested $1 million in YY; shares were worth $129 million at YY's 2012 IPO (hundred-fold return).
- 2008: Became chairman of UCWeb.
- 2010: Founded Xiaomi with partners including former Google executive Lin Bin.
- 2011: Co-founded Shunwei Capital (investment firm); rejoined Kingsoft as chairman in July 2011.
- 2012: Elected deputy to Beijing Municipal People's Congress.
- 2013: Elected delegate to 12th National People's Congress (Guangdong).
- 2018: Xiaomi IPO on Hong Kong Stock Exchange (stock code 01810.HK); Lei rang the gong on 9 July 2018. Xiaomi was the first company listed under "weighted voting rights" structure.
- 2019: Xiaomi named a Fortune Global 500 company — youngest on the list at the time.
- 2020: Xiaomi entered high-end smartphone market with Xiaomi 10 series.
- March 2021: Announced entry into smart EV industry, personally taking charge, planning $10 billion investment over a decade.
- March 2024: Xiaomi SU7 (first EV) unveiled; pre-orders exceeded 100,000.

POLITICS: Elected deputy to the 12th (2013, Guangdong), 13th (2018, Beijing), and 14th (2023, Beijing) National People's Congress.

PHILANTHROPY: By 2017 had donated $1 billion to charity. In 2021 donated over $2.2 billion worth of Xiaomi shares. In 2023 donated 1.3 billion yuan to Wuhan University — the largest individual donation the university has ever received.

PERSONAL: Married to Zhang Tong with two children.

AWARDS: Named Forbes Businessman of the Year 2014; named to Time 100 in 2015. In 2019 recognized as an "Outstanding Builder of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics," which the US Department of Defense used as a reason to add Xiaomi to a China-military-support blacklist in January 2021; the blacklisting was blocked by a US federal court and Xiaomi was subsequently removed after an agreement.

This is a Forbes profile page for Lei Jun, cofounder, chairman, and CEO of Hong Kong-listed Xiaomi, one of the world's most popular smartphone brands. As of July 14, 2026, Lei Jun's real-time net worth is $21 billion, ranking #130 in the world on Forbes' real-time billionaires list. His wealth source is smartphones and automobiles (self-made).

Key biographical details: Age 56, residence in Beijing, China, married with 2 children, holds a Bachelor of Science in Engineering from Wuhan University. He also serves as chairman of Hong Kong-listed software firm Kingsoft and is an investor in JOYY, a Nasdaq-listed live-streaming platform formerly known as YY.com.

Lei's entrepreneurial journey: His first major success was selling online retailer Joyo.com to Amazon in 2004 for $75 million. Forbes rankings: #90 on Billionaires (2026), #7 on China's 100 Richest (2025), #36 on Richest in Tech (2017). He was named Forbes Asia's Businessman of the Year in 2014 after Xiaomi overtook Apple and Samsung to rank No. 1 in China's smartphone market within four years.

# About - Founder | Xiaomi Global

## Leadership Team

[About Us](/global/about)

![Lei Jun](//i02.appmifile.com/679_operator_global/23/05/2024/18390bace96197fc0ccdb716bd2775d9.png)

### Lei Jun

Founder, Chairman and CEO

Lei Jun, born in December 1969, received a bachelor's degree in Computer Science from Wuhan University in July 1991. He is now Xiaomi's founder, executive director, chairman and CEO. Lei Jun is a renowned technology entrepreneur in China. He joined Kingsoft Corporation Limited in 1992 and has held several senior positions, including chairman of the board since July 2011, director of the board at Beijing Kingsoft Office Software, Inc. since December 2011. In 2000, Lei Jun founded joyo.com, an online retailing platform, which was acquired by Amazon in 2004. Meanwhile, as an angel investor, Lei Jun has also invested in various innovative businesses, including JOYY Inc. and UCWeb.

![Lin Bin](//i02.appmifile.com/402_operator_global/23/05/2024/f30365162c60b642178ff71305c6665e.png)

### Lin Bin

Co-Founder and Vice Chairman

Lin Bin, born in February 1968, received a bachelor's degree in Radio Electronics and Engineering from Sun Yat-sen University in July 1990, and an MSc degree from Drexel University in June 1992. He is Xiaomi's co-founder, executive director, and vice chairman, as well as chairman of Xiaomi Foundation Limited in Hong Kong. Lin Bin co-founded Xiaomi with Lei Jun in 2010, serving as president of Xiaomi Corporation until 2019 before he took the role of Xiaomi's vice chairman. Earlier in his career, Lin Bin served as the engineering director at Google between 2006 and 2010. Before that, he worked at Microsoft Corporation from 1995 to 2006 and took on various roles such as software design engineer (SDE), SDE lead, SDE manager, and engineering director. Prior to that, Lin Bin worked as a network engineer at ADP Inc. from 1993 to 1995.

![Lu Weibing](//i02.appmifile.com/453_operator_global/23/05/2024/864065319f36c4ea453338fb4e120f8d.png)

### Lu Weibing

Partner and President

Lu Weibing, born in September 1975, graduated from Tsinghua University in 1998 with a bachelor's degree in chemistry and received his EMBA degree from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business in 2009. He is Xiaomi's partner and president, and president of the Smartphone Department. Lu Weibing joined Xiaomi in 2019 and has since been responsible for sales support in the China Region and the International Department, as well as work related to the REDMI brand. Before joining Xiaomi, Lu Weibing founded Shenzhen Chenyee Technology Co., Ltd and served as CEO of the company from 2017 to 2018. Additionally, he served as president of Gionee Communication Equipment Co., Ltd. in Shenzhen between 2010 and 2017; as general manager of the Overseas Business Department at Beijing Tianyu Communication Equipment Co., Ltd from 2008 to 2010; and as sales general manager of Konka Telecommunications Technology Co., Ltd. from 1998 to 2007.

![Liu De](//i02.appmifile.com/509_operator_global/23/05/2024/6baa77bb8a38f3adb572492dfebb9ade.png)

### Liu De

Co-Founder and Senior Vice President

Liu De, born in August 1973, graduated from Beijing Institute of Technology with a bachelor's degree in Industrial Design in July 1996, and obtained a master's degree in Mechanical Design and Theory from the same institute in March 2001. In April 2010, he received a master's degree in Industrial Design from Art Center College of Design in the US. He is Xiaomi's co-founder, executive director, and senior vice president, and head of Xiaomi's Leadership Management Department. Liu De joined Xiaomi in 2010. His early responsibilities included managing the smartphone supply chain, industrial design, and ecosystem business. Prior to Xiaomi, Liu De founded and led Rethink Concept between 2007 to 2010, and Beijing Xinfengrui Industrial Design Co., Ltd. between 2003 to 2007. In 2001, he established the Industrial Design Department at University of Science and Technology Beijing, where he served as the dean.

![Zeng Xuezhong](//i02.appmifile.com/27_operator_global/23/05/2024/542985b062758c5b70367f9244b5c376.png)

### Zeng Xuezhong

Senior Vice President

Zeng Xuezhong, born in July 1973, obtained a bachelor's degree in physics from Tsinghua University in 1996 and received an EMBA degree from the same institute in 2007. Currently, he is Xiaomi's senior vice president, and president of the International Business Department. Zeng Xuezhong joined Xiaomi in 2020 and was responsible for the R&D and manufacturing of smartphone products as president of the Smartphone Department from 2020 to 2024. Prior to joining Xiaomi, he served as chairman and general manager of HatChip Communications Technology Ltd. from 2019 to 2020, and held various senior management positions at Tsinghua Unigroup, including CEO of UNISOC, president of Unisplendour Corporation Limited, and global executive vice president of Tsinghua Unigroup. From 1996 to 2017, he served as ZTE's executive vice president and CEO of ZTE Terminal, as well as senior vice president of ZTE Corporation and president of ZTE China Region.

![Wang Xiaoyan](//i02.appmifile.com/632_operator_global/23/05/2024/f482189401279495a3c57687c93ca73e.png)

### Wang Xiaoyan

Senior Vice President

Wang Xiaoyan, born in February 1974, obtained a bachelor's degree in Physics from Beijing Normal University in 1994, and received an MBA degree from Renmin University of China in 1999. He is Xiaomi's senior vice president and president of the China Region. Wang Xiaoyan joined Xiaomi in 2019 and was in charge of the E-Commerce Department, Sales Operations Department, New Retail Department and Carrier Department of the China Region. He has served as president of the China Region since 2022. Before joining Xiaomi, he created and managed the Xiaolajiao smartphone brand from 2010 to 2019, served as a senior sales manager at Beijing Tianyu Communication Equipment Co., Ltd. from 2006 to 2010, and worked at ZTE from 1999 to 2005.

![Lam Sai Wai, Alain](//i02.appmifile.com/335_operator_global/23/05/2024/94239106f700bae039788b99af71005c.png)

### Lam Sai Wai, Alain

Vice President

Alain Lam, born in October 1973, graduated from University of Oxford with a master's degree in Engineering in August 1998. He is Xiaomi's vice president and CFO, and chairman of Airstar Digital Technology. Alain joined Xiaomi in 2020 as vice president and CFO of Xiaomi Corporation. Prior to joining Xiaomi, Alain worked at Credit Suisse (Hong Kong) as managing director and head of the Asian Technology, Media and Telecommunications (TMT) Investment Banking Division from 2016 to 2020. From 1997 to 2015, he worked at Morgan Stanley in its London, New York, Menlo Park and Hong Kong offices.

![Zhu Dan](//i02.appmifile.com/695_operator_global/23/05/2024/82828d8e110b3cabdfb2de0126eeedb6.png)

### Zhu Dan

Vice President

Zhu Dan, born in February 1978, received a master's degree in Automatic Control from the Beijing Institute of Technology in 2003. He is Xiaomi's vice president, as well as vice president for R&D in the Smartphone Department. Zhu Dan joined Xiaomi in 2010 and was in charge of the smartphone products. From 2018 to 2021, he held the position of general manager of the Camera Department. Before joining Xiaomi, Zhu Dan worked at Firebrand Technology Co., Ltd. from 2008 to 2010 as the R&D director of the Baseband Department, and at Motorola North Asia Centre from 2003 to 2008 as a research and development engineer.

![Qu Heng](//i02.appmifile.com/335_operator_global/23/05/2024/ae9d9332b37dab2fe4afed22374f2a9d.png)

### Qu Heng

Vice President

Qu Heng, born in October 1981, graduated from the Computer Science and Engineering Department of Beihang University in 2003, and obtained a master's degree in Computer Science and Engineering from Harbin Institute of Technology in 2013. He is Xiaomi's vice president and chairman of Xiaomi's Technology Committee. Qu Heng joined Xiaomi in 2010 and served as general manager of the Ecosystem Department from 2018 to 2023. Before joining Xiaomi, he worked at Kingsoft Corporation Limited from 2005 to 2010, and took on various roles such as engineer, development manager and project manager.

![Xu Fei](//i02.appmifile.com/23_operator_global/23/05/2024/14dbc578781529fb541d3d2c9469cb07.png)

### Xu Fei

Vice President

Xu Fei, born in November 1982, graduated from Tsinghua University with a bachelor's degree in Automation in 2005 and a master's degree in Computer Science and Technology in 2007. She currently serves as Xiaomi's vice president and chief marketing officer (CMO). Xu Fei joined Xiaomi in 2010 as an early member. From 2021 to 2024, she served as vice president of the China Region and general manager of the Marketing Department. Prior to joining Xiaomi, Xu Fei worked as a product manager at Google from 2007 to 2010.

![Zhang Jianhui](//i02.appmifile.com/887_operator_global/23/05/2024/0b6b6805d1387428f2b0ffc66491b7b7.png)

### Zhang Jianhui

Vice President

Zhang Jianhui, born in March 1979, graduated from Henan Agricultural University in 2002, and later received an EMBA degree from China Europe International Business School in 2023. She currently serves as Xiaomi's vice president and chairwoman of Xiaomi's Procurement Committee. Zhang Jianhui joined Xiaomi in 2011. She served as vice president of the China Region from 2018 to 2022, as well as the special assistant to CEO and general manager of the Administration Department from 2022 to 2024. Prior to joining Xiaomi, Zhang Jianhui worked at Beijing Kingsoft Software from 2002 to 2011, where she held positions including district manager, regional manager, and channel director.

![Liu Wei](//i02.appmifile.com/961_operator_global/10/07/2025/0bdb8b38b80a22b45d4838f7b71661d8.jpg)

### Liu Wei

Vice President

Liu Wei, born in August 1976, graduated from the School of Economics and Management, China University of Mining and Technology, in 1999. He is Xiaomi's vice president and director of Xiaomi's Executive Office. Liu Wei joined Xiaomi in 2022, serving as the special assistant to CEO and director of the Executive Office. Prior to Xiaomi, he worked at Kingsoft Corporation Limited from 2000 to 2022, holding roles including project manager, HR director, vice president of Seasun Entertainment, and vice president of Kingsoft. In 2016, he became Kingsoft's senior vice president.

![Hu Zhengnan](//i02.appmifile.com/746_operator_global/16/04/2026/f5a09a65a869b4198ad1458aeb4040e3.jpg)

### Hu Zhengnan

Vice President

Hu Zhengnan, born in April 1975, graduated from Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics with a bachelor's degree in Aircraft Design and Engineering in July 1997, and later received a PhD. in Mechanical Engineering from Huazhong University of Science and Technology in June 2025. He currently serves as Xiaomi's vice president and chief technology officer of the Electric Vehicle Department. Hu Zhengnan joined Xiaomi in 2026. He serves as the group's vice president and chief technology officer of the Electric Vehicle Department. Prior to joining Xiaomi, he served as a venture partner at Shunwei Capital; held positions including senior vice president and dean of the General Research Institute at Geely Auto Group from 2012 to 2021; founded Shanghai Longchuang Automotive Design Co., Ltd. from 2000 to 2011; and worked as an engineer at Shanghai Automotive Industry Technology Centre from 1997 to 2000.

**Lei Jun** (born December 16, 1969, Xiantao, Hubei province, China) is a Chinese business executive who was a cofounder (2010) of electronics maker Xiaomi Corp.; he also serves as chairman and CEO.

Lei attended Wuhan University, from which he graduated (1991) with a bachelor’s degree in computer science. In 1992 he joined the Beijing-based software company Kingsoft Corp., and by 1998 he had risen to become its CEO. He helped transform Kingsoft from a struggling company focused primarily on word-processing programs into a financially stable firm with products that also included video games and computer security software. In 2007 he led Kingsoft through its [initial public offering](/money/initial-public-offering-corporate-finance) (IPO), which raised nearly $100 million when the company was listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. He left Kingsoft shortly after the IPO (though he later rejoined its board of directors), and for the next few years he led a venture capital fund.

In April 2010 Lei founded [Xiaomi Corp.](/topic/Xiaomi) with several partners, including former [Google](/money/Google-Inc) executive Lin Bin. While the company sold various electronics, it was especially focused on [smartphones](/technology/smartphone). By concentrating on online rather than brick-and-mortar sales and by eschewing costly advertising in favour of interacting with customers directly through social media, Xiaomi was able to significantly undersell its competitors and thrive in the Chinese market. By 2014 the company’s valuation at more than $46 billion had made it the most-valuable tech [startup](/money/start-up-company) in the world. In April of that year, Xiaomi demonstrated the power of its brand when it sold 2.1 million smartphones online within just 12 hours, setting a world record for the most mobile phones sold on one online platform in a single day, and by the end of 2014 Xiaomi had surpassed [Samsung](/money/Samsung-Electronics) to become China’s leading smartphone vendor.

In an effort to continue Xiaomi’s growth, Lei increasingly looked for opportunities to expand beyond China. In July 2014 the company began selling [smartphones](/technology/smartphone) in India, which Lei described as Xiaomi’s “most important market after China,” and in May 2015 Xiaomi launched an online marketplace for customers in the United States and Europe, although initially it offered only computer accessories and fitness devices rather than its smartphones. Under Lei’s guidance, Xiaomi became the world’s third largest smartphone manufacturer—behind only [Samsung Electronics](/money/Samsung-Electronics) and [Apple Inc.](/money/Apple-Inc)—in 2014, and Lei himself was widely known as the “[Steve Jobs](/money/Steve-Jobs) of China.” In 2018 he oversaw the company’s IPO, which raised about $3 billion when it was listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

This is the Midea Group Investor Relations page focused on Corporate Governance. Quick Facts highlight five equity incentive programmes: Stock Option Incentive Schemes, Restricted Share Incentive Schemes, Global Partner Schemes, Business Partner Schemes, and Core Employee Stock Ownership Schemes.

The page provides detailed profiles of the Board of Directors and Senior Management.

BOARD OF DIRECTORS:
- Mr. Fang Hongbo (Paul Fang) - Chairman and President; joined Midea 1992; Master's degree; former General Manager of Air Conditioner Division, President of Midea Refrigeration Appliances, Chairman and President of GD Midea Holding.

- Dr. Xiao Geng - Independent Director; PhD in Economics from UCLA; Professor at Shenzhen Finance Institute, CUHK-Shenzhen; Independent Director of Tsingtao Brewery, UBS (China), Bank of Jinzhou.

## Chairman & Managing Director

RIL Chairman and Managing Director, Mukesh D. Ambani, is a chemical engineer from the Institute of Chemical Technology, Mumbai (erstwhile the University Department of Chemical Technology, University of Mumbai).

He pursued an MBA from Stanford University in the USA. He has been on the Board of Reliance since 1977. He initiated Reliance’s backward integration journey – from textiles to polyester fibres and further on to petrochemicals and petroleum refining, then going upstream into oil and gas exploration and production. He has created multiple world-class manufacturing facilities involving diverse technologies that have augmented Reliance’s petrochemicals manufacturing capacities from less than a million tonnes to about 21 million tonnes per year.

In the late nineties, Mukesh Ambani spearheaded the creation of the world’s largest grassroots petroleum refinery at Jamnagar in Gujarat, India, with a capacity of 660,000 barrels per day (33 million tonnes a year), and integrated it with petrochemicals, power generation, port, and related infrastructure. Further, he steered the setting up of another 580,000-barrels-per-day refinery next to the first one in Jamnagar.

With an aggregate refining capacity of 1.4 million barrels of oil per day at a single location, Jamnagar has become the refining hub of the world and has placed India firmly on the global energy map.

Mukesh Ambani also led the development and implementation of a pan-India organized retail network for Reliance, spanning multiple formats and supply-chain infrastructure. Today, Reliance Retail is the largest organised retail player in India. He set global records in customer acquisition for Jio, Reliance’s digital services business. He led and established one of the world’s most expansive 4G and 5G broadband wireless networks, offering end-to-end solutions that address the entire value chain across various digital services in key domains of national interest, such as education, healthcare, security, financial services, government-citizen interfaces, and entertainment.

Mukesh Ambani is a member of The Foundation Board of the World Economic Forum. He is an elected Foreign Member of the prestigious United States National Academy of Engineering. The page provides a detailed biography of Ambani, including his education (chemical engineering from the Institute of Chemical Technology, Mumbai, and an MBA from Stanford University), his tenure on the Reliance Board since 1977, and his key achievements including initiating Reliance's backward integration from textiles to petrochemicals and refining, leading the creation of the world's largest grassroots petroleum refinery at Jamnagar, Gujarat (with a combined refining capacity of 1.4 million barrels per day), building Reliance Retail into India's largest organized retail player, and establishing Jio's 4G/5G broadband networks. # Q2/H1 2026 Results

### **Solid revenue 1 trajectory at +9.7% in H1, with Q2 at +8.7%**

**Increasing profitability, with Adj. Operating Profit 1,2 +15%**

*   Group’s revenue grew 9.7% in H1 at constant exchange rates 1, with Q2 at +8.7%

**Paris, France (July 28, 2026 - 6:00 pm)**– The Board of Directors of EssilorLuxottica met on July 28, 2026 to approve the condensed consolidated interim financial statements for the six months ended June 30, 2026. The Statutory Auditors have performed a limited review of these financial statements.

Francesco Milleri, Chairman and CEO, and Paul du Saillant, Deputy CEO at EssilorLuxottica commented:

“We’re proud to report a successful first half, delivering nearly double-digit revenue growth while increasing adjusted operating profit by 15% at constant currency. Once again, our performance reflects the power of our strategy and our ability to execute with excellence as we continue to transform our industry. We drove strong momentum across all regions and businesses, fueled by our vision care and eyewear innovation and the expansion of our distribution network, with Top Charoen in Thailand further strengthening our global footprint. We made significant progress across our key growth drivers, from the acceleration of our myopia management portfolio to the sustained success of AI-powered wearables, driven by our iconic Ray-Ban and Oakley brands and our core expertise. While doing so, we continued to invest in the future, reinforcing our leadership to develop the next generation of intelligent optical systems through our partnership with Applied Materials. Supported by an increasingly integrated business and industrial platform, and as we double down on the capabilities and technologies that will shape the future of our industry, the dedication and talent of our colleagues around the world remain our greatest asset. With these foundations in place, we’ve never been better positioned to seize the opportunities ahead and accelerate our next chapter of growth”.

**Notes**

_As table totals are based on unrounded figures, there may be discrepancies between these totals and the sum of their rounded component._

**1 Constant exchange rates:** figures at constant exchange rates have been calculated using the average exchange rates in effect for the corresponding period in the relevant comparative year.

**2 Adjusted measures or figures:** adjusted from the expenses or income related to the combination of Essilor and Luxottica (the “EL Combination”), the acquisition of GrandVision (the “GV Acquisition”), other strategic and material acquisitions, and other transactions that are unusual, infrequent or unrelated to the normal course of business as the impact of these events might affect the understanding of the Group’s performance. A description of those other transactions that are unusual, infrequent or unrelated to the normal course of business is provided in the half-year and year-end disclosure (see dedicated paragraph _Adjusted measures_).

**3 Comparable-store sales:** reflect, for comparison purposes, the change in sales from one period to another by taking into account in the more recent period only those stores already open during the comparable prior period. For each geographic area, the calculation applies the average exchange rate of the prior period to both periods.

**4 Comparable or**_**pro forma**_**(revenue):** comparable revenue includes the contribution of GrandVision’s revenue to EssilorLuxottica as if the combination between EssilorLuxottica and GrandVision (the “GV Acquisition”), as well as the disposals of businesses required by antitrust authorities in the context of the GV Acquisition, had occurred at the beginning of the year (i.e. January 1). Comparable revenue has been prepared for illustrative purpose only with the aim to provide meaningful comparable information.

**5 Free Cash Flow:**_Net cash flow provided by operating activities_ less the sum of _Purchase of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets_ and _Cash payments for the principal portion of lease liabilities_ according to the IFRS consolidated statement of cash flow.

**6 Net debt:** sum of _Current and Non-current borrowings_, _Current and Non-current lease liabilities_, minus _Short-term investments_, _Cash and cash equivalents_ and the _Financial debt derivatives at fair value_ as disclosed in the IFRS consolidated financial statements.

**Francesco Milleri** (born 1959) is an Italian businessman who has been the CEO of [EssilorLuxottica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EssilorLuxottica "EssilorLuxottica") since June 2022.[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) He is also the father of Italian-American DJ and record producer [Matteo Milleri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anyma "Anyma").

## Early life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Francesco_Milleri&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Francesco Milleri was born in 1959.[[1]](#cite_note-2-globenewswire.com-cit-1)[[3]](#cite_note-bloombergbio-3) He graduated from the [University of Florence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florence "University of Florence") with a bachelor of laws, and earned a master in business administration from [Bocconi University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bocconi_University "Bocconi University").[[3]](#cite_note-bloombergbio-3) He was also awarded a two-year Donato Menichella scholarship from the [Bank of Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Italy "Bank of Italy") at the [New York University Stern School of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University_Stern_School_of_Business "New York University Stern School of Business").[[3]](#cite_note-bloombergbio-3)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Francesco_Milleri&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Milleri worked as a [business consultant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_consultant "Business consultant").[[3]](#cite_note-bloombergbio-3) In 1996 he founded Abstract, a strategic digital consultancy company.

Following the 2006 acquisition of iDoq, a company specializing in document flow automation and owner of the Lucy Star digitization platform, Abstract began collaborating with Campari, Barilla, and Luxottica. Subsequently, Francesco Milleri was entrusted with leading the digitization phase of Luxottica’s business processes. At the end of this ten-year period, [Leonardo Del Vecchio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Del_Vecchio "Leonardo Del Vecchio") wanted Milleri to stay in the company on a permanent basis, and appointed him first Director with deputy functions and later Vice-president.[[4]](#cite_note-81-ww.fashionnetwork.com-cit-4) He later became the deputy chairman of Luxottica, and succeeded Massimo Vian as its CEO in December 2017.[[5]](#cite_note-reuterssegreti-5) Under his leadership, in 2018 the operation that led to the birth of EssilorLuxottica was completed.[[6]](#cite_note-83-wmido.com-cit-6)

He was appointed executive co-delegate in May 2019, and CEO in 2020.[[7]](#cite_note-28-news.bloomberglaw.com-cit-7) In May 2021, Francesco Milleri was confirmed as EssilorLuxottica CEO.[[1]](#cite_note-2-globenewswire.com-cit-1) On 28 June 2022, he was appointed chairman of EssilorLuxottica following [Leonardo Del Vecchio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Del_Vecchio "Leonardo Del Vecchio")'s death, and in early June 2022, he was also appointed chairman of Del Vecchio's family holding company [Delfin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delfin_(Holding) "Delfin (Holding)").[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2)

Francesco Milleri (born 1959 in Città di Castello, Italy) is an Italian businessman who has served as CEO of EssilorLuxottica since June 2022. He graduated with a bachelor of laws from the University of Florence and earned an MBA from Bocconi University, also receiving a two-year Donato Menichella scholarship from the Bank of Italy at NYU Stern School of Business.

Career highlights: Milleri began as a business consultant and founded Abstract, a strategic digital consultancy, in 1996. After the 2006 acquisition of iDoq, Abstract collaborated with Campari, Barilla, and Luxottica, leading to Milleri leading Luxottica's business digitization. Leonardo Del Vecchio appointed him Director with deputy functions, then Vice-president. He became deputy chairman of Luxottica and succeeded Massimo Vian as CEO in December 2017. In 2018, the EssilorLuxottica merger was completed under his leadership. He was appointed executive co-delegate in May 2019, CEO in 2020, and confirmed as EssilorLuxottica CEO in May 2021. On 28 June 2022, he was appointed chairman of EssilorLuxottica following Del Vecchio's death, and also became chairman of Del Vecchio's family holding company, Delfin.

Other roles include assistant professor of political economy at the University of Florence and director of the Leonardo Del Vecchio Foundation. He is the father of Italian-American DJ and record producer Matteo Milleri (Anyma).
