URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IPMZuC2FktI

SUMMARY:
<summary>
## JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon Speaks at Reagan National Economic Forum (May 29, 2026)

This is a CNBC Television video featuring a full-length interview between JPMorgan Chase Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon and CNBC's Morgan Brennan at the Reagan National Economic Forum. The event took place on Friday, May 29, 2026, and was introduced by Susan McCaw, a member of the board of trustees of the Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute. The forum marked Dimon's second appearance at the event.

### Key Topics and Positions:

**Geopolitical Tectonic Plates:** Dimon emphasized that global geopolitical shifts (the war in Ukraine, Middle East terrorism, the Iranian war, global deficits, remilitarization, and trade restructuring) "dwarf the short-term economy." He expressed that the U.S. should have been more supportive of Ukraine and criticized tolerating Iranian aggression for 47 years, suggesting the U.S. should have acted decisively against Iran decades ago. He called an Iranian nuclear weapon "the biggest threat facing mankind" due to nuclear proliferation risks.

**Alliances and Trade:** Dimon argued that economic allies are critical and advocated for deeper trade relationships with Europe, Canada, Mexico, Australia, Japan, South Korea, and the Philippines. He proposed offering Europe "one big beautiful free trade deal" conditional on implementing the Draghi report recommendations. He supports countering unfair trade with tariffs but wants USMCA and other trade negotiations concluded.

**Dollar Dominance:** Dimon dismissed de-dollarization fears, calling it an "IQ test" — the dollar will remain the reserve currency as long as the U.S. maintains preeminent military and economic positions. He noted that unlike China (which has capital controls), U.S. dollars can be used freely.

**Security and Resiliency Initiative:** Dimon detailed JPMorgan's $1.5 trillion, 10-year Security and Resiliency Initiative (likely to far exceed that amount), investing in military equipment, productive capability, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), rare earths, and semiconductors. The bank hired investor Todd Combs for direct investments. Dimon advocated for "smart industrial policy" including tariffs or barriers to prevent importing rare earths from China (U.S. currently imports only $200 million in rare earths; quadrupling costs would have minimal economic impact). He admitted the U.S. was "asleep at the switch" for 10-15 years on critical supply chain dependencies.

**Permitting and Bureaucracy:** Dimon strongly criticized the U.S. permitting system and bureaucracy across infrastructure, housing, grids, and sewers, calling it "a disgrace." He proposed a 6-month Congressional session focused purely on policy changes (housing, permitting, education) without revenue or spending debates, estimating this could drive 1% higher growth.

**Affordability and the American Dream:** Dimon rejected the "K-shaped economy" narrative, arguing the top 70% are doing fine (middle class has grown richer) while the bottom 30% have seen stagnant wages for 25 years and can no longer earn living wages without college. He emphasized fixing this through good policy (education, housing, infrastructure, crime) rather than government spending, noting "trillions of dollars" have been spent without results.

**American Dream Initiative:** JPMorgan announced this initiative covering affordable housing mortgages, small business support (expanding from 7 million to 10 million small business clients), financial education, and work skills. Dimon emphasized teaching American values and the Constitution's founding principles (freedom, liberty, pursuit of happiness defined as having purpose).

**Tax Policy:** Dimon praised Jeff Bezos for engaging in the tax debate. He proposed reforming the Earned Income Tax Credit — eliminating the child requirement, changing the income threshold from $14,000 to $12,000 for single parents, which would give working recipients about $26,000 ($52,000 for two-parent households). He argued this would pay for itself through workforce participation, dignity, reduced crime, and better social outcomes, costing roughly $50 billion.

**Monetary Policy and New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh:** Dimon expressed support for new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (calling him "high quality, experienced"), noting the Fed overstepped into regulatory policy (climate, DEI) and violated constitutional requirements by skipping cost-benefit analyses. He supports reducing the Fed's balance sheet but cautioned Warsh faces 12 committee members and "almost no chance" of changing anything within 6 months.

**Inflation:** Dimon believes inflationary forces are stronger than generally perceived — ticking up from Iran conflict, food, healthcare (up 10% annually), remilitarization, AI spending, trade restructuring, immigration restrictions, and cumulative effects of $2 trillion annual government spending. He suggested inflation could hit 4%, and the 10-year Treasury at 4.5% may be at equilibrium.

**Markets:** Dimon called the equity market "exuberant," noting hype in AI-related stocks and low credit spreads as risks. He said JPMorgan can handle rates at 2% or 8% and isn't betting the company on either scenario. He praised SpaceX as "extraordinary" and supportive of the IPO environment, though noted ECM (equity capital markets) can close and open quickly (citing 400 IPOs in 2022 vs. 20 the next year).

**Biggest Risk:** Dimon identified "the geopolitics of how the free world plays out in the next 20 years" as the biggest underappreciated risk.

**Crypto/Blockchain:** Dimon remains pragmatic — JPMorgan is one of the biggest blockchain users, has a JPMorgan deposit coin moving money 24/7, and believes blockchain will replace financial market infrastructure. On stablecoins, he only asks for a level playing field with the same rules as AML, BSA, KYC, insurance, disclosures, and liquidity requirements.

**M&A:** Dimon addressed his earlier comments about $10-20 billion of potential acquisitions, saying the bank has excess capital and should always consider acquisitions. He joked about buying CNBC ("Versant"), noting they look "cheap." He emphasized using competitive analysis (asking why JPMorgan didn't build Stripe, why Chase UK isn't like Revolut, which is worth $75 billion) as a management tool.

**Private Credit:** Dimon downplayed systemic risks — private credit is $1.7 trillion versus investment-grade at $15 trillion and mortgages at $13 trillion — but warned that weakening underwriting standards and transparency will cause credit to perform worse than expected in the next credit cycle.

**Legacy:** Dimon said his legacy priorities are family first, country second, then Chase. He described his values (purpose, hard work, making the world better, not allowing bullies, treating people with respect) and quoted his brother's teaching. He wants his gravestone to say people are "better off" because of him. He has eight grandchildren, three children, and a wife.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
JPMorgan Chase announced a major reshuffling of top management under CEO Jamie Dimon on Thursday, in the latest development in the race to succeed the country's largest bank's longtime leader. The co-CEOs of the bank's commercial and investment bank, Doug Petno (61) and Troy Rohrbaugh (56), have been elevated to co-presidents effective immediately. Marianne Lake, CEO of JPMorgan's consumer and community bank, will retire after more than 25 years at the company. 

The moves narrow the succession race down to Petno or Rohrbaugh, according to an executive familiar with the matter. Petno becomes sole CEO of the commercial and investment bank, while Rohrbaugh replaces Lake as CEO of the consumer bank. Since neither has worked within the consumer bank, Bank of America analyst Ebrahim Poonawala said the moves set up Rohrbaugh as the lead candidate. Lake will stay for the coming weeks to smooth Rohrbaugh's transition.

The board granted "one-time retention" equity awards worth $30 million each to Petno and Rohrbaugh, and $20 million each to COO Jennifer Piepszak and asset & wealth management CEO Mary Erdoes.

The 70-year-old Dimon, the longest-serving big bank CEO and the only remaining CEO from the 2008 financial crisis, is expected to stay for three more years. In May 2024, Dimon said his exit timetable is "not five years anymore" and that succession was "well on the way." In January 2026, when asked how much longer he wanted to be CEO, Dimon replied "at least" five more years. Dimon previously interviewed Elon Musk earlier this month as part of JPMorgan's promotion of the SpaceX IPO.

For years, Lake and Jennifer Piepszak were viewed as the frontrunners, but Piepszak pulled herself out of the running in January 2025 after being elevated to COO. Up until the announcement, a Kalshi prediction market contract had placed majority odds on Lake as the most likely successor. RBC analyst Gerard Cassidy said the reshuffling "comes as a surprise," while Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo noted that investors may want Dimon to stay, "but this comes with a cost of loss of talent" in reference to Lake's departure.
</summary>

This is a CNBC "Squawk Box" interview with Exxon Mobil Chairman and CEO Darren Woods, discussing the company's Q1 earnings results and its response to the Middle East conflict, specifically the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The interview was posted on May 1, 2026, and the stock was up just over half a percent following better-than-expected quarterly results.

Key points from the interview:

1. **Earnings and Strategy**: ExxonMobil beat expectations in Q1. Woods emphasized that since 2018, the company has avoided predicting oil prices and instead focused on low-cost production growth based on its unique capabilities. He noted that production is needed worldwide to grow economies and improve lifestyles, regardless of market conditions.

2. **Production Growth**: Since 2018, ExxonMobil has more than doubled its U.S. production, growing at over 10% compounded annual growth rate. The company was the only U.S. company to expand refining production in 2023, with a 200,000 barrels-per-day improvement that has already paid for itself. 4. **Derivatives and Timing**: Because of the large volume of barrel movements, ExxonMobil's trading organization put hedges in place to lock in profits. The physical barrels remain in inventory until delivery, creating deferred profit that was highlighted in the earnings release to explain a loss booked in the current quarter that will be made up in a future quarter.

5. **Oil Price Outlook**: Woods called the supply disruption "unprecedented." He estimated that once the Strait of Hormuz reopens, it will take 1-2 months for flow to reestablish, plus about a month of transit time to get barrels from the Persian Gulf to demand destinations. So far, the impact has been mitigated by oil in transit when the strait closed, Strategic Petroleum Reserve releases, and commercial inventory draws — but these mitigating factors will run out if the strait remains closed, and prices will eventually respond to the supply disruption.

### PART 4: Governance Trend Context (CEO/Chair combination)

- According to a 2022 Conference Board/ESGAUGE survey (shared with Fortune), the percentage of S&P 500 companies combining the board chair and CEO roles dropped from 49% in 2018 to 44% in 2022, while companies with an independent board chair increased from 30% to 37% in the same period. CEOs serve as board chairs at 55% of companies with annual revenue of $50 billion or more, but only 25% of companies with revenue under $100 million [9].
- Spencer Stuart US Board Index data (2003–2011) shows companies combining CEO/chairman roles declined from 77% in 2003 to 59% in 2011, while those splitting roles rose from 23% to 41%; independent non-executive chairmen increased from 9% (2004) to 21% (2011). Only 18 S&P 500 companies had a formal policy to separate the roles in 2011 (up from 6 in 2010) [11].
- Equilar data (2016): 50.3% of S&P 500 companies had separate CEO and chairman roles (down from 56.2% in 2012); 35.1% had a non-executive chairman (up from 27.7% in 2012) [10].
- Many tech companies with founder-CEOs (like Facebook/Meta and Amazon) prefer combined roles [9].
- The dual CEO-chairman role is a governance issue raised by activists: NLPC argued against ExxonMobil's Darren Woods partly because "Woods holds both CEO and Chair titles, concentrating power and limiting board oversight" [55]. The Accountability Board filed a proposal calling on UnitedHealth to separate the CEO and board chair roles, stating "In our view, independent Chairs are like seatbelts: it's easy to forget you might need one when the road is smooth but once the storm rolls in, you're sure glad it's there" [46].

<Task>
Your focus is to call the "ConductResearch" tool to conduct research against the overall research question passed in by the user. 
When you are completely satisfied with the research findings returned from the tool calls, then you should call the "ResearchComplete" tool to indicate that you are done with your research.
</Task>

<Available Tools>
You have access to three main tools:
1. **ConductResearch**: Delegate research tasks to specialized sub-agents
2. **ResearchComplete**: Indicate that research is complete
3. **think_tool**: For reflection and strategic planning during research

**CRITICAL: Use think_tool before calling ConductResearch to plan your approach, and after each ConductResearch to assess progress. Do not call think_tool with any other tools in parallel.**
</Available Tools>

<Instructions>
Think like a research manager with limited time and resources. Follow these steps:

1. **Read the question carefully** - What specific information does the user need?
2. **Decide how to delegate the research** - Carefully consider the question and decide how to delegate the research. Are there multiple independent directions that can be explored simultaneously?
3. **After each call to ConductResearch, pause and assess** - Do I have enough to answer? What's still missing?
</Instructions>

<Hard Limits>
**Task Delegation Budgets** (Prevent excessive delegation):
- **Bias towards single agent** - Use single agent for simplicity unless the user request has clear opportunity for parallelization
- **Stop when you can answer confidently** - Don't keep delegating research for perfection
- **Limit tool calls** - Always stop after 3 tool calls to ConductResearch and think_tool if you cannot find the right sources

**Maximum 3 parallel agents per iteration**
</Hard Limits>

<Show Your Thinking>
Before you call ConductResearch tool call, use think_tool to plan your approach:
- Can the task be broken down into smaller sub-tasks?

After each ConductResearch tool call, use think_tool to analyze the results:
- What key information did I find?
- What's missing?
- Do I have enough to answer the question comprehensively?
- Should I delegate more research or call ResearchComplete?
</Show Your Thinking>

<Scaling Rules>

As of August 23, 2026, identify which Fortune 500 companies (global ranking) currently have a CEO who also serves as the Board Chair (i.e., the executive holds both the CEO and Chairman of the Board roles simultaneously). For each such company, provide the following details:

# Research Report: US Companies on the 2026 Fortune Global 500 with Combined CEO & Board Chair Role (as of Aug 23, 2026)

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

- The list is available online at fortune.com/ranking/global500 and in print on August 18, 2026 [1]. Fortune's lists calendar lists "Global 500 (July 28)" as an already-published 2026 list [8].
- In 2025, these corporations collectively generated $43.1 trillion in revenue (up 3.2% from the previous year), employed 70.2 million people, earned $3.39 trillion in profit in its most profitable year ever, and their revenue represents more than one-third of the world's GDP [1][7].
- Aggregate revenues reached $43.1 trillion (up 3%), profits hit $3.4 trillion (up 14%), and companies employ 70.2 million people worldwide—representing two-thirds of global GDP. The top 50 companies account for 33% of total revenue and 39% of profits [1].
- Amazon took the No. 1 spot, ending Walmart's 12-year reign at the top, followed by State Grid, UnitedHealth Group, and Saudi Aramco. Amazon eclipsed the $700 billion mark with a 12% jump in 2025 revenue ($700+ billion, a 12 percent increase over the previous year) [1][6].
- Jeff Bezos is featured on Fortune's August/September 2026 cover; Editor in Chief Alyson Shontell noted Amazon's $200 billion capital commitment largely to AI and cloud computing [1]. "Amazon has topped the Fortune Global 500, knocking Walmart off its pedestal. The company has continually reinvented itself across new businesses and bold bets—including a $200 billion capital commitment, largely to building its capacity for AI and cloud computing, in this year alone." — Alyson Shontell [1][6].

**2026 Top 10 (with revenue):**
1) Amazon (US, $716.92B), 2) Walmart (US, $713.16B), 3) State Grid (China, $555.37B), 4) UnitedHealth Group (US, $447.57B), 5) Saudi Aramco (Saudi Arabia, $445.53B), 6) Apple (US, $416.16B), 7) McKesson (US, $403.43B), 8) Alphabet (US, $402.84B), 9) CVS Health (US, $402.07B), 10) China National Petroleum (China, $401.93B) [2][7].

**Country breakdown (2026):** US 141, China 116, Japan 40, Germany 28, France 24, UK 21, Canada 14, South Korea 13, Switzerland 12, India 10 [2]. Regional: East Asia 175 (35%), North America 155 (31%), Europe 123 (24.6%), rest of world 47 (9.4%) [2].
- U.S. companies reached their highest presence since 2008 with 141 firms (up three), generating $15.5 trillion in aggregate revenues (up 6%). Greater China ranked second with 122 companies, down eight and its lowest count since 2018 [1][6].
- Women CEOs reached a record 34 (6.8%), up one from the prior year. Notable leaders include Jane Fraser (Citigroup), Gail K. Boudreaux (Elevance Health), Mary Barra (General Motors), and Sandy Ran Xu (JD.com). The U.S. leads with 16, followed by France (6), China (3), and Brazil, Germany, and the U.K. (2 each) [1].
- Technology is the standout growth sector: 38 companies (up four), revenues rising 20%+ to ~$4 trillion, and profits climbing 36% to ~$835 billion. Alphabet became the most profitable company in the world with $132 billion in profit [1].
- The "Magnificent Seven" (Amazon, Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta, Tesla) posted record aggregate revenue of $2.3 trillion and $608 billion in profits [1].
- Financial sector remains the largest with 123 companies, followed by energy (77), technology (38), motor vehicles and parts (35), and healthcare (31) [1].
- There were 24 newcomers, including 13 debuts (EP Group, Galaxy Digital, WT Microelectronics, AMD, Coupang) and 11 returning companies [1].

Chinese tech companies rose significantly: Tencent gained 19 spots to No. 97, and Alibaba rose seven spots to No. 56. **3. JPMorgan Chase & Co. — Jamie Dimon**
- Full name: James (Jamie) Dimon [34].
- Roles: Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co. [34][35].

Hemsley was named chief executive officer, effective immediately... and will remain chairman of the Board of Directors, while Witty will serve as a senior adviser to Hemsley" [43]. ### PART 4: Governance Trend Context (CEO/Chair combination)

- According to a 2022 Conference Board/ESGAUGE survey (shared with Fortune), the percentage of S&P 500 companies combining the board chair and CEO roles dropped from 49% in 2018 to 44% in 2022, while companies with an independent board chair increased from 30% to 37% in the same period. CEOs serve as board chairs at 55% of companies with annual revenue of $50 billion or more, but only 25% of companies with revenue under $100 million [9].
- Spencer Stuart US Board Index data (2003–2011) shows companies combining CEO/chairman roles declined from 77% in 2003 to 59% in 2011, while those splitting roles rose from 23% to 41%; independent non-executive chairmen increased from 9% (2004) to 21% (2011). Only 18 S&P 500 companies had a formal policy to separate the roles in 2011 (up from 6 in 2010) [11].
- Equilar data (2016): 50.3% of S&P 500 companies had separate CEO and chairman roles (down from 56.2% in 2012); 35.1% had a non-executive chairman (up from 27.7% in 2012) [10].
- Many tech companies with founder-CEOs (like Facebook/Meta and Amazon) prefer combined roles [9].
- The dual CEO-chairman role is a governance issue raised by activists: NLPC argued against ExxonMobil's Darren Woods partly because "Woods holds both CEO and Chair titles, concentrating power and limiting board oversight" [55]. The Accountability Board filed a proposal calling on UnitedHealth to separate the CEO and board chair roles, stating "In our view, independent Chairs are like seatbelts: it's easy to forget you might need one when the road is smooth but once the storm rolls in, you're sure glad it's there" [46].

### PART 5: Additional Supporting Details on Qualifying Executives (verbatim key facts)

**Satya Nadella (Microsoft):**
- Joined Microsoft in 1992; named CEO February 4, 2014; led Microsoft's shift to cloud computing; acquisitions include LinkedIn ($26.2B, 2016) and GitHub ($7.5B, 2018); revised mission to "empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more" [31].
- As of November 2023, Microsoft stock had increased nearly tenfold since 2014 with a 27% annual growth rate, ending a 14-year period of near zero growth [31].
- In January 2026, he asked people to stop calling AI "slop" and accept AI as the "new equilibrium," which backfired and led to the "Microslop" backlash [31].
- Education: bachelor's in electrical engineering from Manipal Institute of Technology (1988), MS in computer science from University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (1990), MBA from University of Chicago Booth School of Business (1997) [27][31].

**Mark Zuckerberg (Meta):**
- Holds title of chairman and retains majority voting control through the company's dual-class stock structure [38].
- Meta board has 13 directors, including Zuckerberg; all but two current directors have joined since 2019 [38].
- Recent board additions include Dana White (UFC CEO, elected January 6, 2025), Charlie Songhurst, John Elkann, Patrick Collison (2025), Tony Xu, and Drew Houston [38][39][40][41].

**Jamie Dimon (JPMorgan Chase):**
- Became CEO January 1, 2006; Chairman of the Board since December 31, 2006 (per LinkedIn) / "one year later" after becoming CEO (per company profile) [34][35].
- JPMorgan is a global financial services firm with assets of $3.2 trillion [34].
- In 2026, JPMorgan announced a management reshuffle elevating Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to co-presidents, narrowing the succession race; Marianne Lake announced retirement; Dimon stated in January 2026 he wants to remain CEO "at least" five more years [33].
- Board granted "one-time retention" equity awards worth $30 million each to Petno and Rohrbaugh, and $20 million each to COO Jennifer Piepszak and asset & wealth management CEO Mary Erdoes [33].
- Dimon announced a $1.5 trillion, 10-year Security and Resiliency Initiative and an "American Dream Initiative" [32].

**Stephen Hemsley (UnitedHealth Group):**
- Joined UnitedHealth Group in 1997 as COO; became president in 1999; appointed CEO in 2006 (succeeding William W. McGuire); became Board chair in 2017; returned as CEO May 13, 2025 [42][43][44].
- Under his leadership, UnitedHealth Group created Optum, now the largest employer of physicians in the U.S. [42].
- When he returned as CEO in 2025, he was awarded a package including $60 million in stock options (vesting over three years) plus a $1 million base salary [42].
- The 2025 leadership transition followed a difficult period: UnitedHealth suspended its 2025 outlook due to higher-than-expected medical costs; Hemsley pledged the company will "return to growth" in 2026 and reiterated the long-term growth objective of 13–16% [43][45].
- He graduated from Fordham University in 1974 with a bachelor's degree in accounting [42][44].

**Darren Woods (ExxonMobil):**
- Joined Exxon in 1992; ran refining and chemical divisions before becoming CEO [50].
- Education: BS in electrical engineering from Texas A&M University; MBA from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management [50][51].
- 2023 total compensation was $31 million (199-to-1 CEO-to-median-worker pay ratio); in 2024, it rose to $44.1 million (231-to-1 ratio) [50]. NLPC noted his pay rose 19.3% to $44.1 million in 2024 [55].
- Serves as Chairman of the American Petroleum Institute and is a member of its executive committee, as well as the National Petroleum Council, Business Roundtable, and Business Council [51].
- ExxonMobil is committed to investing up to $30 billion into hydrogen, carbon capture, biofuels, and lithium production through 2030 [55].

**Larry Culp (GE Aerospace):**
- Joined GE board April 2018; CEO of GE October 2018; CEO of GE Aerospace June 2022; Chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace when it launched as a public company in April 2024 [58][60].
- First outsider to run GE in the company's 126-year history [57].
- Previously President and CEO of Danaher Corporation from 2000/2001 to 2014, during which the company increased revenues and market capitalization five-fold [57][58].
- Employment agreement extended through December 31, 2027, with option to extend through December 31, 2028 [61].
- GE Aerospace has an installed base of approximately 44,000 commercial and 26,000 military aircraft engines, employs 52,000 people globally, and is headquartered in Evendale, Ohio [61].
- 2024 total compensation was $87.4 million [57].
- In July 2026 at Farnborough, Culp noted GE Aerospace increased engine deliveries by over 30% year-over-year in the first half of 2026, is "sold out into the early 2030s," and announced a deal for over 1,000 engines with Indigo Airlines in India [59].

**Fully Comprehensive Findings**

## 1. Context: The 2026 Fortune Global 500 List

The 2026 Fortune Global 500 (37th annual ranking) was released by Fortune magazine on **July 28, 2026** (published online at fortune.com; in print on newsstands August 18, 2026) [3][6][10][36]. Key facts about the 2026 list:

- Ranks the world's 500 largest corporations by revenue for the 2025 fiscal year [6].
- The 500 companies combined to generate **$43.1 trillion in revenue in 2025, up 3.2%** from the previous year; earned **$3.39 trillion in profit** (its most profitable year ever, up 14%); and employ **70.2 million people**; their revenue represents more than one-third of the world's GDP [3][6][10][7].
- **Top 10 for 2026:** 1) Amazon (US, $716.92B), 2) Walmart (US, $713.16B), 3) State Grid (China, $555.37B), 4) UnitedHealth Group (US, $447.57B), 5) Saudi Aramco (Saudi Arabia, $445.53B), 6) Apple (US, $416.16B), 7) McKesson (US, $403.43B), 8) Alphabet (US, $402.84B), 9) CVS Health (US, $402.07B), 10) China National Petroleum (China, $401.93B) [3][6][7][10].
- **Amazon topped the list, ending Walmart's 12-year run at No. 1** [3][6][10].
- Country breakdown: US 141, China 116, Japan 40, Germany 28, France 24, UK 21, Canada 14, South Korea 13, Switzerland 12, India 10 [7]. Greater China had 122 companies (down eight, its lowest count since 2018); European-based companies totaled 123; companies are based in 242 cities and 36 countries/territories; top five cities: Beijing, Tokyo, New York, London, Paris [6][7].
- Women CEOs reached a record 34 (6.8%), up one from the previous year [6].
- Notable ranks confirmed: Nvidia No. 28; TSMC No. 82; Tencent No. 97; Alibaba No. 56; Wistron No. 198 (biggest climber, +298 spots); Quanta Computer No. 211; SK Hynix No. 210; Chery Automobile No. 383 (new entry); ASML No. 453 (new entry); Daikin Industries No. 498 (new entry); Coupang No. 479 (new entry); WT Microelectronics No. 431 (new entry) [3][8][10][40].

## 2. Qualifying Companies: Non-US Global 500 Companies Where the Same Person Is CEO AND Chairman of the Board (as of August 23, 2026)

### France

**TotalEnergies SE — Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer** [11]
- Born June 24, 1963, in Le Petit-Quevilly, Normandy, France; French citizen [11][15].
- Career at Total: joined January 1997; became CEO of TOTAL S.A. and Chairman of the Executive Committee on **October 22, 2014**; elected to the board May 29, 2015; became **Chairman of the Board on December 19, 2015** (the India Energy Week biography states the date as December 16, 2015), thus becoming Chairman and CEO [11][13][15]. Wikipedia confirms: "In May 2015, Pouyanné was elected as a member of the board of directors of Total. In December he was appointed chairman and CEO of Total, combining both roles." [15]
- Last reappointment at the Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting on May 24, 2024, serving until 2027 [11].
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** He chaired the 2026 combined Shareholders' Meeting held Friday, May 29, 2026 [14]; he was featured as Chairman and CEO at an Atlantic Council fireside chat on February 24, 2026 [12]; and Fortune's company profile page (2026) lists "Chairman and CEO is Patrick Pouyanné" [68].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #20** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources). The World Benchmarking Alliance lists TotalEnergies' revenue at $196 billion USD [67]; Fortune's Global 500 2025 list had it at #20 (source's prior-year context) [7]. TotalEnergies is "one of the world's largest energy companies" and listed in the Fortune Global 500 [67].

**LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton — Bernard Arnault, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer** [19][20]
- Born March 5, 1949, in Roubaix, France; age 77 [19][20].
- Became chairman of LVMH's executive management board on **January 13, 1989**, after a strategic battle for control; has served as CEO since 1989 [20]. A Fortune article (March 5, 2026) confirms he "has served as LVMH CEO since 1989, overseeing a 37-year tenure" [16].
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** The Fortune March 2026 article confirms he remains chairman and CEO [16]; an Observer article (July 2026) describes "77-year-old chairman and CEO Bernard Arnault" and notes shareholders approved a bylaw change allowing him to remain chairman and CEO until age 85 (the age limit was previously raised from 75 to 80 in 2022) [17]; Forbes profile as of August 23, 2026, lists him as "Chairman and CEO of LVMH" with a net worth of $142 billion [19].
- Succession status: He has not named a successor; his five children hold senior roles (four with board seats). He told CNBC in December 2025: "Talk to me again in 10 years… I hope that, unless I get the ball on the head in a tennis court, I will make these 10 years." [16][17]
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #130–140** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources). The company reported H1 2026 revenue of €38.6 billion and a 3% organic revenue increase to €19.3 billion in Q2 2026 [17].

**Hermès International SCA — Axel Dumas, Executive Chairman (CEO)** [51][53]
- Born July 3, 1970, in Neuilly-sur-Seine, France; sixth-generation member of the Hermès-Dumas family [52].
- Became CEO in **June 2013**, succeeding Patrick Thomas (who departed January 2014) [52]. The Business of Fashion profile states he "took over as executive chairman of the Paris-listed company in 2014, after previously serving as co-chief executive and head of operations" [53]. The Cambridge Family Enterprise profile confirms he serves as "CEO of Hermès International SCA" [55].
- **Still in the role as of August 2026:** He presented the group's 2025 annual results (revenue over €16 billion) on February 12, 2026, as CEO [51].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #380–420** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources). Hermès is Europe's third-largest luxury goods group [53].

**EssilorLuxottica — Francesco Milleri, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer** [119]
- Born 1959 in Città di Castello, Italy [117].
- Appointed CEO of EssilorLuxottica in **December 2020**; became **Chairman and CEO on June 28, 2022**, following the death of Leonardo Del Vecchio [117][119]. His official EssilorLuxottica bio states: "Francesco Milleri is Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of EssilorLuxottica." [119]
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** He commented on the Q2/H1 2026 results (published July 28, 2026) as "Chairman and CEO" alongside Deputy CEO Paul du Saillant [116]; a Reuters article (April 28, 2026) reports him as CEO addressing the annual general meeting [120].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #430–445** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources). Market value was ~€86 billion as of April 2026 [120].

**Michelin (Compagnie Générale des Établissements Michelin) — Florent Menegaux, Managing Chairman and General Partner** — *Borderline case; see explanation below* [60]
- Menegaux joined Michelin in 1997; became Group Managing General Partner in 2018; appointed CEO of Michelin in May 2019 [59][60].
- On January 12, 2026, SAGES (the Non-Managing General Partner, headed by Vincent Montagne) renewed Menegaux's term as Managing General Partner for a maximum of four years, with the unanimous agreement of the Supervisory Board chaired by **Barbara Dalibard** [56][57].
- Michelin's governance page lists two Managers: "Florent Menegaux, the Managing Chairman and General Partner, and Philippe Jacquin, General Manager" [60].
- **IMPORTANT CAVEAT:** Michelin operates a two-tier French structure with a separate Supervisory Board chaired by **Barbara Dalibard** (a different person). Because the Supervisory Board Chair (the board-equivalent role) is a separate person from the CEO/Managing General Partner, Michelin does NOT strictly qualify under the user's criteria of "CEO and Board Chair combined in one executive," and should be treated as **excluded/borderline** [56][60].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: Not confirmed in gathered sources; Michelin is a long-standing Global 500 member.

### China

**Tencent Holdings — Ma Huateng (Pony Ma), Chairman and CEO** [30]
- Born October 29, 1971, in Chaoyang, Shantou, Guangdong [28].
- Co-founded Tencent in 1998; has been Chairman and CEO since founding [26][27][28][30].
- Tencent's official Board of Directors page (updated March 18, 2026) lists: "**Ma Huateng (Pony Ma), age 54 – Executive Director, Chairman and CEO.** Core founder of Tencent, employed since 1999… Mr Ma has overall responsibilities for strategic planning and positioning and management of the Group." [30]
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026** (confirmed by the official board page and the RevenueMemo ownership analysis dated August 2026, which states "Ma Huateng (Pony Ma), who remains Chairman and CEO") [26][30].
- **2026 Global 500 rank: No. 97** (confirmed by Tencent's own announcement of July 30, 2026: "Tencent has entered the Top 100 of the 2026 Fortune Global 500 for the first time, ranking No. 97 and rising 19 places from last year") [36]. Tencent reported 2025 revenue of RMB 751.8 billion (~US$109 billion, up 14% YoY) [26].

**BYD Company Limited — Wang Chuanfu, Chairman, Executive Director and President** [47]
- Born February 15, 1966, in Wuwei County, Anhui Province (Baidu Baike) [47]; Wikipedia gives April 8, 1966 [48].
- Founded BYD in 1995; serves as Chairman, Executive Director, and President of BYD Company Limited [47][48].
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** He chaired BYD's 2025 annual general meeting on June 9, 2026, as "Chairman and President" [46]; a Reuters article (June 16, 2026) refers to "BYD Chairman Wang Chuanfu" [50].
- **2026 Global 500 rank: No. 91** (confirmed by BYD's own announcement, July 28, 2026: "BYD ranked No. 91 on the 2026 Fortune Global 500 list, marking its fifth consecutive year on the index") [38]. BYD reported 2025 annual revenue of RMB 804 billion (USD 111 billion), net profit of RMB 32.6 billion (USD 4.5 billion), and NEV sales of 4.6 million units [38].
- Note on title: BYD uses "President" as the CEO-equivalent title (Wang is "Chairman, Executive Director and President") [47].

**Xiaomi Corporation — Lei Jun, Founder, Chairman and CEO** [103][105]
- Born December 16, 1969, in Xiantao, Hubei [101].
- Founded Xiaomi in April 2010; serves as "founder, executive director, chairman and CEO" [103][105][104].
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** Forbes profile (updated July 14, 2026) lists him as "cofounder, chairman and CEO of Hong Kong-listed Xiaomi" [102].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #330–385** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources). Xiaomi was named a Fortune Global 500 company in 2019 (youngest on the list at the time) [101]; its 2025 revenue position would place it in the lower-middle range of the list.

**Midea Group Co., Ltd. — Fang Hongbo (Paul Fang), Chairman and President** [106][107]
- Joined Midea in 1992; "Director, Chairman and Chief Executive officer of the company since 2012" (GlobalData) [106][107]. Midea's official governance page lists "Mr. Fang Hongbo (Paul Fang) - Chairman and President" [106].
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** Forbes profile (updated March 10, 2026) lists him as "the chairman of China's Midea" [109]; Midea Group's LinkedIn (2026) features "Chairman Paul Fang" [110].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #270–290** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources). Midea is a Fortune Global 500 company [108].

### Taiwan

**Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) — Dr. C.C. Wei, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer** [35]
- TSMC's official executives page: "Dr. C. C. Wei is Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (TSMC). Prior to this appointment, Dr. Wei was TSMC's Chief Executive Officer from June 2018 to June 2024, and TSMC's Board of Directors elected Dr. Wei as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer in **June of 2024**." [35]
- He became the first executive to hold both roles since founder Morris Chang, taking over as chair from Mark Liu [24].
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** He was named one of Time magazine's 100 most influential people of 2026 (April 2026) as "TSMC Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei" [21][22]; he addressed the company's annual general meeting in Hsinchu on June 4, 2026, as Chairman and CEO [23].
- **2026 Global 500 rank: No. 82** (confirmed: "TSMC climbed 44 places to 82nd position with revenue of US$122.26 billion") [7][39][40].

**Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd. (Foxconn) — Young Liu, Chairman and President** [61]
- Appointed **in 2019** following the retirement of founder Terry Gou; "the first time Foxconn separated ownership from professional executive management at its top leadership level" [61]. His official title is Chairman of Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn); the company uses "President" as the CEO-equivalent title [61][62].
- **Still in the role as of August 2026:** Foxconn press releases from June 2026 ("Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn) and Brookfield Form Renewable Energy Partnership in Vietnam", June 9, 2026; "Foxconn and SK Group Deepen Collaboration on AI Infrastructure", June 4, 2026) confirm his continuing chairmanship [62].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #24–27** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources; Hon Hai is a long-standing top-30 Global 500 company). Note: Taipei Times confirms Hon Hai Precision Industry Co is on the 2026 list [39].

### Japan

**SoftBank Group Corp. — Masayoshi Son, Chairman & CEO** [22]
- Born August 11, 1957; founded Nihon SoftBank (now SoftBank Group Corp.) in September 1981 and "has continued to serve as its chairman & CEO" since [22]. Current title: Representative Director, Corporate Officer, Chairman & CEO (since November 2020, to present) [22].
- **Still in both roles as of August 2026:** The SoftBank Group Report 2026 (dated June 24, 2026) contains his "CEO Message" [21]; he presented at a June 16, 2026, enterprise event as "Chairman & CEO, SoftBank Group Corp." [23]; Forbes profile (as of August 22, 2026) lists him as "CEO of SoftBank Group" [25].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #240–260** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources). SoftBank Group reported net profit of 5 trillion yen ($31 billion) on sales of 7.8 trillion yen ($49 billion) for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 [25].

- Born February 7, 1949 [43].
- Career timeline: President & CEO since September 1984; Chairman and CEO November 2002; **Chairman, President and CEO since September 2005** (current position) [43]. Official Fast Retailing profile: "Tadashi Yanai serves as Chairman, President and CEO of FAST RETAILING CO., LTD., Chairman of the Fast Retailing Foundation, and Chairman of UNIQLO CO., LTD." [43]
- **Still in all roles as of August 2026:** His CEO Message page was last updated May 8, 2026, authored as "Chairman, President and CEO" [41].
- 2026 Global 500 rank: **Approximately #310–340** (not explicitly confirmed in gathered sources).

## 3. Companies Checked and EXCLUDED (CEO and Board Chair are Different People, or dual role not held)

**Sony Group Corporation (Japan) — EXCLUDED.** Kenichiro Yoshida retired as President and CEO in April 2025 and is now **Executive Chairman** (a separate role). Hiroki Totoki has been President and CEO since April 1, 2025 [98][99][100]. Sony's February 5, 2026, press release confirms: "Kenichiro Yoshida will retire from his position as Representative Corporate Executive Officer and continue as Executive Chairman of Sony Group Corporation" effective April 1, 2026 [96]. Wikipedia: Yoshida is "currently serving as executive chairman of Sony," having "served as president and CEO from April 2018 to April 2025" [97]. Therefore CEO (Totoki) and Chairman (Yoshida) are different people.

**Samsung Electronics (South Korea) — EXCLUDED.** Jay Y. Lee was appointed **Executive Chairman** on October 27, 2022, by the Board of Directors [72][73][75]. However, the CEO roles are held separately: "Vice Chairman & CEO Jun Young-hyun (appointed 2024)" and "Jong-Hee Han – Vice Chairman & CEO, DX Division" [71]. Therefore the CEO and Board Chair are different people. (Note: As of April 15, 2026, Lee's net worth was $25.4 billion, making him South Korea's richest person [74].)

**Toyota Motor Corporation (Japan) — EXCLUDED.** Akio Toyoda stepped down as President and CEO on April 1, 2023, to become Chairman; Koji Sato succeeded him [77][78][80]. At the June 17, 2026, annual meeting, "Toyota shareholders re-elected Akio Toyoda as chairman and backed new CEO Kenta Kon as a board member"; Kon "became CEO in April" 2026, replacing Koji Sato (now vice chairman) [79]. Therefore Chairman (Toyoda) and CEO (Kon) are different people.

**Volkswagen AG (Germany) — EXCLUDED.** Oliver Blume is CEO of Volkswagen AG (since September 1, 2022; extended by the Supervisory Board until end of 2030, effective January 1, 2026) [81][82]. However, the **Chairman of the Supervisory Board is Hans Dieter Pötsch** (a separate person) [81][82][85]. (Blume also stepped down as CEO of Porsche AG as of January 1, 2026, ending his dual-role arrangement; Dr. Michael Leiters became Porsche CEO [83][84][85].) Therefore CEO and Board Chair are different people.

**Mercedes-Benz Group AG (Germany) — EXCLUDED.** Ola Källenius is Chairman of the Board of Management (CEO) (since May 2019; contract extended to mid-2029) [87][90]. However, the **Chairman of the Supervisory Board is Martin Brudermüller** (a separate person), per Mercedes-Benz's official governance page [90]. Therefore CEO and Board Chair are different people.

**Bayer AG (Germany) — EXCLUDED.** Bill Anderson is Chairman of the Board of Management (CEO) of Bayer AG (member of the Board of Management since April 1, 2023; CEO since June 1, 2023; contract extended until March 31, 2029) [91][95]. However, the **Chairman of the Supervisory Board is Prof. Dr. Norbert Winkeljohann** (a separate person) [91][94]. Therefore CEO and Board Chair are different people.

**Saudi Aramco (Saudi Arabia) — EXCLUDED (contextual).** Ranked No. 5 on the 2026 Global 500 [7]. The top-10 list identifies it as Saudi Arabia's sole representative company on the list per country counts (1 company) [2]. (No evidence was gathered that its CEO and Board Chair roles are combined; the CEO of Saudi Aramco and the Chairman of its Board are separate individuals as a matter of public record.)

**State Grid, China National Petroleum, UnitedHealth Group, Apple, McKesson, Alphabet, CVS Health (top-10 companies) — US-based or CEO/Chair split.** These were not identified as qualifying dual-role non-US companies in the gathered sources. Amazon (No. 1) has Executive Chair Jeff Bezos with CEO Andy Jassy as separate roles [6].

## 4. Additional Relevant Data Points Gathered

- **Masayoshi Son (SoftBank)** details: net worth $63.5 billion as of August 22, 2026 [25]; on June 2, 2026, SoftBank's market value surpassed Toyota's to rank first in Japan [24]; he is chairman of Stargate LLC (AI infrastructure JV) [24][25].
- **Pony Ma (Tencent)** details: net worth $50.5 billion as of March 10, 2026 (Forbes) [29]; holds roughly 8% of Tencent shares primarily through Advance Data Services Limited [26].
- **Wang Chuanfu (BYD)** details: wealth of 160 billion yuan on the 2026 Hurun Global Rich List [47]; BYD aims to become the world's largest automaker by scale within five years [46][50].
- **Francesco Milleri (EssilorLuxottica)** details: appointed "Cavaliere del Lavoro" by the President of the Italian Republic in 2025 [119]; the company's Q2 2026 revenue grew +8.7% at constant exchange rates [116].
- **Young Liu (Foxconn)** details: awarded India's Padma Bhushan in 2024 (third-highest Indian civilian honor) [61]; under his leadership Foxconn's workforce fell from ~1.3 million to ~900,000 due to AI/automation [64].
- **C.C. Wei (TSMC)** details: Time profile was written by Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, who called Wei "a humble yet disciplined leader" [21]; Wei said at the June 4, 2026 AGM that TSMC is "not afraid of competition" [23].

You are a research supervisor. Your job is to conduct research by calling the "ConductResearch" tool. For context, today's date is Mon Aug 24, 2026.

<Task>
Your focus is to call the "ConductResearch" tool to conduct research against the overall research question passed in by the user. 
When you are completely satisfied with the research findings returned from the tool calls, then you should call the "ResearchComplete" tool to indicate that you are done with your research.
</Task>

<Available Tools>
You have access to three main tools:
1. **ConductResearch**: Delegate research tasks to specialized sub-agents
2. **ResearchComplete**: Indicate that research is complete
3. **think_tool**: For reflection and strategic planning during research

**CRITICAL: Use think_tool before calling ConductResearch to plan your approach, and after each ConductResearch to assess progress. Do not call think_tool with any other tools in parallel.**
</Available Tools>

<Instructions>
Think like a research manager with limited time and resources. Follow these steps:

1. **Read the question carefully** - What specific information does the user need?
2. **Decide how to delegate the research** - Carefully consider the question and decide how to delegate the research. Are there multiple independent directions that can be explored simultaneously?
3. **After each call to ConductResearch, pause and assess** - Do I have enough to answer? What's still missing?
</Instructions>

<Hard Limits>
**Task Delegation Budgets** (Prevent excessive delegation):
- **Bias towards single agent** - Use single agent for simplicity unless the user request has clear opportunity for parallelization
- **Stop when you can answer confidently** - Don't keep delegating research for perfection
- **Limit tool calls** - Always stop after 3 tool calls to ConductResearch and think_tool if you cannot find the right sources

**Maximum 3 parallel agents per iteration**
</Hard Limits>

<Show Your Thinking>
Before you call ConductResearch tool call, use think_tool to plan your approach:
- Can the task be broken down into smaller sub-tasks?

After each ConductResearch tool call, use think_tool to analyze the results:
- What key information did I find?
- What's missing?
- Do I have enough to answer the question comprehensively?
- Should I delegate more research or call ResearchComplete?
</Show Your Thinking>

<Scaling Rules>
**Simple fact-finding, lists, and rankings** can use a single sub-agent:
- *Example*: List the top 10 coffee shops in San Francisco → Use 1 sub-agent

**Comparisons presented in the user request** can use a sub-agent for each element of the comparison:
- *Example*: Compare OpenAI vs. Anthropic vs. DeepMind approaches to AI safety → Use 3 sub-agents
- Delegate clear, distinct, non-overlapping subtopics

**Important Reminders:**
- Each ConductResearch call spawns a dedicated research agent for that specific topic
- A separate agent will write the final report - you just need to gather information
- When calling ConductResearch, provide complete standalone instructions - sub-agents can't see other agents' work
- Do NOT use acronyms or abbreviations in your research questions, be very clear and specific
</Scaling Rules>

As of August 23, 2026, identify which Fortune 500 companies (global ranking) currently have a CEO who also serves as the Board Chair (i.e., the executive holds both the CEO and Chairman of the Board roles simultaneously). For each such company, provide the following details:

1. The executive's full name
2. The date they assumed the dual role (i.e., when they became CEO and Board Chair, or when they added the second title to the first)
3. A direct link to the company's most recent proxy statement (DEF 14A filing) confirming the arrangement
4. A link to at least one independent news source (e.g., reputable news outlet, business press) confirming that this executive currently holds both titles as of August 23, 2026

Important exclusions and constraints:
- Do NOT include executives who previously held both titles but no longer do so as of August 23, 2026 (e.g., those who stepped down from one role, retired, or were replaced).
- Only include companies that are on the current Fortune 500 global list as of August 2026.
- Only include companies where the SAME person currently serves as both CEO and Board Chair — not where different people hold each role, and not where there is an interim or acting arrangement unless clearly confirmed.
- Do not include companies where the CEO is not the Board Chair even if the CEO holds another chairman-type title (e.g., Executive Chairman is a separate person, or the Chairman role is held by someone else).

For sources, prioritize:
- Official SEC EDGAR filings for proxy statements (DEF 14A)
- Reputable business news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, CNBC, etc.) or the company's official press releases for independent confirmation
- The Fortune 500 official list/website for company ranking confirmation

The output should be a comprehensive, verified list of all qualifying companies and executives, with each entry fully documented with the requested links and details.

args.reflection:
This is a very large research task: identify all Fortune Global 500 companies (2026 list) where the CEO is also Board Chair as of Aug 23, 2026, and document each with executive name, date of assuming dual role, a DEF 14A proxy statement link, and an independent news confirmation link.

Key strategic considerations:
1. The Fortune Global 500 has 500 companies; likely 100+ have combined CEO/Chair roles. Full exhaustive documentation for all is enormous, but I should aim for comprehensive coverage with a pragmatic approach.
2. DEF 14A proxy statements are only filed by US SEC filers. Non-US companies on the Fortune Global 500 generally don't file DEF 14A (they file 20-F/6-K if US-listed). So the proxy-statement documentation constraint effectively focuses on US companies; for non-US companies I'll need to use other official documents/announcements.
3. The task decomposes naturally: (a) build the qualifying list (US vs non-US), (b) gather DEF 14A links, (c) gather news confirmations.
4. Sub-agents can't see each other's work, so I must give standalone, self-contained instructions.

Round 1 plan: 3 parallel agents — (1) US-based Fortune Global 500 companies with combined CEO & Board Chair (names + dates), (2) non-US-based Fortune Global 500 companies with combined CEO & Board Chair (names + dates), (3) a verification/documentation agent focused on SEC EDGAR DEF 14A links for the most prominent combined-role US companies plus news confirmations. Then assess and follow up.

# Research Report: US Companies on the 2026 Fortune Global 500 with Combined CEO & Board Chair Role (as of Aug 23, 2026)

## List of Queries and Tool Calls Made

**Queries executed:**
1. "Fortune Global 500 2026 list full ranking US companies"
2. "Fortune Global 500 2026 announced August companies ranked"
3. "S&P 500 companies where CEO is also chairman of board 2026 combined role"
4. "Fortune 500 US companies CEO also serves as chairman board 2025 2026"
5. "Apple CEO John Ternus chairman board 2026"
6. "Walmart CEO John Furner chairman board 2026"
7. "Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella chairman board 2026"
8. "JPMorgan Jamie Dimon CEO chairman 2026 board"
9. "Meta Mark Zuckerberg CEO chairman 2026 board"
10. "UnitedHealth Stephen Hemsley CEO chairman 2026 board"
11. "ExxonMobil Darren Woods chairman CEO 2026"
12. "Chevron Mike Wirth chairman CEO 2026 General Motors Mary Barra chairman board 2026"
13. "GE Aerospace Larry Culp chairman CEO 2026 Home Depot CEO chairman board 2026"

**Tool calls:** 4 think_tool reflections (2 per search round)

---

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

### PART 1: The 2026 Fortune Global 500 List (Context)

**List release and key facts:**
- The 2026 Fortune Global 500 is the 37th running of the list, ranking the world's 500 largest corporations by revenue for the 2025 fiscal year [1][2][7].
- The list is available online at fortune.com/ranking/global500 and in print on August 18, 2026 [1]. Fortune's lists calendar lists "Global 500 (July 28)" as an already-published 2026 list [8].
- In 2025, these corporations collectively generated $43.1 trillion in revenue (up 3.2% from the previous year), employed 70.2 million people, earned $3.39 trillion in profit in its most profitable year ever, and their revenue represents more than one-third of the world's GDP [1][7].
- Aggregate revenues reached $43.1 trillion (up 3%), profits hit $3.4 trillion (up 14%), and companies employ 70.2 million people worldwide—representing two-thirds of global GDP. The top 50 companies account for 33% of total revenue and 39% of profits [1].
- Amazon took the No. 1 spot, ending Walmart's 12-year reign at the top, followed by State Grid, UnitedHealth Group, and Saudi Aramco. Amazon eclipsed the $700 billion mark with a 12% jump in 2025 revenue ($700+ billion, a 12 percent increase over the previous year) [1][6].
- Jeff Bezos is featured on Fortune's August/September 2026 cover; Editor in Chief Alyson Shontell noted Amazon's $200 billion capital commitment largely to AI and cloud computing [1]. "Amazon has topped the Fortune Global 500, knocking Walmart off its pedestal. The company has continually reinvented itself across new businesses and bold bets—including a $200 billion capital commitment, largely to building its capacity for AI and cloud computing, in this year alone." — Alyson Shontell [1][6].

**2026 Top 10 (with revenue):**
1) Amazon (US, $716.92B), 2) Walmart (US, $713.16B), 3) State Grid (China, $555.37B), 4) UnitedHealth Group (US, $447.57B), 5) Saudi Aramco (Saudi Arabia, $445.53B), 6) Apple (US, $416.16B), 7) McKesson (US, $403.43B), 8) Alphabet (US, $402.84B), 9) CVS Health (US, $402.07B), 10) China National Petroleum (China, $401.93B) [2][7].

**Country breakdown (2026):** US 141, China 116, Japan 40, Germany 28, France 24, UK 21, Canada 14, South Korea 13, Switzerland 12, India 10 [2]. Regional: East Asia 175 (35%), North America 155 (31%), Europe 123 (24.6%), rest of world 47 (9.4%) [2].
- U.S. companies reached their highest presence since 2008 with 141 firms (up three), generating $15.5 trillion in aggregate revenues (up 6%). Greater China ranked second with 122 companies, down eight and its lowest count since 2018 [1][6].
- Women CEOs reached a record 34 (6.8%), up one from the prior year. Notable leaders include Jane Fraser (Citigroup), Gail K. Boudreaux (Elevance Health), Mary Barra (General Motors), and Sandy Ran Xu (JD.com). The U.S. leads with 16, followed by France (6), China (3), and Brazil, Germany, and the U.K. (2 each) [1].
- Technology is the standout growth sector: 38 companies (up four), revenues rising 20%+ to ~$4 trillion, and profits climbing 36% to ~$835 billion. Alphabet became the most profitable company in the world with $132 billion in profit [1].
- The "Magnificent Seven" (Amazon, Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta, Tesla) posted record aggregate revenue of $2.3 trillion and $608 billion in profits [1].
- Financial sector remains the largest with 123 companies, followed by energy (77), technology (38), motor vehicles and parts (35), and healthcare (31) [1].
- There were 24 newcomers, including 13 debuts (EP Group, Galaxy Digital, WT Microelectronics, AMD, Coupang) and 11 returning companies [1].
- Companies are based in 242 cities and 36 countries/territories. Top five cities: Beijing, Tokyo, New York, London, and Paris (which returned to top five for first time since 2021) [1].
- AI chipmakers Nvidia jumped 38 spots to No. 28, and Taiwan Semiconductor leaped 44 spots to No. 82. Netherlands-based ASML entered the list for the first time at No. 453. Chinese tech companies rose significantly: Tencent gained 19 spots to No. 97, and Alibaba rose seven spots to No. 56. Health care giant McKesson broke into the top 10 at No. 7; it is one of 138 companies that have been on the list since 1995 [7].

**Houston-area companies on the 2026 Global 500 (useful anchor ranks):** No. 15 ExxonMobil, No. 36 Chevron, No. 61 Phillips 66, No. 159 Sysco, No. 243 ConocoPhillips, No. 292 Enterprise Products Partners, No. 343 Plains GP Holdings, No. 460 SLB, and No. 481 Hewlett Packard Enterprise [6].

**US Fortune 500 top 20 (2026, for rank approximations):** 1. Amazon ($716.9B), 2. Walmart ($713.2B), 3. UnitedHealth Group ($447.6B), 4. Apple ($416.2B), 5. McKesson ($403.4B), 6. Alphabet ($402.8B), 7. CVS Health ($402.1B), 8. Berkshire Hathaway ($371.4B), 9. ExxonMobil ($332.2B), 10. Cencora ($321.3B), 11. Microsoft ($281.7B), 12. Costco ($275.2B), 13. Cigna ($274.9B), 14. Cardinal Health ($222.6B), 15. Nvidia ($215.9B), 16. Meta ($201.0B), 17. Elevance Health ($199.1B), 18. Centene ($194.8B), 19. Chevron ($189.0B), 20. Ford Motor Company ($187.3B) [15].

---

### PART 2: QUALIFYING US COMPANIES — CEO is ALSO Board Chair (as of Aug 23, 2026)

The following US companies on the 2026 Fortune Global 500 have a confirmed combined CEO/Board Chair role as of late August 2026:

**1. Microsoft Corporation — Satya Nadella**
- Full name: Satya Narayana Nadella (born August 19, 1967, in Hyderabad, India; Indian-American business executive) [31].
- Roles: Chairman and CEO of Microsoft [27][31].
- Dates: Succeeded Steve Ballmer as CEO on February 4, 2014; was named Chairman of the board on June 16, 2021, replacing independent director John Thompson (following a unanimous board vote / unanimous election by the board's independent directors) [28][29][30][31].
- Verification as of 2026: Clay.com dossier (April 15, 2026) states "Satya Nadella is the CEO and executive chairman of Microsoft, having taken the reins from Steve Ballmer in 2014" [27]. Wikipedia (current) states "He is the chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of Microsoft, succeeding Steve Ballmer in 2014 as CEO and John W. Thompson in 2021 as chairman" [31].
- Context: When named chairman, Microsoft said "In this role, Nadella will lead the work to set the agenda for the board, leveraging his deep understanding of the business to elevate the right strategic opportunities and identify key risks and mitigation approaches for the board's review" [28][30]. Thompson became lead independent director [29][30]. Nadella's 2024 compensation was $79.1 million (up 63% from $48.5 million in 2023); 2025 compensation per Boardroom Alpha was $96.5M [31][52].
- Approximate 2026 Global 500 rank: Not in the Global 500 top 10; ranked #11 on the 2026 US Fortune 500 with $281.7B revenue [15]. Approximate Global 500 rank: ~#11–13.

**2. Meta Platforms, Inc. — Mark Zuckerberg**
- Full name: Mark Zuckerberg [39][40].
- Roles: Founder, Chairman and CEO of Meta Platforms (formerly Facebook) [39][40].
- Dates: Founded Meta (as Facebook) in 2004 and has served as its Chief Executive Officer since inception; has served as Chairman of the board of directors since 2012 [39][40]. Meta's investor relations page: "Mark Zuckerberg is the founder, chairman and CEO of Meta, which he originally founded as Facebook in 2004. Mark is responsible for setting the overall direction and product strategy for the company" [40].
- Verification as of 2026: A formal letter dated August 17, 2026, from 18 U.S. Members of Congress is addressed to "Mark Zuckerberg, Chairman and CEO of Meta Platforms, Inc." [37]. VectorShift leadership directory and Meta's official investor governance page (current) both list "Mark Zuckerberg – Founder, Chairman and CEO" [39][40]. Zuckerberg retains majority voting control through the company's dual-class stock structure [38].
- Approximate 2026 Global 500 rank: Ranked #16 on the 2026 US Fortune 500 with $201.0B revenue [15]. Approximate Global 500 rank: ~#16–18.

**3. JPMorgan Chase & Co. — Jamie Dimon**
- Full name: James (Jamie) Dimon [34].
- Roles: Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co. [34][35].
- Dates: Became CEO on January 1, 2006, and one year later (December 31, 2006, per LinkedIn) also became Chairman of the Board [34][35]. JPMorganChase official profile: "Dimon became CEO on January 1, 2006 and one year later also became Chairman of the Board" [34]. LinkedIn: "Jamie Dimon became Chairman of the Board on December 31, 2006, and has been Chief Executive Officer and President since December 31, 2005" [35]. A company press release headline confirms "Jamie Dimon Elected Chairman Of The Board Of JPMorgan Chase" [36].
- Verification as of 2026: A CNBC Television video (May 29, 2026) introduces him as "JPMorgan Chase Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon" at the Reagan National Economic Forum [32]. A June 2026 Yahoo Finance article on the bank's succession race describes the "70-year-old Dimon, the longest-serving big bank CEO and the only remaining CEO from the 2008 financial crisis, [who] is expected to stay for three more years"; in January 2026, when asked how much longer he wanted to be CEO, Dimon replied "at least" five more years [33]. Official leadership page (current): "Jamie Dimon is Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co., a global financial services firm with assets of $3.2 trillion and operations worldwide" [34].
- Approximate 2026 Global 500 rank: Not in the Global 500 top 10; rank not explicitly captured in sources. Approximate Global 500 rank: ~#25–35 (financial sector, revenue ~$190B).

**4. UnitedHealth Group — Stephen J. Hemsley**
- Full name: Stephen J. Hemsley (born June 4, 1952) [42].
- Roles: Board Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of UnitedHealth Group Inc. [42][44].
- Dates: Hemsley has served as chair of the Board of Directors since September 2017 [44]. He served as CEO from 2006 to 2017, then stepped down to become executive chairman; he returned to the CEO post on May 13, 2025, effective immediately, after Andrew Witty stepped down as CEO for personal reasons [42][43][44][45]. Business Roundtable: "Stephen Hemsley has served as chief executive officer of UnitedHealth Group since May 2025 and chair of the Board of Directors of the company since September 2017" [44].
- Verification as of 2026: UnitedHealth's official May 13, 2025 press release: "Stephen J. Hemsley was named chief executive officer, effective immediately... and will remain chairman of the Board of Directors, while Witty will serve as a senior adviser to Hemsley" [43]. As of February 2026, his net worth was estimated at least $990 million [42]. A 2025 shareholder proposal (The Accountability Board) called on UnitedHealth to separate the CEO and board chair roles, confirming he holds both [46].
- Approximate 2026 Global 500 rank: **#4** (UnitedHealth Group, $447.57B revenue) [2][7].

**5. ExxonMobil Corporation — Darren Woods**
- Full name: Darren Wayne Woods (born December 16, 1965, in Wichita, Kansas) [50].
- Roles: Chairman and CEO of ExxonMobil [50][51][55].
- Dates: Became President of Exxon Mobil Corporation on January 1, 2016; was elected Chairman and CEO effective January 1, 2017, succeeding Rex Tillerson [50][51]. "He is the 23rd President (assumed office January 1, 2016) and 16th Chairman (assumed office January 1, 2017) of ExxonMobil" [50].
- Verification as of 2026: CSIS profile (current) identifies "Darren W. Woods, Chairman and CEO of ExxonMobil Corporation" [51]. CNBC video (July 31, 2026): "ExxonMobil Chairman and CEO Darren Woods joins 'Squawk Box'" [48]. CNBC video (May 1, 2026): "Exxon Mobil Chairman and CEO Darren Woods" [49]. ExxonMobil corporate speech page (February 11, 2026, LNG 2026 conference in Doha): "ExxonMobil Chairman and CEO Darren Woods" [47]. A 2025 SEC exempt solicitation from NLPC urging shareholders to vote against Woods's re-election notes: "Woods holds both CEO and Chair titles, concentrating power and limiting board oversight" [55].
- Approximate 2026 Global 500 rank: **#15** (per Houston InnovationMap Houston-area rankings) [6].

**6. GE Aerospace — H. Lawrence "Larry" Culp Jr.**
- Full name: H. Lawrence (Larry) Culp Jr. (born Henry Lawrence Culp Jr., March 1963, in Washington, D.C.) [57].
- Roles: Chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace [57][58][60][61].
- Dates: Joined the GE Board of Directors in April 2018; appointed CEO of GE in October 2018 (succeeding John L. Flannery; first outsider to run GE in the company's 126-year history); in June 2022 assumed additional duty as CEO of GE Aerospace; became Chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace when it launched as a public company in April 2024 [57][58][60].
- Verification as of 2026: Business Roundtable profile (current): "H. Lawrence 'Larry' Culp, Chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace... appointed CEO of GE in October 2018, and was appointed CEO of GE Aerospace in June 2022" [58]. Bloomberg Talks interview (July 21, 2026, Farnborough International Air Show): "GE Aerospace Chairman and CEO Larry Culp" [59]. GE Aerospace press release (July 1, 2024) extended his employment agreement as "Chairman and CEO" through December 31, 2027, with an option to extend through December 31, 2028 [61]. Note: Culp also serves as non-executive Chairman of GE HealthCare's board [60][58].
- Approximate 2026 Global 500 rank: Not in the Global 500 top 10; rank not explicitly captured in sources. Approximate Global 500 rank: ~#55–65.

---

### PART 3: US Global 500 Companies EXCLUDED (CEO and Board Chair are different people, or interim/unconfirmed)

**1. Walmart (2026 Global 500 rank #2)** — EXCLUDED
- CEO: John Furner became president and CEO of Walmart Inc. on February 1, 2026, succeeding Doug McMillon (who retired effective January 31, 2026) [22][23][24][25][26].
- Chairman: Greg Penner is Chairman of Walmart's Board [24][26]. (At Walmart's June 4, 2026 annual meeting, "the meeting was called to order by Board Chairman Greg Penner" [26].)
- Furner joined the Walmart board of directors effective immediately upon being named CEO (November 2025), but he is not board chair [24][26].
- Global 500 rank #2 ($713.16B revenue) [2].

**2. Apple Inc. (2026 Global 500 rank #6)** — EXCLUDED as of Aug 23, 2026
- As of August 23, 2026: Tim Cook is still CEO (through the summer), and Arthur Levinson is Apple's non-executive chairman (served for 15 years) [17][19].
- On September 1, 2026 (AFTER the Aug 23, 2026 cutoff): John Ternus becomes CEO, Tim Cook becomes executive chairman (a separate role from CEO), and Arthur Levinson becomes lead independent director. Ternus will join the board on that date [17][18][19][20][21]. "Apple announced a leadership succession plan, effective September 1, 2026, where John Ternus will become CEO and Tim Cook will transition to the role of executive chairman of the board" [17]. Since Cook will hold "executive chairman" while Ternus is CEO, roles remain split; and as of Aug 23, 2026, the CEO and Chair are still different people (Cook CEO, Levinson non-executive Chair) [17][19].
- Note: Cook, 65, joined Apple in March 1998 and was named CEO in August 2011; under his leadership market cap increased more than 20-fold, closing at $4 trillion, and revenue nearly quadrupled to over $400 billion [19]. Ternus, 50, joined Apple's product design team in 2001, became VP of Hardware Engineering in 2013, joined the executive team in 2021 [17][19].

**3. Berkshire Hathaway (2026 Global 500 rank #8)** — EXCLUDED
- CEO: Greg Abel was slated to become CEO on January 1, 2026 [12].
- Chairman: Warren Buffett remains chairman [12].
- (Per Databahn's 2026 Fortune 500 recap: "Berkshire Hathaway: Greg Abel slated to become CEO on January 1, 2026, with Warren Buffett remaining chairman") [12].
- Global 500 rank #8 ($371.4B revenue per US Fortune 500) [2][15].

**4. Alphabet (2026 Global 500 rank #8)** — EXCLUDED
- CEO Sundar Pichai is not the board chair; Alphabet has an independent chair structure (not detailed in sources, but Alphabet was not identified in any source as having a combined CEO/Chair). Listed here for completeness as a top-10 US company that did not qualify.

**5. Amazon.com (2026 Global 500 rank #1)** — EXCLUDED
- CEO Andy Jassy is not the board chair; Jeff Bezos is Executive Chairman of Amazon's board (a separate role from CEO). Bezos is featured on Fortune's August/September 2026 cover ("Jeff Bezos: Amazon just became the world's largest company. He's not done") [4][1]. Since Bezos is a separate "Executive Chairman" (different person from CEO Jassy), Amazon is explicitly excluded per the user's criteria.

**6. CVS Health (2026 Global 500 rank #9)** — EXCLUDED

### PART 4: Governance Trend Context (CEO/Chair combination)

- According to a 2022 Conference Board/ESGAUGE survey (shared with Fortune), the percentage of S&P 500 companies combining the board chair and CEO roles dropped from 49% in 2018 to 44% in 2022, while companies with an independent board chair increased from 30% to 37% in the same period. CEOs serve as board chairs at 55% of companies with annual revenue of $50 billion or more, but only 25% of companies with revenue under $100 million [9].
- Spencer Stuart US Board Index data (2003–2011) shows companies combining CEO/chairman roles declined from 77% in 2003 to 59% in 2011, while those splitting roles rose from 23% to 41%; independent non-executive chairmen increased from 9% (2004) to 21% (2011). Only 18 S&P 500 companies had a formal policy to separate the roles in 2011 (up from 6 in 2010) [11].
- Equilar data (2016): 50.3% of S&P 500 companies had separate CEO and chairman roles (down from 56.2% in 2012); 35.1% had a non-executive chairman (up from 27.7% in 2012) [10].
- Many tech companies with founder-CEOs (like Facebook/Meta and Amazon) prefer combined roles [9].
- The dual CEO-chairman role is a governance issue raised by activists: NLPC argued against ExxonMobil's Darren Woods partly because "Woods holds both CEO and Chair titles, concentrating power and limiting board oversight" [55]. The Accountability Board filed a proposal calling on UnitedHealth to separate the CEO and board chair roles, stating "In our view, independent Chairs are like seatbelts: it's easy to forget you might need one when the road is smooth but once the storm rolls in, you're sure glad it's there" [46].

### PART 5: Additional Supporting Details on Qualifying Executives (verbatim key facts)

- Joined Microsoft in 1992; named CEO February 4, 2014; led Microsoft's shift to cloud computing; acquisitions include LinkedIn ($26.2B, 2016) and GitHub ($7.5B, 2018); revised mission to "empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more" [31].
- As of November 2023, Microsoft stock had increased nearly tenfold since 2014 with a 27% annual growth rate, ending a 14-year period of near zero growth [31].
- In January 2026, he asked people to stop calling AI "slop" and accept AI as the "new equilibrium," which backfired and led to the "Microslop" backlash [31].
- Education: bachelor's in electrical engineering from Manipal Institute of Technology (1988), MS in computer science from University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (1990), MBA from University of Chicago Booth School of Business (1997) [27][31].

**Mark Zuckerberg (Meta):**
- Holds title of chairman and retains majority voting control through the company's dual-class stock structure [38].
- Meta board has 13 directors, including Zuckerberg; all but two current directors have joined since 2019 [38].
- Recent board additions include Dana White (UFC CEO, elected January 6, 2025), Charlie Songhurst, John Elkann, Patrick Collison (2025), Tony Xu, and Drew Houston [38][39][40][41].

- Became CEO January 1, 2006; Chairman of the Board since December 31, 2006 (per LinkedIn) / "one year later" after becoming CEO (per company profile) [34][35].

- In 2026, JPMorgan announced a management reshuffle elevating Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to co-presidents, narrowing the succession race; Marianne Lake announced retirement; Dimon stated in January 2026 he wants to remain CEO "at least" five more years [33].
- Board granted "one-time retention" equity awards worth $30 million each to Petno and Rohrbaugh, and $20 million each to COO Jennifer Piepszak and asset & wealth management CEO Mary Erdoes [33].
- Dimon announced a $1.5 trillion, 10-year Security and Resiliency Initiative and an "American Dream Initiative" [32].

- Under his leadership, UnitedHealth Group created Optum, now the largest employer of physicians in the U.S. [42].
- When he returned as CEO in 2025, he was awarded a package including $60 million in stock options (vesting over three years) plus a $1 million base salary [42].

- Joined GE board April 2018; CEO of GE October 2018; CEO of GE Aerospace June 2022; Chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace when it launched as a public company in April 2024 [58][60].
- First outsider to run GE in the company's 126-year history [57].

- GE Aerospace has an installed base of approximately 44,000 commercial and 26,000 military aircraft engines, employs 52,000 people globally, and is headquartered in Evendale, Ohio [61].
